This is the complete guide to migrating your financial data from Microsoft Money to Monize. There are two ways to do it: Import your .mny file directly -- Monize reads the Microsoft Money file itself. This is the recommended method and the one you should use unless something prevents it. Export QIF files from Microsoft Money and import those -- the older, manual method. Use it only if the direct import refuses your file. For importing from other sources using CSV or OFX/QFX files, see Importing Transactions .

Monize reads Microsoft Money .mny files directly -- not a QIF export of one, but the file itself, with its accounts, transactions, transfers, splits, securities, price history, exchange rates and scheduled bills intact. Nothing needs to be installed, Microsoft Money does not need to be on the machine, and the file never leaves your Monize server. The older route is to export one QIF file per account from Microsoft Money and import those. Monize still supports it in full, but it asks considerably more of you and carries less information across.

Direct .mny import QIF export Effort One file, one upload One export per account (two per investment account), then mapping each file Transfers Linked using Money's own record of which two rows are the two sides Matched by name and amount; import order matters Splits Imported Imported (requires "Loose QIF") Closed accounts Imported, and stay closed Must be reopened in Money before they can be exported Price history Imported Not available Exchange rates Imported Not in QIF -- cross-currency transfers need manual fixing Scheduled bills Imported (you choose which) Not exported -- must be recreated by hand Loan payments Principal leg wired to the loan account; funding account, payment amount and interest category filled in where unambiguous Detected from category names, with confirmation Verification Every account's balance is reconciled against the balance computed from the Money file Manual comparison against Money Merging into existing data Not supported in v1 -- import into an empty profile. The same file is refused a second time Possible, but duplicates are your problem Use the direct .mny import. It reads every Money version from Money 97 to Money Plus Sunset. Fall back to QIF only if the direct import cannot read your file -- for example a damaged file that Money itself can still open and export.

Import into an empty profile. Version 1 does not merge. It creates what the file describes, and if an account of the same name already exists it adds transactions to it rather than working out which ones you already have. On a profile that already has data you will get duplicates. If you have been trying Monize out and want to start over from Money, the review step offers Start fresh , which runs the same Delete My Data operation as Settings > Danger Zone before the import begins. It asks you to type a confirmation word and re-enter your password, and it cannot be undone. Work from a copy. Monize never writes to the file, but a spare copy of three decades of finances costs nothing. Money 97, 98 and 99 files import directly , with no conversion step, recurring bills included. A few things in them cannot come across exactly: A scheduled payment Money recorded with no account to pay from (Money 99 can leave a scheduled loan payment that way) cannot become a bill and is listed as skipped. An investment account's "Other income" and "Other expenses" arrive as ordinary categorized transactions in its cash account, and employee stock option grants, vesting and expiry are not imported. A CD, which Money 99 buys by amount, arrives as units worth 1 each. Money 99 keeps only the latest exchange rate for each currency, so a trade of a security quoted in another currency, made before that rate's date, is converted at the market exchange rate for its date instead, and listed so you can check it. .mbf backup archives are not supported. Restore the backup in Money first and import the resulting .mny . Check the file size limit if you self-host. The default ceiling is 300 MB, set by MNY_IMPORT_LIMIT_MB . See Troubleshooting the .mny Import if a large upload fails. Read the Money file once. Monize refuses to import a file whose exact bytes it already imported into your account, so a second click cannot double your data. To import the same file again, use Start fresh .

Navigate to Tools > Import Transactions to begin. Step 1: Upload the file Select or drag your .mny file onto the upload area. Import Microsoft Money files one at a time -- a .mny file holds a whole profile, so there is nothing to bulk-select. Monize reads the file on the server and shows a preview. Nothing is written yet. If the file cannot be opened, the reason appears in red on the upload step (see Troubleshooting the .mny Import ). Step 2: Enter the password, if asked Every Money file is encrypted, but most are encrypted with a blank password and open without asking. The prompt -- "This Money file needs a password" -- appears only when a real password is set. Enter it under Money file password and click Open file . The password is used once to read the file and is never stored. A wrong password says so specifically, so you can tell "this needs a password" apart from "that one was wrong". Money passwords are case sensitive. Step 3: Review what will be imported This step is worth the minute it takes. The file summary names the detected Money format (Money 97-99, Money 2001, Money 2002, or Money Plus / Sunset) and the base currency. If the Money version lacks a table Monize reads (Money 2001 has no scheduled bills, for example), a note says what is skipped because of it. Counts for transactions (with the number of transfers linked), payees, categories, tags from classifications, accounts, securities, investment transactions (with share transfers), price history, exchange rates and scheduled bills are each shown against the total in the file, so "40 of 500 payees" is visible before rather than after. Every account is listed with its type, currency, transaction count, opening balance and the final balance computed from the Money file itself . Compare a few against Money -- that same number is what the verification report reconciles against afterwards. A Money investment account appears as its two Monize halves, " - Cash" and " - Brokerage". An account Monize had to rename (two accounts sharing a name) shows its name in Money underneath, and closed, favourite and excluded-from-net-worth accounts are marked. Untick any account you do not want , or use Select all / Select none . Closed accounts are included by default and stay closed; they still hold history worth keeping. Override an account's currency with its dropdown if Money had it wrong. Scheduled bills appear as a checkbox list with each bill's account, frequency, next due date and amount, and whether it is a transfer or an investment. Money keeps one row per occurrence, so a long history holds thousands of rows for a handful of real bills; Monize detects the live series and pre-ticks those. An unticked bill is simply not created. A frequency Monize cannot express exactly is marked as the closest one, and bill series missing a template or a usable date are reported as skipped. Notes about this file collects anything ambiguous -- securities sharing a symbol, an action code Money did not document, a repeat interval with no exact equivalent. Where a note is about particular transactions, Show the n transactions lists them with their date, account, payee and amount, so you can find them in Money. Worth reading; none of it stops the import. Step 4: Start the import Choose the import options under the accounts, then click Start import . It runs on the server, so you can leave the page and come back. A large file takes a few minutes. The progress list shows which phase is running, with a row counter: preparing; accounts, categories and payees; transactions; investments; scheduled bills; prices and exchange rates; recalculating balances; verifying. Only one import can run at a time for your account. If the server restarts mid-import, nothing is left half-written: Try again runs it again from the file you already uploaded, and Start over goes back to the upload step. Step 5: Check the verification report When the import finishes, the Balance verification table lists every account with the balance computed from your Money file, the balance it ended up with in Monize, and the difference. Holdings verification compares, for every investment account, the shares Monize now holds against Money's own open tax lots -- Money reconciles against those lots itself, so they are the number to trust. The counts above the tables say what was created. A green run says every account reconciles; anything that does not is listed with the difference so you can look at it directly. Notes about this import repeats anything the import had to decide. The report downloads as JSON with Download report if you want to keep it; Done returns to the upload step.

Set on the review step, before you start the import. Option Default What it does Only import payees that are used On Money keeps payees long after their last transaction. Leaving this on skips the unused ones Only import categories that are used On Money seeds a full category tree whether you use it or not Import closed accounts On Closed accounts keep their history and are created closed Import price history On Money's own record of what each security was worth, day by day. Turn it off if you would rather start from live quotes Import exchange rates On Historical rates between the currencies in your file, used only for dates Monize has no rate for. Rates already stored are never replaced Start fresh: remove my existing Monize data first Off Removes your existing Monize data before importing. Typed confirmation and password required With Start fresh ticked, Start import first opens Remove Existing Data . It lists what is removed -- every transaction and split; every scheduled transaction; every security, price, holding and investment transaction; every account, category and payee; every budget, custom report, tag and import mapping -- and warns that this cannot be undone, even if the import then fails. Type DELETE and your Password (an account that signs in through single sign-on confirms with its identity provider instead), then click Delete my data and import .

Accounts of every type, with opening balances, currencies, and closed and favourite flags. A Money investment account becomes Monize's linked cash and brokerage pair, matching how Money itself stores them. Money's watch accounts ("Investments to Watch") are created excluded from net worth, since they track quotes rather than money you hold. Transactions , including splits, reference numbers, memos, and the cleared/reconciled status of each. Voided transactions are imported as voided rather than dropped. Transfers , using Money's own record of which two rows are the two sides. Nothing is matched by guesswork. Loan and mortgage payments , with the principal leg wired to the loan account as a transfer split. Where the payments make it unambiguous, the loan's funding account, payment amount and interest category are filled in too. Money's Pmt Num arrives in the loan register's reference number column. Securities and investment transactions : buys, sells, dividends, reinvestments, share transfers between accounts, and stock splits. Each trade puts exactly one row in one cash register, wherever Money put it: the account's own cash side for a trade paid out of it, the paying account for one funded from elsewhere. Price history and exchange rates , both additive -- importing on top of prices a quote provider already fetched converges rather than duplicating. Exchange rates are shared by everyone on your Monize server, so a rate from your file only fills a date Monize has no rate for; it never replaces one already stored. Scheduled bills you ticked, created active and set not to post automatically, so nothing lands in your accounts without you. Classifications , as tags. Money's two user-named classifications ("Classification 1" and "2", which you may have called Properties or Projects ) become tags named Classification:Item , for example Properties:20 Spring Apartment . Every transaction, split and scheduled bill that carried the item in Money carries the tag in Monize. Only items a transaction actually uses are created.

Data type Notes Budgets Money's budget tables have no clean equivalent in Monize's. Recreate with Budgets -- Monize can auto-generate budgets from your imported spending history Savings goals No equivalent entity Attachments Files embedded in the Money file Categories deeper than two levels Flattened into Parent:Child names; Monize's category tree is two levels deep

No merge, no de-duplication. Version 1 targets a fresh profile. Monize refuses to import a file whose exact bytes it already imported into your account, and names the earlier import; to import it again, use Start fresh . A different save of the same Money file (whose bytes differ) is not recognised as the same file, and importing it creates the transactions a second time. A failure after the data was saved says so. If an import fails after its records were written (a final check, for example), the wizard tells you the records are in your account and does not offer to try again: importing the same file again would duplicate them. Check your accounts before importing anything else. Securities quoted in another currency than their account. Money records a trade in the account's currency. Monize stores the trade's price and total in the security's own currency, converted with the exchange rate your file holds for that date, and keeps the cash movement in the account's currency. If your file has no rate for that pair within 45 days before the trade, the market rate for the date is used, or failing that the trade is imported unconverted; either way the report lists it, so you can check the price. Foreign-currency cost basis. Money stores a foreign holding's cost basis converted to your base currency at the historical rate, not in the security's own currency. Monize imports what the file says, so a holding bought in a currency other than your base one can show a cost basis that differs from what you paid in the original currency. The verification report flags these, and the share counts themselves are unaffected. Two Money codes are still unconfirmed. Money's act 5 and 14 -- a reinvestment variant and a cash corporate action -- have never appeared in any file available to this project, so their handling is inferred. Any transaction mapped through one carries a note in the report rather than being silently accepted. Securities sharing a symbol. Money allows two funds with the same ticker. Monize's symbols are unique per user, so the second gets a suffix ( VOO-2 ) and a note in the report -- never collapsed into the first. A security with no symbol gets a generated placeholder and is excluded from automatic price updates.

The verification report does most of the checking for you, so the post-import work is short: Read the report. Any account or holding that does not reconcile is named with the difference. Review auto-created securities in Tools > Securities . A security that had no symbol in Money gets a generated placeholder symbol and is excluded from price updates until you give it a real symbol and exchange. Recreate budgets and savings goals -- see Budgets . Check your scheduled bills in Bills and Deposits . Imported bills are active but set not to post automatically; switch on auto-posting for the ones you want it on. Check net worth on the Dashboard against your Money net worth report. If the result is not what you wanted, see Starting Over -- or simply re-run the import with Start fresh ticked.

Nothing is written unless the whole import succeeds, so a failure leaves your data as it was, and the uploaded file is kept for one more attempt. What you see What it means "That file was written by a version of Microsoft Money that Monize cannot read" Open it once in the free Money Plus Sunset edition, save it, and import the result "That file is not a Microsoft Money (.mny) file" Wrong file, or the upload was corrupted "That Money file looks incomplete" The upload was cut short -- try again "That Money file was decrypted but its contents could not be read" The file decrypted but its internals are damaged. Open it in Money and save a fresh copy "That Money file is password protected" Enter the file's password when prompted "This file was already imported into your account" Importing it again would duplicate its records. To replace them, start over with Start fresh ticked "The import saved your data, but a step after that failed" or "...stopped responding after it had already saved your data" The records are in your account. Check your accounts before importing anything else; importing the same file again would duplicate them "That password does not open the Money file" Money passwords are case sensitive -- check and retry "The import stopped responding" The server restarted mid-import. Your file is still here: press Try again "The uploaded Money file is no longer available" Uploaded files are kept 24 hours. Upload it again "An import is already running" Wait for it to finish -- possibly in another tab Two failures look like the app is broken and are configuration: The upload is refused as too large. The frontend passes a Money file to the backend through its own upload route, which refuses anything over MNY_IMPORT_LIMIT_MB (default 300). The variable must be set on the frontend as well as the backend. The server is killed partway through every attempt. It is running out of memory. A Money file is held in memory while it is read, so the backend needs roughly twice the file size available. See helm/README.md for the sizing rules.

Everything from here on describes the older QIF route: exporting one file per account from Microsoft Money and importing those. It is still fully supported, and the QIF import wizard handles: Regular banking transactions (chequing, savings, credit cards) Investment transactions (buy, sell, dividends, splits, reinvestments) Split transactions (multiple categories per transaction) Account-to-account transfers Category creation and mapping Security creation and mapping Multi-currency accounts The process is designed for bulk operations -- you can import multiple QIF files at once, and the system coordinates between files to link transfers, reuse categories, and handle cross-references. Prefer the direct .mny import. QIF carries no price history, no exchange rates and no scheduled bills, cannot export closed accounts without reopening them first, and matches transfers by inference rather than from Money's own records. Use QIF only when the direct import cannot read your file.

h: Part 3: Preparing Microsoft Money for Export
x: Before exporting, take these preparatory steps in Microsoft Money to ensure a clean migration.

Create a spreadsheet or list with the following for each account: Detail Example Account Name "Main Chequing" Account Type Chequing, Savings, Credit Card, Investment, etc. Currency USD, CAD, GBP, etc. Opening Balance $1,234.56 Opening Balance Date January 1, 2005 Why this matters: The opening balance and date are critical. For imported accounts to show the correct current balance, the opening balance must be set to the balance as of the first transaction date in the QIF file. Microsoft Money often includes an "Opening Balance" transaction in the QIF export, which Monize detects automatically. However, having this information written down gives you a fallback if the auto-detection does not match.

If you have closed accounts in Microsoft Money that you want to import, you may need to temporarily reopen them -- Microsoft Money does not allow exporting closed accounts. The easiest way to do this is to go to Tools - Settings - Account settings (global) - Close or Reopen Accounts The direct .mny import has no such restriction: closed accounts come across with their history and stay closed.

h: 3.3 Make a List of All Accounts
x: Microsoft Money exports one account at a time, so make a checklist: [ ] Main Chequing (Regular) [ ] Savings (Regular) [ ] Visa Credit Card (Regular) [ ] Emergency Fund (Regular) [ ] RRSP Brokerage (Investment) [ ] RRSP Brokerage (Regular - for cash transactions) [ ] TFSA Brokerage (Investment) [ ] TFSA Brokerage (Regular - for cash transactions) [ ] Home (Asset) Important for Investment Accounts: Each investment account requires TWO exports -- one as "Investment" type (for securities transactions) and one as "Regular" type (for cash transactions). Mark both on your checklist.

Monize supports bulk-upload of .QIF files. We suggest you create the following folders to store your exported QIFs: 1-Assets 2-NativeAccounts 3-ForeignAccounts 4-Investments-Cash 5-Investments-Brokerage This makes it easy to select all the files a certain type for bulk-import.

Follow these steps for each chequing, savings, credit card, cash, line of credit, and asset account: Step 1: Open Microsoft Money and load your .mny file Step 2: Go to File > Export Step 3: In the export dialog, select Loose QIF format Always choose "Loose QIF" -- it carries more information than "Strict QIF," including split transaction details and transfer references. Step 4: Choose a save location (Desktop is easiest) and name the file after the account Step 5: Select Regular as the account type Step 6: Select the specific account to export from the account list Step 7: Click Continue to export Step 8: Check the account off your list and repeat for the next account

Investment accounts in Microsoft Money contain two types of data: Investment transactions (buy, sell, dividend, etc.) Cash transactions (deposits, withdrawals, fees) You must export each investment account twice . Go to File > Export Select Loose QIF Name the file with the account name and "-Investment" suffix (e.g., RRSP-Investment.qif ) Select Investment as the account type Select the specific investment account Click Continue Go to File > Export again Select Loose QIF Name the file with the account name and "-Regular" suffix (e.g., RRSP-Regular.qif ) Select Regular as the account type Select the same investment account Click Continue
We recommend you give the files the same name as the source account. Monize attempts to auto-match QIF files to accounts by filename, so closer names mean less manual mapping during import.

The order in which you import your QIF files matters. Monize handles transfers between accounts by matching pending transactions from previously imported files. Importing in the right order ensures transfers are linked correctly and reduces manual cleanup. This ordering applies to the QIF method only. A direct .mny import brings every account across in one pass and links transfers from Money's own records, so there is no order to get right.

Import your accounts in this order: 1. Asset Accounts | 2. Bank, Credit Card and Line of Credit Accounts (Home Currency) | 3. Bank, Credit Card and Line of Credit Accounts (Foreign Currency) | 4. Investment Cash Accounts (-Regular exports) | 5. Investment Brokerage Accounts (-Investment exports) Loan accounts can't be exported from Microsoft Money, but the transactions will be built via the payments made from the source accounts. The import process will recognize this and ask for confirmation.

Order Account Type Reason 1 Asset Accounts Assets rarely have transfers to other accounts. Import them first to establish any asset-related categories. 2 Bank Accounts (Home Currency) These are your primary accounts and typically the source/destination of most transfers. Importing them early means subsequent imports can link transfers to these accounts. 3 Bank Accounts (Foreign Currency) Foreign currency accounts may have transfers to/from home currency accounts. Importing after home currency accounts ensures the other side of cross-currency transfers already exists. 4 Investment Cash Accounts Import the "-Regular" (cash) QIF files for investment accounts next. These contain deposits/withdrawals to the investment account's cash balance, often transferred from bank accounts (already imported). 5 Investment Brokerage Accounts Import the "-Investment" QIF files last among the investment pair. These contain buy/sell/dividend transactions. Monize automatically creates the corresponding cash-side transactions in the linked cash account.

Monize supports importing multiple QIF files in a single bulk operation. When you select multiple files: Files are processed sequentially in the order listed Categories, payees, and accounts created in file 1 are available for file 2, and so on Transfer matching happens across all files in the batch The best approach is to select ALL your QIF files at once and let Monize process them in order.

h: Part 6: Importing QIF Files into Monize Step by Step
x: Navigate to Tools > Import Transactions to begin the import process.

The upload step presents a drag-and-drop area where you can select your QIF files. Click the upload area or drag your QIF files onto it You can select multiple files at once for bulk import Monize parses each file and extracts metadata: Account type detected from the QIF header Number of transactions Date range of transactions Categories found Transfer accounts referenced Securities found (for investment files) After parsing, you advance to account selection. Pre-Selection: If you start the import from a specific account ( Accounts , edit the account, Import ), that account is pre-selected. A blue banner shows "Importing to: [Account Name]", and for a single file the account selection step is skipped.

For each QIF file, you need to specify which Monize account the transactions should be imported into. A gray information box shows: File: The filename being imported Transactions: Number of transactions found Date Range: Earliest to latest transaction dates Detected Type: Account type identified from the QIF header (e.g., Chequing, Investment, Credit Card) Choose from the "Import into account" dropdown. The dropdown shows all compatible accounts: For investment QIF files (detected type: Investment), only brokerage accounts are shown For regular QIF files , all non-brokerage accounts are shown Auto-Matching: Monize attempts to match QIF filenames to account names automatically. If a match is found, it is pre-selected in the dropdown. When you upload several files at once, every file gets its own dropdown; files matched by name are shown in green, and files Monize could only guess for (by account type) in amber. If the destination account does not exist yet: Click + Create new account ( + Create new under a file in a bulk import) Fill in: Account name (e.g., "My Chequing") Account type (Chequing, Savings, Credit Card, etc.) Currency (USD, CAD, etc.) Click Create The new account is created immediately and auto-selected as the destination. Investment accounts: When you create an Investment type account during import, both the brokerage and linked cash accounts are created automatically. Monize detects the date format (MM/DD/YYYY, DD/MM/YYYY, YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-DD-MM) from the dates in each file; the date range in the information box shows how they were read. There is no override on this step, so if the dates look swapped, check your Windows regional date setting and export again.

If the QIF file contains category references, you need to map them to Monize categories. Categories are displayed in three groups: Needs attention (amber border) -- Categories that could not be auto-matched. These require your input. Auto-matched to loan accounts (shown expanded) -- Categories that match loan or mortgage account names, indicating loan payments. Auto-matched to categories (collapsed by default) -- Categories that Monize matched to existing categories. Click Show n auto-matched to categories to expand and verify. At the top of the list, a line summarizes the mapping status: "[X] need attention" (amber) -- categories requiring manual mapping "[X] matched to categories" (green) -- successfully auto-matched "[X] matched to loans" (blue) -- matched to loan accounts For each unmatched category, you can: Option A: Map to an existing category Select from the dropdown of existing Monize categories Option B: Create a new category Enter a new category name under Or create new Choose a Parent category , or + Create new parent... to name a new one The category is created during import Option C: Skip the category Leave the dropdown at Skip (no category) to import transactions without a category You can categorize them later in the Transactions page If a QIF category name matches an existing loan or mortgage account name, Monize detects it as a loan payment. These transactions are imported as transfers to the loan account rather than regular categorized transactions. You can also tick This is a loan payment on any category yourself. Then pick the loan under Select existing loan , or create it with Or create new loan : its name, Loan type (Loan or Mortgage), Institution and Initial loan amount (the original principal).

This step appears only when importing investment QIF files that contain security references. Monize can look up securities automatically: A lookup runs automatically for every unmatched security when you first reach this step ("Looking up securities...") Click Lookup next to any security to search again by what is in its symbol or name field; when several securities fit, you choose one from a list Lookup results fill in the security name, symbol, type, exchange and currency, trying your preferred exchanges ( Settings > Preferences ) first For each security, you can: Option A: Map to an existing security Select from the "Map to existing" dropdown Option B: Create a new security Enter the symbol under Or create new (symbol) (e.g., "AAPL") Enter the Security name (e.g., "Apple Inc.") Select the Security type (Stock, ETF, Mutual Fund, Bond, Option, GIC, Cryptocurrency, Cash/Money Market, Other) Choose the Exchange (e.g., "NYSE", "TSX") and the Currency ; picking an exchange sets the currency it trades in Each security row is colour-coded: Green border -- Ready to import (mapped to existing or new security details filled in) Amber border -- Needs attention (no mapping selected)

This step appears when the QIF file references transfers to other accounts (e.g., [Savings Account] notation in QIF). Note: This step is skipped for investment QIF files. Investment transfers are handled automatically through the linked cash account. For each referenced transfer account: Option A: Map to an existing account Select from the "Map to existing" dropdown Option B: Create a new account Enter the account name under Or create new Select the Account type Select the Currency Tip: If you are importing all files in bulk, transfers between imported accounts are linked automatically. You only need to map accounts that are not part of the current import batch.

The review step shows a summary of everything that will happen during import. File: filename.qif Transactions to import: [count] Target account: [account name] Files to Import: List of each file with transaction count and target account Total: [X] files, [Y] transactions Categories: Total, mapped, new to create, mapped to loans, new loans to create Transfer Accounts: Total, mapped, new to create Securities: Total, mapped, new to create Click Import Transactions to begin. The button shows a loading spinner while processing. For bulk imports, files are processed sequentially. Entities created in earlier files (categories, accounts, payees, securities) are available for subsequent files. Important: Each file is imported inside a database transaction. If the import of a file fails, none of its changes are kept. A single transaction that cannot be imported is counted as an error and the rest of the file still imports.

After successful import, the complete step shows detailed results. Metric Description Imported Number of transactions successfully imported Skipped Number of transfers skipped because the other account's import already recorded them; the skipped rows are listed Errors Number of transactions that failed to import Categories created New categories added Accounts created New accounts added Payees created New payees added Securities created New securities added For bulk imports, each file shows its individual results with success/error indicators: Green background for files with no errors Red background for files with errors, including the first 3 error messages If the import created a loan or mortgage account without scheduled payments, a Set Up Recurring Payments box offers Set Up Payments for it. After import, you have two options: "View Investments" / "View Transactions" -- Go directly to see your imported data. These take you to the account(s) you just imported -- single, bulk, or multi-account QIF -- not whichever account you last happened to view; imports into closed accounts stay visible too. "Import More Files" -- Return to the upload step for additional imports
These steps apply to the QIF method. After a direct .mny import, see After the Import instead -- the verification report covers most of this for you.

Compare each account's current balance in Monize against your Microsoft Money records. If balances do not match: Check the opening balance -- it should match the balance as of the first transaction date Look for missing or duplicate transactions Check that transfers between accounts were matched correctly (not doubled)

Cross-currency transfers from Microsoft Money may need manual adjustment because the QIF format does not include exchange rate information. Look for transactions with a memo containing "PENDING IMPORT" and update the amounts to reflect the actual exchange rates.

Navigate to Investments Check that each holding shows the correct quantity and cost basis Compare against your Microsoft Money portfolio summary Check that the securities created during import have the right symbols and names

Securities created during import use the symbol, exchange and type entered on the Map Securities step, and get price updates like any other. If one was created with a guessed symbol: Navigate to Tools > Securities Edit the security to correct its symbol, exchange, and type Prices are fetched for the corrected symbol from then on

Navigate to Tools > Categories and review the category hierarchy. Categories imported from Microsoft Money use the QIF naming convention (with / separating parent and child). You may want to reorganize or rename them.

QIF export from Microsoft Money does not include scheduled/recurring transactions. You must recreate these manually: Navigate to Bills & Deposits Create each recurring bill and deposit See Bills and Deposits for details The direct .mny import brings scheduled bills across, so this step is not needed there.
Run the Uncategorized Transactions report ( Reports > Uncategorized Transactions ) to find any transactions that were imported without a category. Assign categories as needed.
Navigate to the Dashboard and check the Net Worth chart. Monize automatically calculates monthly net worth snapshots after import. Compare the trend against your Microsoft Money net worth report.

If your import did not go as expected and you want to start fresh, you can delete all your financial data without losing your user account or settings. Navigate to Settings Scroll to the Danger Zone section Click "Delete Data..." Check all four optional boxes (Accounts, Categories, Payees, Currency preferences) for a completely clean slate Enter your password to confirm This removes all transactions, accounts, categories, securities, budgets, and other financial data. Your user account, preferences, and security settings (2FA, trusted devices) are preserved. You can then re-import your files. If you are re-running a direct .mny import, you do not need to do this first -- tick Start fresh on the review step and the same operation runs as part of the import. For more details, see Settings and Security > Danger Zone .
For .mny import problems, see Troubleshooting the .mny Import .

Cause: Trying to import an Investment QIF file into a non-brokerage account, or a Regular QIF file into a brokerage account. Solution: Make sure you select the correct account type: Investment QIF files (-Investment) go into brokerage accounts Regular QIF files (-Regular or standard banking) go into non-brokerage accounts Cause: The date format was detected incorrectly (e.g., MM/DD was interpreted as DD/MM). Solution: The date format of a QIF file is detected from its dates, and there is no override in the wizard. Check the short date format in Windows' regional settings, export the file again from Microsoft Money, and import the new file. Or use the direct .mny import, which does not depend on a date format at all. Cause: Importing the same file twice, or transfer transactions appearing in both accounts. Solution: Monize skips the second side of a transfer that is already recorded when importing the other account If duplicates still appear, use the Duplicate Transaction Finder report to identify and remove them For future imports, always import all related files in a single bulk operation Cause: The transfer accounts were not mapped correctly, or the files were imported in separate sessions. Solution: When possible, import all files at once using bulk import Check that account names in QIF match the Monize account names Manually link unmatched transfers by editing the transactions Cause: Microsoft Money does not include a security master list in QIF exports. Solution: During the Map Securities step, use the Lookup button to search for each security If lookup fails, manually enter the symbol, name, type, exchange and currency After import, check the securities created in Tools > Securities Cause: Microsoft Money's opening balance transaction may not match the expected starting point. Solution: Navigate to Accounts Edit the account Adjust the opening balance and opening date to match your records The current balance will be recalculated Cause: QIF files do not contain exchange rate information. Solution: Search transactions for "PENDING IMPORT" in the memo field Edit each flagged transaction Adjust the amount in the destination account to match the actual transfer amount This correctly sets the effective exchange rate Cause: Very large QIF files (near the 10 MB limit or files with thousands of transactions). Solution: The import has a 5-minute timeout If a single file is too large, try splitting it into smaller date ranges in Microsoft Money

h: Part 10: What Cannot Be Imported via QIF
x: The QIF format and Microsoft Money export have limitations. The following data must be recreated manually in Monize. Several of these limits do not apply to the direct .mny import -- the right-hand column says which. Data Type Status (QIF) Notes Account balances Auto-detected Extracted from QIF "Opening Balance" record. The .mny import computes and verifies every balance from the file Transactions Imported All regular and investment transactions Voided transactions Imported (as void) Money exports these as $0.00 rows with a VOID payee prefix and the amount dropped. Monize strips the prefix (so no separate "VOID ..." payees are created), marks the transaction void , and adds a note that the original amount was lost in the export. The Dashboard is your financial command center -- a single-page overview of your accounts, spending, income, net worth, investments, and upcoming bills. Use Customize beside the greeting to change the dashboard. Open features such as Shared Expenses from Tools , or from the navigation menu on a phone.

When you log in, the Dashboard is the first page you see. It greets you by name and arranges its widgets in a two-column grid (one column on a phone). Every widget's title is a link to the page or report it summarizes, so you can go from the summary to the detail in one click. The default layout shows these widgets, in this order: Widget Shows Favourite Accounts Balances of the accounts you starred Upcoming Bills & Deposits Scheduled transactions coming due Top Movers The day's biggest price moves among your securities (with investments only) Portfolio Value over Time Your investments' value over time (with investments only) Net Worth Net worth month by month Assets vs Liabilities What you own against what you owe today Expenses by Category Where your money went Income vs Expenses Money in against money out Budget Status How your current budget period is going Spending Insights Observations from the AI insights Many more widgets are available but hidden by default; see Optional Widgets .

Click Customize in the top-right of the dashboard header to tailor which widgets appear and in what order. The Customize dashboard dialog mirrors your dashboard: widgets flow left to right, two per row on large screens. Show or hide widgets -- click a widget's X to hide it, or add one back later Reorder widgets -- drag a widget tile to a new position, or use the arrow buttons (the arrow buttons also work on a phone, where widgets stack in a single column) Add opt-in widgets -- hidden widgets appear in a Hidden widgets tray beneath the layout; click one to add it to your dashboard Reset to default -- restore the standard layout at any time Click Save to apply your changes. At least one widget must stay on the dashboard. Your layout is saved to your account, so it syncs across all your devices .

Configurable widgets show a gear icon in their header. Click it to open that widget's settings, where (depending on the widget) you can: Choose a Timeframe preset. Each widget offers the ranges that suit it: the spending and income widgets offer MTD, 1M, 3M, 6M, 1Y and YTD; Portfolio Value offers 1W, MTD, 3M, 6M, YTD, 1Y, 2Y, 5Y and All; Net Worth offers 1Y, 2Y, 5Y and 10Y Filter the widget to specific Accounts Pick the Chart type or View (for example, pie or bar, region or country, labels or legend) Set a custom Display name and Description so the widget's header reads however you like The chosen timeframe is shown beside the gear. These per-widget settings also persist across your devices.

The widgets below are hidden by default and can be added from the Customize dialog. Most are derived from a report and carry their own gear settings. Widget Shows Availability Cash Flow Forecast Projected balances from your scheduled transactions Always Favourite Securities Quotes for the securities you starred With securities only Favourite Reports The reports you've starred; click one to open it Always Spending by Payee Spending grouped by payee Always Monthly Spending Trend Spending and income trended by month Always Income by Source Income grouped by source, as a pie or bar chart Always Credit Utilization by Account Utilization for each credit account Always Total Credit Utilization Combined used vs available credit Always Sector Allocation Portfolio breakdown by sector Investments only Security Type Allocation Holdings by security type or asset class Investments only Geographic Allocation Holdings by region, exchange, or country Investments only Top Recurring Expenses Your largest recurring expenses Always Weekend vs Weekday Spending Spending split between weekends and weekdays Always Cash Flow Sankey Where your income came from and where it went Always Warranties expiring soon Warranties that expire in the next 30 days (see Warranties ) Always Note The investment widgets (Top Movers, Portfolio Value, Sector Allocation, Security Type Allocation, and Geographic Allocation) only appear when you have investment holdings, and Favourite Securities only when you have securities. Note Delegates: If you're viewing an account you've been granted access to, the dashboard is limited to the Favourite Accounts widget, plus Upcoming Bills and the expiring-warranties widget if those sections were granted. The Customize button is hidden for delegates. See Shared Access .

This widget lists the accounts you starred as favourites. Each card shows: Account name and its institution Current balance in the account's currency (the currency is named when it is not your home currency) For credit cards with statement dates set, the payment Due day and the Settlement day of the billing cycle Click a card to open that account's transactions, or its detail page if you chose Show its dashboard under Default Account View in Settings -> Preferences . To mark an account as a favourite, go to Accounts and click the star beside it. See Favourite Accounts .

You can reorder your favourite account cards to arrange them in the order you prefer: Click Reorder in the widget's header Drag the account cards into your preferred order, or use the up and down arrow buttons Click Done ; the new order is saved automatically
When an investment account is a favourite, the dashboard card displays its market value rather than the cash balance. Clicking it opens the Investments page filtered to that account.

The Upcoming Bills & Deposits widget shows your scheduled transactions that are coming due, ordered by date. Each entry shows: When it is due -- Overdue, Today, Tomorrow, or the number of days left Name and payee, with a Bill , Deposit , Transfer , or Reminder badge A Manual badge on schedules that are not posted automatically Amount of the occurrence, flagged when posting it would take its account below zero Two switches in the header change what the widget shows: Due soon lists only what is overdue or inside each schedule's reminder window; All upcoming lists the next occurrence of every active schedule, however far off The List and Calendar buttons switch between the list and a small month calendar The list shows a few more entries than you have favourite accounts, with a +N more link to the rest. Click an entry to open it in Bills & Deposits , ready to post. This helps you anticipate upcoming cash flow needs and ensure sufficient funds are available.

The Cash Flow Forecast widget (opt-in) is the same forecast as on the Bills & Deposits page, with its own period and accounts. Choose 7D , 30D , 90D , 6M , or 1Y in the header, and pick the accounts to forecast in the gear settings. No selection draws all your accounts as one line. A scheduled transaction that fell due and was neither posted nor skipped counts on the first day of the forecast.

If you have an active budget, the Budget Status widget summarizes your current budget period: Overall progress -- the share of the budget spent, and the amount spent against the total Safe to spend today -- how much you can spend per day and stay on track Days left in the current budget period Top Categories -- the categories closest to their limits, with progress bars Click View full budget to open the full Budget Dashboard . Note Without an active budget, the widget offers a Create Budget button instead.

The Spending Insights widget lists the active observations from Financial Insights -- notable changes in spending, unusual transactions, and other things worth your attention -- each as a short, plain-language note coloured by severity. The header counts how many are active. Insights are generated by your AI provider on the Insights page. Until any exist, the widget offers Go to Insights , where you can generate them.

For new users, a Getting Started card above the widgets links to the first setup tasks: Review your settings -- currency, date format, and theme Set up categories -- create categories or import a default set Add your first account Import from QIF -- bring in accounts and transactions from QIF files It also offers to start the guided introduction tour ( Retake it once you have finished it). Click Dismiss (the X) to hide the card for good.

If you hold investments, the Top Movers widget shows the securities in your portfolio with the largest daily price changes, with the trading day it compares named in the header. All , Gainers , and Losers filter the list by direction Price ranks by the change in each security's price; Holdings ranks by the change in the value of what you hold Click a security to open its price history, with your own buys and sells marked on the chart The refresh button fetches the latest prices; View portfolio opens Investments Only moves from the same trading day are compared, so a security whose price was not updated today is left out rather than ranked against today's moves.

If you hold investments, this widget charts your investments' total value over the chosen timeframe, with the current value and the Investment result for the period (what the investments themselves earned, with your own deposits and withdrawals and uninvested cash left out). The refresh button updates the current value. Filter it to specific investment accounts in the gear settings.

The Favourite Securities widget (opt-in) lists the securities you've starred, each with its latest quote and daily price change. It's a watchlist for the tickers you care about, whether or not you currently hold them. To add a security here, open Tools -> Securities and star the securities you want to track. The refresh button fetches the latest prices, and clicking a security opens its price history.

The Expenses by Category widget is a donut chart of your spending by category over a selectable timeframe (default: 1M), optionally filtered to specific accounts. The total spent sits inside the donut. Hover over a segment to see the category name and amount Click a segment to open its transactions for the same period Small categories are grouped into Other ; click it to see what it contains Refunds reduce the category they were filed under, so the figures agree with the Spending by Category report In the gear settings, Top level categories counts subcategories against their parent, and the View choice names the categories in Labels beside the donut or in a Legend under it

This bar chart compares your income and expenses over a selectable timeframe (default: 1M), optionally filtered by account. Each period shows: A green bar for total income A red bar for total expenses Totals for Income , Expenses , and Net below the chart Income and expenses are classified by category type (income category vs expense category), not by the sign of the amount. Clicking on an income or expense bar navigates to the Transactions page filtered to the corresponding category type for that period.

The Net Worth chart tracks your total net worth month by month, with the current figure and its change over the timeframe: Assets -- every account with a positive balance, plus investment market values Liabilities -- credit cards, loans, mortgages, and lines of credit Net worth -- assets minus liabilities By default the bars are stacked By account type , showing what each type adds to (or takes from) your net worth, with net worth itself as a line across them. In the gear settings, choose Net worth for one solid bar per month, and a timeframe of 1Y, 2Y, 5Y, or 10Y. The two buttons in the header switch to a stacked view of the share of assets against liabilities each month. Accounts you excluded from net worth are left out.

The Assets vs Liabilities widget compares your current total assets against your total liabilities as a donut, with your net worth inside it. Where the Net Worth chart tracks the trend, this widget shows the balance between the two sides today. In the gear settings, choose whether the two sides are named in Labels beside the donut or in a Legend under it.
The Spending by Payee widget (opt-in) ranks your spending by payee over the chosen timeframe (default: 3M).
The Monthly Spending Trend widget (opt-in) trends your expenses and income month by month, over 6M, YTD, 1Y (the default), or 2Y.
The Income by Source widget (opt-in) breaks down your income by category over the chosen timeframe (default: 1Y), as a pie or a bar chart.

Two opt-in widgets track how much of your available credit you are using. They include credit cards and lines of credit that have a credit limit set. Credit Utilization by Account shows the utilization of each account Total Credit Utilization shows your combined used and available credit

Three opt-in widgets break down your holdings, each filterable to specific investment accounts: Sector Allocation -- your portfolio by sector, counting both the stocks you hold directly and the sectors inside your ETFs Security Type Allocation -- your holdings by security type (stocks, ETFs, mutual funds, bonds, cash), or by Asset class , which looks inside funds Geographic Allocation -- your holdings by Region , Exchange , or Country ; region and exchange group each holding by where it is listed, while country looks inside funds

The Top Recurring Expenses widget (opt-in) finds the expenses that repeat and charts the largest, with your estimated monthly total inside the donut. In the gear settings, choose the range it looks back over (6M to All), the Minimum occurrences a charge needs to count, and whether to show Labels or a Legend .
The Weekend vs Weekday Spending widget (opt-in) splits your spending between weekends and weekdays over 1M, 3M (the default), 6M, or 1Y. The By day view breaks it down by day of the week.

The Cash Flow Sankey widget (opt-in) is a flow diagram of the chosen period (default: MTD): income categories flow into your income, and out to expense categories, savings and investments, debt payments, and other accounts, with any leftover shown as unspent. In the gear settings, choose Categories or Subcategories for the level of Detail , and the Diagram or Table view. Click a node to open its transactions. The full version is the Cash Flow Sankey report in Reports .

Investment prices can be refreshed manually from the refresh buttons on the Top Movers, Favourite Securities, and Portfolio Value widgets. Prices and exchange rates are also updated automatically on weekdays at 5 PM New York time.
Monize supports a wide variety of account types to represent your complete financial picture. This page covers creating, managing, and organizing your accounts.

Monize supports 10 account types: Account Type Description Typical Use Chequing Checking or current account Day-to-day banking Savings Savings account Emergency fund, short-term savings Credit Card Credit card account Credit card spending and payments Investment Brokerage account Stocks, ETFs, mutual funds, bonds Loan Installment loan Personal loans, auto loans Line of Credit Line of credit Revolving credit facilities Mortgage Mortgage account Home mortgage tracking Asset Asset tracking Property, vehicles, collectibles Cash Cash wallet or petty cash Physical cash tracking Other Miscellaneous Any account that does not fit other types

Credit Card accounts include a credit limit and optional statement dates (the payment due day and the settlement day of the billing cycle). The available credit is the credit limit minus the current balance. Loan and Mortgage accounts are debt accounts with a dedicated payment setup, so Monize can split each payment into principal and interest, show an amortization schedule, and project your payoff. Mortgages add a mortgage type, a rate-fixed term, and an amortization period. See Loan and Mortgage Setup . Line of Credit accounts are revolving debt accounts with an optional credit limit and interest rate; their detail page shows a revolving-balance view. Investment accounts are normally created as a linked pair -- a brokerage ledger for your securities and a cash ledger for the money -- shown as one account. See Investment Account Pairs for details. Asset accounts track the value of physical assets like property or vehicles. Transactions on asset accounts represent changes in value, booked to a value-change category you choose.
Navigate to Accounts from the top navigation bar Click + New Account Fill in the New Account form:

Field Description Account Name A descriptive name for the account Account Type Select from the available types Currency The currency this account operates in. It is locked once the account has transactions

Field Description Opening Balance The starting balance (defaults to 0). For loans and mortgages this is the Loan Amount or Mortgage Amount Account Number The institution's account number for your reference Institution The financial institution that holds the account (see Financial Institutions ). Required for loans and mortgages, where it is labelled Lender/Institution Credit Limit For every type except assets, loans, and mortgages Interest Rate % For every type except assets; required for loans and mortgages Foreign Currency Conversion Fee The percentage your bank adds to purchases in another currency, so Monize can show what foreign transactions really cost you Statement Dates Credit cards only: the Due Date and Settlement Date (day of the month) Description Any additional notes about the account Favourite Show the account on the Dashboard (the star button) Exclude from Net Worth Leave the account out of net worth figures and reports Click Create Account When you edit an existing account, the form also offers Balance alerts : Notify below and Notify above amounts that send you a notification when the balance crosses them. The edit form's Import and Export buttons import a QIF file into the account or export its transactions. Tip When importing from Microsoft Money, you do not need to create accounts manually if you plan to create them during the import process. However, creating accounts first gives you more control over the exact names, types, and opening balances. Note When you choose a Loan or Mortgage account type, the form reveals extra payment fields, and an Asset shows a Value Change Category and a Date Acquired (the asset is left out of net worth before that date). See Loan and Mortgage Setup below.

Selecting the Loan or Mortgage account type on the account form reveals a dedicated payment setup panel so Monize can track your amortization, split each payment into principal and interest, and project your payoff. Saving it creates the scheduled payment in Bills & Deposits .

When you create a Loan , the Loan Payment Details panel asks for: Field Description Payment Amount The regular payment made against the loan Payment Frequency Weekly, Every 2 Weeks, Semi-Monthly, Monthly, Quarterly, or Yearly First Payment Date The date the first scheduled payment is due Payment From Account The account the payment is drawn from (e.g. your chequing account) Interest Category The expense category the interest portion of each payment is booked to As you fill in the loan amount, interest rate, payment, frequency, and first payment date, a Payment Preview appears showing the principal and interest portions of the first payment, the total number of payments, and the estimated payoff date.

Mortgage accounts offer everything a loan does, plus mortgage-specific settings in the Mortgage Details panel: Field Description Mortgage Type Annuity (Level Payment) -- the total payment is the same every period, including most variable-rate mortgages; Canadian Fixed Rate -- interest compounds twice a year; Linear (Constant Principal) -- the principal part is the same every period and the total falls; Interest Only -- you pay only interest and the balance is repaid at the end Rate-Fixed Term How long the interest rate or contract term runs, entered as years plus months; Monize can remind you before it ends Amortization Period The full amortization, entered as years plus months Payment Frequency Monthly, Semi-Monthly (15th and month end), Bi-Weekly, Accelerated Bi-Weekly, Weekly, or Accelerated Weekly. The accelerated frequencies are for annuity mortgages only First Payment Date , Payment From Account , Interest Category Same as for loans What an Extra Repayment Does Linear mortgages only: whether an extra repayment shortens the term or lowers the installment Not sure which type you have? Click Not sure? Enter a few installments , copy two or three consecutive installments from a statement, and click Suggest a Type ; Monize explains its suggestion, and Use This Type applies it. The Amortization Preview shows the calculated payment amount, the effective rate , the first payment's principal and interest split, the total number of payments, total interest, and the estimated payoff date. A linear or interest-only mortgage has no fixed payment, so each installment is worked out on its due date from the balance and the rate.

If your bank posts one undivided debit for each mortgage or loan installment, turn on Match imported bank payments and enter a Payee pattern (with a * wildcard, for example *MY BANK* ) and an optional Description pattern . When an imported or synced bank row matches, Monize splits it into principal and interest, books it as the installment, and marks the scheduled payment as paid, instead of you ending up with a duplicate. Turning this on turns off auto-posting on the linked bill, because the bank's own row is what gets matched.

If you have already imported transaction history for a loan or mortgage that has no scheduled payment, its edit form offers Set Up Recurring Payments . The Set Up Loan Payments (or Set Up Mortgage Payments ) dialog analyses your existing transactions and detects: The payment frequency and regular payment amount The principal / interest split from your most recent payment Any recurring extra principal payments An estimated interest rate, interest category, and source account Each detected value is presented with a confidence indicator for you to review and adjust before clicking Set Up Payments . You can also choose to Automatically post transactions when due . If you are not sure how to record loan payments in the first place, a collapsible How to record loan payments guide is built into the form: principal is a transfer to the loan account, interest is an expense.

So that extra principal payments are scored correctly in the schedule, simulator, and Past Impact analysis, the mortgage form's Overpayment recognition settings tell Monize how you record them. An overpayment is recognized as 100% principal when it matches any one of: An Overpayment category An Overpayment payee Overpayment memo text (a case-insensitive match against the payment's memo) Any single match is enough -- you do not have to use all three. A loan's detail page offers the same settings under Payment recognition .

Banks book interest in different ways, and Monize reads all of them. The Interest Recording setting tells Monize how to find the interest portion of each payment: Mode Use when Automatic (recommended) Let Monize detect the style (the default) Split leg of the payment Each payment is a split transaction with a principal line and an interest line Separate expense (principal is a transfer) Interest is booked as its own standalone expense transaction, apart from the principal transfer Interest-only grace periods appear as their own rows in the schedule. Interest is counted by its category across your full history regardless of the loan's configured start date, so a migrated loan's earlier activity is not hidden. If you refinance sequentially, give each refinance its own interest category so the periods stay cleanly separated. See the loan detail page tools for how recognized overpayments and interest flow into the simulator and rate detection.

Each account can record the financial institution that holds it -- the bank, brokerage, credit union, or lender behind the account. Institutions are records of their own, kept on Tools -> Institutions , so several accounts can share one and each institution carries its brand logo.

Identify accounts at a glance -- The institution's logo and name appear beside the account in the account list and on the dashboard. Group related accounts -- The Institutions page counts the accounts at each institution, so you can see your exposure to any one bank or lender. Required for debt accounts -- The institution is mandatory for loan and mortgage accounts, since it identifies your lender. For all other account types it is optional.

Open the account form when creating a new account, or click Edit on an existing account. In the Institution field, select an existing institution, or type a new name to create one. Click Create Account or Update Account . On the Financial Institutions page, New Institution adds one with its Name , Website , and an optional two-letter Country . The logo is fetched automatically from the website. Each institution's Accounts action lists the accounts assigned to it, where you can add or remove accounts. Deleting an institution unassigns its accounts without deleting them.

The Accounts page lists all your accounts grouped by type, each group with its own subtotal. The table has these columns: Account Name -- with the institution's logo, the favourite star, and the account's description Type Status -- Active or Closed Last Reconciled -- the date of the account's last reconciliation, or Never Unreconciled -- how many of the account's transactions are not yet reconciled (unreconciled or cleared, whatever their date): the transactions the Reconcile screen lists. It refreshes when you return to the page, so a reconcile done in another tab or on another device shows here too Balance -- in the account's currency; an investment account shows its combined value with the investments and the cash each on its own line beneath it (at Normal density) Actions -- Details , Edit , Reconcile , Close (or Reopen ), and Delete The Balance always stays in view. On a narrower window the columns to its left make room for it: long account names are shortened, and Last Reconciled and Unreconciled are left out first, then Status , then Type . Click an account to open its transactions. Investment accounts open their detail page , and so does every account if you choose Show its dashboard under Default Account View in Settings -> Preferences . Details always opens the detail page. Close is only available when the account's balance is zero, and Delete only for accounts with no transactions (see Deleting Accounts ).

At the top of the accounts page, the summary shows: Total Active Accounts Net Worth -- assets minus liabilities Total Assets -- the accounts with a positive balance, plus investment market values Total Liabilities -- the money you owe The three money figures leave out accounts you excluded from net worth.

The filter bar above the list lets you narrow down which accounts are shown: Search -- A text box that filters accounts by name as you type. Click the X inside the box to clear the search. Status -- Switch between All , Active , and Closed accounts. Account Type -- Show only selected account types (e.g. only chequing and savings). It lists just the types you actually have; leaving it empty shows all types. Net Worth -- Show the accounts included in or excluded from net worth (shown when you have excluded an account). Shared with me -- Show only the joint accounts other people share with you (shown when you have any). A counter beside the filters shows how many accounts match, in the form "X of Y accounts" . When the filters match nothing, a Clear Filters action resets them all at once. Note Your filter and row density choices are remembered between visits.

An account's detail page is tailored to its type, rather than a plain transaction list. The header has View Transactions (the account's register) and Edit Account , plus Reconcile on banking accounts and credit cards (an investment account has its own buttons, below), and a caret beside the account name that switches to another account, with your favourites first.

Summary cards: Current Balance , Projected Balance in 90 days, Money In and Money Out this month, and the Average Balance over the trailing 12 months; with an interest rate set, also the Interest Rate and the Interest Earned this year Balance History chart, with a 90-day balance forecast projected from your scheduled bills and deposits A Cash Flow chart of the net flow over the last 12 months Top Categories and Top Payees this month Recurring Charges : the scheduled bills on the account, plus Possible recurring charges found in its transactions, each with a Create bill button that turns it into a scheduled bill

Summary cards: Current Balance , Credit Limit , Available Credit , Utilization , and Interest Rate Current Statement Cycle : the statement balance, expenses and payments since the statement, the payment due date, and when the statement closes (needs the card's statement dates) Balance History Spending This Cycle by category, including late-posting, unreconciled charges carried over from the previous cycle , so the amount owed is right Interest & Fees charged this year A Payoff Calculator that estimates how long the balance takes to clear at a fixed monthly payment Make a Payment , which records a payment (the statement balance, the full balance, or a custom amount) from a chequing, savings, or cash account now, or schedules it monthly

Current Value , Purchase Value , Total Appreciation , and the Annualized rate A Value History chart Update Value , to record a new valuation as of a date An Equity panel when the asset is linked to its financing loan (for example, a house linked to its mortgage), showing value minus outstanding debt and equity over time. Use Link Loan to link one

Accounts with transactions in another currency gain a Foreign Currency Transaction Fees section: the fees paid per currency, charted over time, and a list of the foreign-currency transactions. Both export to CSV, and the chart to PNG.

An investment account's detail page is the Investments view for that one account: its Portfolio Summary , Asset Allocation , Portfolio Value Over Time , holdings, its Investment Income this year (dividends and interest, and realized gains), and the brokerage and cash registers of the pair behind a toggle. The header has Refresh to fetch the latest prices, Open in Investments , and Edit Account .
Loan, mortgage, and line-of-credit accounts have a detail page with their payment schedule and payoff tools. Open it with the Details row action , or from the account panel beside its register.

For loans and mortgages, the top of the page shows a row of summary cards: Card Meaning Current Balance The amount still owed Original Amount The opening balance (or the amount derived from history) Interest Rate The annual rate; Canadian fixed-rate mortgages also show the effective rate Payment The regular payment amount and its frequency (for a linear mortgage, the Next Installment and its due date) Est. Payoff When the loan is projected to be fully repaid Est. Remaining Interest The interest still to be paid over the remaining schedule Below the cards, the page includes a month-grouped Loan Schedule with real per-row interest, a Payoff Timeline chart, an interactive Overpayment Simulator with Saved Scenarios and a scenario comparison chart, an Impact of Overpayments Made (Past Impact) analysis, and an editable Rate History timeline with Detect Mortgage Type . A Payment matching panel shows the payment matching rule linked to the loan (or offers Create one ), lists the installments it settled, and offers Process history to run the rule over what you already imported. Export PDF saves the whole page as a PDF. The schedule, rate history, and scenario comparison export to CSV , and the payoff comparison chart exports to PNG . See Loan Detail Page Tools for the full breakdown of each tool.

Because a line of credit revolves rather than amortizing to a fixed payoff, its detail page shows a revolving-balance view instead of an amortization schedule: Current Balance -- The amount currently drawn Credit Limit and Available Credit -- Shown when a credit limit is set Utilization % -- The portion of the limit in use, colour-coded to flag high utilization Peak Balance -- The highest balance reached (shown when no limit is set) Balance History -- A chart of the balance over time, counting both draws and repayments

Click Edit on any account in the list, or Edit Account on its detail page, to open the Edit Account form. All fields from account creation can be updated, except the currency once the account has transactions. For loans and mortgages, changing the Payment From Account moves the upcoming scheduled payments and the payment-matching rule to the new account.

When an account is no longer active (e.g., you closed a bank account), you can close it in Monize: Make sure its balance is zero Click Close on the account in the list Confirm in the Close Account dialog Closed accounts are hidden from transaction dropdowns and appear under the Closed filter, but their historical data is preserved for reporting. Click Reopen to make an account active again. Closing or reopening an investment account acts on both of its ledgers.

Accounts can only be deleted if they have no transactions. If an account has transactions, you must either delete the transactions first or close the account instead. Deleting an investment account deletes both of its ledgers.
Reconciliation helps you verify that your Monize records match your bank statement.

Click Reconcile on the account in the list (or on its detail page) In Start Reconciliation , enter the Statement Date and Statement Ending Balance from your bank, then click Start Reconciliation The Unreconciled Transactions up to the statement date are listed. Tick each one that appears on your statement ( Select All and Select None help); transactions already cleared start ticked Watch the summary: Statement Balance , Reconciled Balance , the Selected total, and the Difference When the difference is zero, click Finish Reconciliation . The ticked transactions become Reconciled While reconciling you can sort by any column, Group by money in and out with a subtotal for each, edit or delete a row, and Add Transaction for one that is missing. Rows flagged Missed are dated on or before a statement you already reconciled; rows flagged Overdue have waited longer than a statement cycle. When you finish reconciling a credit card or line of credit, Monize offers to update the next instance of its scheduled payment to the reconciled balance ( Update Next Payment ), or to create one ( Create Scheduled Payment ). Accounts with transactions waiting too long to be reconciled show a reconciliation badge in the header, linking straight to that account's reconciliation. Tip To protect reconciled statements from accidental changes, turn on Lock reconciled transactions in Settings -> Preferences . Without it, Monize warns before an edit that would change a reconciled transaction's date or amount.

Status Meaning Unreconciled New transaction, not yet on a statement Cleared Matches a bank statement entry Reconciled Confirmed by a completed reconciliation Void Cancelled transaction; it no longer moves the balance

Mark accounts as favourites to have them displayed on the Dashboard: In the account list, click the star icon next to an account (or turn on Favourite in the account form) The account will appear in the Favourite Accounts widget on the Dashboard, and as a quick filter on the Transactions page

When you create an Investment account with Create as Cash + Brokerage pair (recommended) turned on, Monize creates two linked ledgers: Brokerage -- Holds your securities (stocks, ETFs, mutual funds, bonds, etc.) Cash -- Tracks the cash balance within the brokerage, and is where transfers in and out land The pair appears as one account in the account list, pickers, reports, and on the dashboard, under the name you gave it, with its combined value and the investments and cash shown beneath. When you buy securities, the cash balance decreases. When you sell or receive dividends, the cash balance increases. Reconciling an investment account reconciles its cash ledger. The edit form reaches the cash ledger's opening balance, account number, and description in its Cash account section. Clicking an investment account in the list opens its detail page ; its View Transactions opens the Investments page filtered to that account. Important For Microsoft Money users: In Microsoft Money, investment accounts contain both securities and cash in a single account. In Monize, these are split into two linked ledgers. When importing, the QIF parser handles this automatically -- the "Investment" export maps to the brokerage ledger and the "Regular" export maps to the cash ledger.

Each account has a designated currency. If you have accounts in different currencies: Transactions in that account are recorded in the account's currency (a transaction can be entered in another currency and converted; see Transactions ) The Dashboard and reports convert balances to your home currency using the latest exchange rates Cross-currency transfers record both amounts and the effective exchange rate For more details, see Currency Management .
Transactions are the core of your financial data in Monize. This page covers creating, searching, filtering, and managing transactions.

The Transactions page (the register) shows your transactions across all accounts, or the accounts you filter to. From top to bottom it has a chart summarizing what is in view, a row of your favourite accounts, the filter panel, and the list itself, which you can also read as a month calendar.

Navigate to Transactions Click + New Transaction Fill in the New Transaction form: The three buttons at the top of the form choose what you are entering: a Transaction , a Split across several categories (see Split Transactions ), or a Transfer between accounts (see Transfers Between Accounts ). Click Create Transaction . The arrow beside it offers Create Transaction & New , which saves and starts another, keeping the account and date.

Field Required Description Account Yes Which account this transaction belongs to Date Yes The date of the transaction Payee No Who the transaction was with Category No The expense or income category Amount Yes The transaction amount (negative for expenses, positive for income). The +/- button flips the sign, the calculator button works out a figure for you, and the currency button beside it lets you enter the amount in another currency Reference Number No Cheque number, confirmation number, or another reference Tags No One or more tags for flexible labelling; the tags you used most recently are listed first Description No Additional notes; links in it become clickable Status No Unreconciled, Cleared, Reconciled, or Void Attachments No Receipts, invoices, and other files (see Attachments ) Picking a payee fills in its default category, if you have not chosen one yet. When the Amount is an expense or income, its sign follows the category you choose, unless that category has automatic sign turned off.

The date field supports keyboard shortcuts for quick date entry: Key Action T Jump to today Y Jump to first day of the year R Jump to last day of the year M Jump to first day of the month H Jump to last day of the month + or = Next day - Previous day Page Up Next month Page Down Previous month Tip On desktop, hover over the info icon next to the date label to see these shortcuts. The calendar popover also has a year picker , so you can jump to a distant year in one step instead of paging month by month.

If the payee does not exist, type its name and choose to create it, directly from the transaction form without leaving the page. A category can be created the same way, including a subcategory written as Parent: Child .

The transaction form includes a history button (clock icon) next to the Payee field.
