Clicking it opens a popover listing recent transactions, and selecting one quick-fills the form with the payee, category, amount, description, and tags from that transaction. You can then adjust any field before saving. The history button appears on the new transaction form only -- it is hidden when editing an existing transaction. It is also available in split mode : selecting a recent split entry copies its payee and rebuilds the split rows from the source transaction. The popover behaves differently depending on whether a payee is selected: Context What the popover shows No payee selected Recent transactions : a deduplicated list with one row per unique payee/category combination. Useful when you have not decided what you are entering yet. Payee selected (or typed) Recent for that payee: its most recent transactions, in date order with no deduplication. Useful for repeating a familiar purchase exactly. For payee-scoped results, free-text payee names are matched exactly. If you have not selected an existing payee from the dropdown but have typed a name that matches a previous free-text entry, the popover scopes to that name. Splits are included. A split parent appears as a single row labelled "Split: Category A, Category B" (truncated with a count if more than two categories). Selecting it rebuilds the full split breakdown in the form. Transfers are excluded. Transfers between accounts are managed through their own form mode and do not appear in the quick-fill list. The number of entries shown in the popover is configurable from 3 to 20 (default 5 ). Adjust it under Settings -> Preferences -> Transactions -> Recent transactions in quick-fill . See Settings and Security for details. Tip When you are creating a transaction for a payee you visit often, type or pick the payee first, then open the history -- you will see only that payee's prior entries in date order, which is faster than scrolling the global list.

When you were charged in a currency other than the account's, click the currency button beside the Amount field and pick the Entry currency . Type the amount exactly as it appears on your statement: Monize fetches the exchange rate for the transaction's date and shows the converted total in the account's currency, with the rate it used. If the account has a foreign currency conversion fee set, the fee is included and named. Where no rate is found, enter the converted amount yourself. The register can show such a transaction in the account's currency or the original one.

Every transaction can carry files -- receipts, invoices, statements. In the form's Attachments section: Add attachment picks a file: an image or a PDF, up to 10 MB, and up to 10 files per transaction Scan document takes a photo with your phone's camera (or picks one on a desktop), finds the page in it, and lets you straighten it, drag its corners, and choose a colour, greyscale, or black-and-white finish before attaching it. The original photo is kept beside the clean copy On a new transaction the files are uploaded when you save it Click an attachment to preview it inside Monize: images at Fit to screen or Actual size , PDFs page by page, with Download at the bottom. The register has an Attachments column with the count, and the Attachments filter ( Any , Yes , No ) finds the transactions still missing a receipt. Below the attachments, Add warranty records a warranty for the purchase.

The transaction list displays your transactions in a table with the following columns: Column Description Date Transaction date. The Hide the year button in its header drops the year so more of the payee fits Account Account name (not shown when you are looking at a single account) Payee Who the transaction was with, with the payee's logo Category Assigned category, the destination of a transfer, or the categories of a split Description Transaction notes Ref # Reference or cheque number Tags The transaction's tags Attachments How many files are attached Amount Transaction amount (red for expenses, green for income) Balance Running balance, shown while the list is sorted by date and narrowed to one account or by a filter Status Reconciliation status; click to change it Actions Edit , Copy , and Delete Click a row to open it in the edit form. Click a payee, category, account, date, or tag in a row to filter the list by it. On a phone, each transaction is a card, and a long press opens its actions.
Click a column header to sort by it, and again to reverse the order. The running balance is only shown while the list is sorted by date. On a phone, sorting is a row of chips.

The Columns button above the list shows or hides columns; you can also right-click a column header (or long-press it on a phone) to hide it. Your choice is remembered in this browser. Default columns for every browser are set under Settings -> Preferences -> Default Views .

The density button above the list (labelled with the current density) adjusts how much fits on screen: Normal -- Default spacing with generous padding Compact -- Reduced padding, fits more transactions on screen Dense -- Minimal padding for maximum data density, with single-letter statuses

Transactions are paginated at 50 per page. Use the controls above and below the list to go to the first, previous, next, or last page, or type a page number. On a phone, swipe left or right to turn the page.
Export saves the transactions that match your filters as a CSV file.

The Table and Calendar buttons above the list switch the register to a month calendar. Each day shows its transactions, and your filters still apply. Previous month and Next month move through the months; click the month heading to jump to any month by typing it (for example Mar 1998 or 2026-03 ). On a phone, swipe left and right The Layers buttons show or hide each day's Transactions and its end-of-day Balances ; days after today show the projected balance, marked as such Scheduled transactions from Bills & Deposits appear on their due days, marked Scheduled (or Overdue ) Click a day to see everything on it, add a New transaction on this day , or Add a note : day notes are sticky notes that can cover one day or a span of days
The filter panel provides powerful options for finding specific transactions. Hide folds it away.

Filter Description Search Free text, or the search syntax Show Accounts Offer All , Active , or Closed accounts in the account filter Accounts Filter by one or more accounts Payees Filter by one or more payees Categories Filter by one or more categories Tags Filter by one or more tags Status Filter by one or more reconciliation statuses (Unreconciled, Cleared, Reconciled, Void) Tag key and Condition Filter by a key:value tag : has a value, has no value, value contains, or value does not contain Time Period Quick presets that set the date range for you: All Dates, Today, Yesterday, This Week, Last Week, Last 30 Days, Month to Date, Last Month, Last 365 Days, Year to Date, Last Year, or Custom Start Date and End Date Set the date range yourself Amount From and Amount To Set a minimum and/or maximum amount Currency Transactions entered in a particular foreign currency Attachments Yes or No to find transactions with or without attachments Note When the filter panel is collapsed, each active filter appears as a removable chip -- click the x on a chip to clear just that filter. If any of your accounts are marked as favourites, a Favourites row of quick-select buttons appears above the panel so you can limit the list to a favourite account in one tap.

Several words find the transactions that contain all of them, anywhere in the payee, description, reference, category, tags, or transfer account. A word that reads as an amount in your number format also matches that exact amount, and one that reads as a date in your date format (ISO YYYY-MM-DD is always accepted) matches that date. A line under the box shows how Monize read your search, and the ? button lists the syntax; choose an example to put it in the box. Type To find costco gas Transactions containing both words "costco gas" That exact phrase -refund Leave out anything matching refund payee:costco Payee contains costco payee:="Costco" Payee is exactly Costco #10 Cheque or reference number 10 exactly ref:10* Reference starts with 10 amount:>100 Amount over 100 amount:50..100 Amount from 50 to 100 date:2026-03 Any day in March 2026 is:split Split transactions (also is:transfer , is:uncategorized ) has:attachment Has an attachment (also has:warranty , has:ref , has:memo , has:tag ) The fields are payee , memo (the description), cat , tag , account , ref , amount , date , status , is , and has .

When you filter the list to a single account , payee , or category , an info panel appears beside the chart summarizing it: Account -- the current balance, type, account number, currency, credit limit or interest rate, and the next scheduled payment; for loans and mortgages, the current payment, estimated payoff, and remaining interest. A caret beside the name switches to another account, and an icon opens the account's detail page Payee -- total spent, income, the number of transactions, the average amount, the last transaction, the default category, the next bill, the top categories, and a detected recurring pattern Category -- the total, this month's budget, the monthly average, subcategories, top payees, and the next scheduled transaction Each panel can be edited from its pencil icon, and collapsed so the chart uses the full width.

Your filter selections are saved in your browser's local storage, so they persist between sessions. When navigating from a report, the dashboard, or another page, the link's filters are applied via URL parameters and override your saved filters temporarily.

Above the list, a chart summarizes the transactions currently in view. Which chart you get depends on your filters, and Hide chart folds it to a thin strip (you can start with it folded under Settings -> Preferences -> Default Views ).

With more than one account in view and no payee, category, tag, or search filter, a bar chart shows the current balance of each account, with the average and total. The Auto , Linear , and Log buttons set the scale, and clicking a bar filters the list to that account. The chart can be downloaded as a PNG.

When you filter by payee, category, tag, or search, a bar chart of the income and expense totals of the matching transactions. It rolls up to an adaptive Month / Quarter / Year granularity (auto-selected by the span in view, with a manual toggle) and gap-fills empty periods , so bars are spaced by real elapsed time rather than one equal-width bar per active period. Click a bar to narrow the list to that period. Averages are computed over elapsed periods.

With a single account in view, a running-balance chart for it. When no start-date filter is set, it spans the account's entire history ; the axis switches between month and year labels as the span grows, and an all-zero (e.g. closed) account shows a banner instead. For liability accounts (credit cards, loans, mortgages, lines of credit) a negative balance is normal, so the chart uses a neutral Min Balance label instead of flagging the low point as a warning. When you filter by a tag key , a Spending by chart breaks the spending down by the key's values.
A split transaction distributes a single payment across multiple categories. For example, a supermarket purchase might be split between "Groceries" and "Household Supplies."

In the transaction form, click Split Enter the Total Amount In Split Details , give each row a type ( Category , Transfer to another account, or Investment ), its category or account, an amount, an optional memo, and optional tags Click Add Split for more rows; a split needs at least two The split amounts must total the transaction amount. The footer shows what remains; Distribute Evenly and Distribute Proportionally spread the remainder for you, and a row's button adds the remainder to that row Click Create Transaction Removing the second-to-last row turns the transaction back into a regular one. Split transactions show their categories in the category column of the transaction list. Click on the transaction to see the full breakdown.
Transfers move money between your accounts (e.g., from chequing to savings).

In the transaction form, click Transfer Choose the From Account and the To Account Enter the Transfer Amount (always positive) Optionally choose a Payee and a Category (see the note below) Click Create Transfer Monize creates two linked transactions -- one in each account. The source account shows a withdrawal and the destination shows a deposit. Editing or deleting either side changes both. You can also turn an existing transaction into a transfer, or a transfer back into a transaction, by switching its mode in the edit form and clicking Convert to Transfer (or Convert to Transaction ). Note A transfer is never counted as income or an expense. Assigning it a category is optional and does not change that -- but a categorised transfer does appear in the monthly category breakdown, which is handy for tracking things like recurring investment contributions. Accounts other people share with you as joint accounts can be a transfer's destination too.

If the source and destination accounts are in different currencies, the form asks for the Amount Received in the destination's currency as well, filled in from the current exchange rate. Both amounts are recorded, so the effective rate is the one your bank actually used. See Currency Management for details.

Click on any transaction in the list to open it in the Edit Transaction form. Modify any field and click Update Transaction . Note Monize warns you before you edit or delete a reconciled transaction , so a carefully balanced statement does not drift by accident. You can still proceed after confirming, unless Lock reconciled transactions is turned on in Settings -> Preferences .

Set a transaction's status to Void to cancel it while keeping the record. A void transaction keeps its amount but no longer moves the account balance, and it is shown struck through. Voiding one side of a transfer voids both. To bring it back, edit the transaction and choose another status.

Click Delete on the row to permanently remove a transaction. The account balance is adjusted accordingly. You can undo a deletion right away (see Undo and Redo ). Caution If the transaction is part of a linked transfer, deleting it also deletes the linked transaction in the other account.
Bulk Update allows you to modify multiple transactions at once, such as changing the category, payee, or status for a batch of transactions.

Open the Filters panel on the Transactions page Click the Bulk Update button (beside the Show Accounts controls on desktop, or at the bottom of the filter panel on a phone) Checkboxes will appear next to each transaction in the list

Click the checkbox next to individual transactions to select them Use the select all checkbox in the table header to select all transactions on the current page If all transactions on the page are selected, a banner will offer to Select all N matching transactions across all pages (useful when filters are applied)

After selecting transactions, click Bulk Update in the selection banner In the Bulk Update Transactions dialog, toggle on the fields you want to change: Payee -- Change the payee for all selected transactions Category -- Assign a new category; on split transactions the new category is applied to their split lines Description -- Replace the description (leave it empty to clear it) Status -- Set the status to Pending (unreconciled), Cleared, or Void Tags -- Replace the tags (leave it empty to clear them) Only the fields you toggle on are updated; other fields are left unchanged Click Update N Transactions to save the changes Transfers have their linked counterpart updated as well.
Click Cancel Bulk in the filter panel to exit without making changes Completing a bulk update automatically exits bulk mode Clicking Clear selection in the selection banner also exits bulk mode
You can delete multiple transactions at once using the same selection mechanism as Bulk Update.

Enter bulk mode using the Bulk Update button in the filter panel Select transactions using checkboxes (individual, page-level, or all matching) Click Delete in the selection banner Confirm the deletion in the dialog
Mode Description By selection Deletes the specific transactions you selected by checkbox By filter Deletes all transactions matching the current filter criteria (when "select all matching" is used)

Deletion is permanent Linked transfer counterparts are automatically deleted along with the selected transaction Account balances are recalculated after deletion A confirmation dialog shows the count of transactions to be deleted before proceeding

Each transaction has a reconciliation status: Status Shown as Description Unreconciled Pending (○ when dense) New transaction, not yet verified against a statement Cleared Cleared (C) Verified to match a bank statement entry Reconciled Reconciled (R) Confirmed by a completed reconciliation Void VOID (V) Cancelled; the record is kept but no longer moves the balance The status flow is typically: Unreconciled -> Cleared -> Reconciled Click the status in the list to cycle it, or set it in the transaction form or during the account reconciliation process. A void transaction can only be changed in the form. See Account Reconciliation for details.
The Copy dropdown on each transaction row provides two actions:
Opens a copy of the transaction with the same account, payee, amount, category, tags, and description in the Duplicate Transaction form, so you can adjust any fields (such as the date) before saving.

Converts a transaction into a recurring scheduled transaction. The scheduled transaction form opens pre-filled with the transaction's details. Set the frequency, next due date, and other scheduling options, then click Create . The original transaction is not modified in either case. For more on scheduled transactions, see Bills and Deposits .

Monize tracks your recent actions and lets you undo and redo them using keyboard shortcuts: Shortcut Action Ctrl+Z (or Cmd+Z on Mac) Undo the last action Ctrl+Shift+Z (or Cmd+Shift+Z on Mac) Redo the last undone action Ctrl+Y (or Cmd+Y on Mac) Redo (alternative shortcut) Undo and redo work across all data pages -- transactions, accounts, categories, payees, tags, securities, budgets, scheduled transactions, and custom reports. A toast notification confirms each undo or redo operation. The Action History button (the clock icon in the header) lists your recent actions, with Undo and Redo buttons. Note These shortcuts are disabled when focus is inside a text input field, so they do not interfere with normal text editing.

Monize includes a full-featured budget planner that analyzes your spending history to suggest realistic budgets, tracks spending in real time with velocity projections, supports rollover per category, groups categories into flexible spending pools, and alerts you before you overspend.

Navigate to Budgets from the top navigation bar. The Budgets page lists every budget you have created with its Name , Strategy , Type , number of Categories , the date it Started , and its Status (Active or Inactive). Click a row to open that budget's dashboard, or click + New Budget to start the budget wizard. If you have no budgets yet, the page offers Create Your First Budget instead. The budget system integrates with your transactions, scheduled bills, and categories to give you a complete picture of your financial plan.

Monize includes a Budget Wizard that analyzes your historical spending to suggest realistic targets -- no manual data entry required. The wizard walks you through four steps, shown along the top as Analyze , Categories , Configure , and Review . Use Back at any step to return to the previous one.

Choose a Budget Strategy -- Select one of four strategies (see Budget Strategies below). Selecting a card opens a detail panel with its Pros , Cons , and who it is Best for . Analysis Period -- Choose 3 months , 6 months (the default), or 12 months of transaction history to analyze. Longer periods smooth out anomalies; shorter periods reflect recent habits. Budget Profile -- Pick how aggressive your targets should be: Profile Description Comfortable Based on your 75th percentile spending -- allows headroom On Track (default) Based on your median spending -- realistic targets Aggressive Based on your 25th percentile -- a stretch goal to save more Click Analyze My Spending to generate suggestions. The analysis looks at how each category's spending is distributed month by month, spots fixed expenses (rent, subscriptions) as opposed to variable spending (dining, groceries), and estimates your monthly income.

This step lists every category found in your history, in three tables: Income -- your income categories Expenses -- your spending categories, largest first. Categories with a regular, unchanging amount carry a Fixed badge Transfers / Savings -- regular transfers to savings accounts and loan or card payments Each row has: Column Description (checkbox) Include or leave out the category. Expense categories with no suggested amount start unticked Category The category (or transfer account) name Trend / Median A small sparkline of recent months, with your median monthly amount Amount The suggested budget amount -- edit it to your preference Use the profile buttons ( Comfortable , On Track , Aggressive ) at the top to switch the suggested amounts for all categories at once. The totals at the bottom show Total Income , Total Expenses , Transfers , and Remaining . For 50/30/20 budgets, each expense row also has a Need / Want / Saving picker, and a 50/30/20 Allocation box compares what you have assigned to each group against its target. Only categories found in your history are listed here. To budget for a category you have never used, create the budget first and add it later. Click Next: Configure to continue.

Configure your budget settings, grouped into sections: Section Settings Budget Details Budget Name (defaults to " Month Year Budget"), Budget Type (Monthly, Annual, or Pay Period), and Start Date . The strategy you chose in step 1 is shown here for reference Income Link budget to income -- category amounts become percentages of your base income (see Income-Linked Budgets ) -- and Base Monthly Income , prefilled with the income estimated by the analysis Rollover Rules Default Rollover Type for every category: None, Monthly, Quarterly, or Annual. It defaults to Monthly for the Rollover strategy and None otherwise. You can change individual categories after the budget is created Alert Thresholds Warning at (%) (default 80) and Critical at (%) (default 95) Flex Groups Click Configure to give expense categories a flex group name (for example "Fun Money") -- see Flex Groups Excluded Accounts Accounts whose transactions should not count toward the budget (for example an investment or business account) Click Next: Review to continue.

The review step shows a complete summary of your budget before it is created: Summary cards -- Est. Income , Total Expenses , Transfers , and Remaining Budget details -- Name , Type , Strategy , Start Date , Rollover , Alerts , Income Linked , and Excluded Accounts Category table -- every included category with its amount and type (Income, Expense, or Transfer) On mobile, the Type column is hidden to give category names and amounts more room. Click Create Budget to finish. The new budget appears on the Budgets page.

Click a budget on the Budgets page to open its dashboard, your main view for tracking the budget in real time. A Back to Budgets link returns to the list, and the arrow beside the budget's name ( Switch to another budget ) jumps straight to another budget. Under the name, a bar describes the budget's strategy. The Edit and Delete buttons are at the top right.

Four cards at the top provide an at-a-glance overview: Card Description Total Budget Your total budgeted spending for the period Spent Total spending so far, with the percentage of the budget used Remaining Budget remaining, with the number of days left in the period (or Period ended ) Savings Income received so far minus spending, marked On track or Over budget

A circular gauge from 0 to 100 summarizing how well you are sticking to your budget. Score Range Label 90--100 Excellent 70--89 Good 50--69 Needs Attention Below 50 Off Track The score starts at 100 and: loses points for every category over budget, more the further over it is loses a few points for every category above 95% of its budget gains a point for every category below half of its budget loses points when total spending is over the whole budget The Budget Health Score report gives a more detailed version that weights essential (Needs) categories more heavily.

Shows your spending pace and whether you will finish the period within budget: Daily burn rate -- How much you are spending per day Safe to spend -- How much you can spend per day and stay on track Projected month-end -- Where you will land at the current pace Pace status -- Under budget pace (green), On track (yellow), or Over budget pace (red) Budget total , Bills coming and Truly available -- your budget less the scheduled bills still to come this period A progress bar showing Day X of Y and the days remaining Because the widget factors in upcoming bills from your scheduled transactions, "safe to spend" reflects your truly available discretionary budget.

The Category Budgets list shows every expense category in the budget with a progress bar. Each row shows: Category name -- including its parent category, for example "Food: Groceries" Progress bar -- Colour-coded by percentage used (green, yellow, red), with a marker showing where you should be today ("Expected pace") Amount spent of the budgeted amount , and the percentage used Pace status -- Under pace , On pace , or Over pace compared with how far through the period you are Amount left , or how much you are over Use the Sort dropdown to sort by % Used (the default), Spent , Remaining , or Name , and the arrow beside it to reverse the order. On mobile, the sort controls stack below the heading. Click a category row to open the Transactions page filtered to that category and the budget period.

Two widgets appear above the health score for specific strategies: Zero-Based Assignment (Zero-Based budgets) -- how much of your income is assigned ( Assigned: x / y ), marked Fully assigned , Under-assigned , or Over-assigned 50/30/20 Allocation (50/30/20 budgets) -- for Needs , Wants , and Savings , the target percentage against the percentage and amount actually budgeted

A flex group pools several related categories under one shared limit -- for example, "Fun Money" for Restaurants, Movies, and Hobbies. Individual categories within a group can go over budget, but as long as the group total is within its limit, you have stayed on plan. You assign categories to flex groups in step 3 of the wizard ( Flex Groups > Configure ), or later from the budget's edit page ( Flex Group (optional) in a category's settings). When at least one group exists, a Flex Groups card on the dashboard shows each group's combined spending against its combined budget.

Integrates with your scheduled transactions to show: Bills coming due this period with dates and amounts Total upcoming -- the sum of those bills Truly available -- remaining budget minus upcoming bills This prevents a false sense of security when you have budget left but bills still to pay. When nothing is due, the card says "No bills due this period."

A calendar for the current month in which each day is shaded by how much you spent, from Less to More . Darker days are your heavier spending days, which helps you spot patterns such as weekend spending. Hover over or tap a day to see its total.
A chart of your Budgeted amount against your Actual spending over recent periods, so you can see whether you are improving over time. It needs at least a couple of periods of history.

The What-If Scenario Planner at the bottom of the dashboard lets you try budget changes without committing them. Drag a category's slider to change its amount and the planner immediately shows the Current Budget , the Proposed Budget , the Projected Savings , and the Savings Change . Each changed category shows its Original amount. Nothing is saved: click Reset to put every slider back, or leave the page. To make a change permanent, edit the budget (see Editing a Budget ).

Monize supports four budget strategies, each suited to a different financial style: Strategy Description Fixed Set fixed amounts per category. Simple and predictable. Unused budget resets at the end of each period. Rollover Unused budget carries forward to the next period based on per-category rollover rules. Good for saving toward irregular expenses. Zero-Based Every dollar of income is assigned a purpose: income minus all budgeted amounts should equal zero. The dashboard shows how much is still unassigned. 50/30/20 Categories are grouped as Needs (50%), Wants (30%), or Savings (20%) of your income. The wizard and dashboard compare each group with its target. You can change a budget's strategy later from its edit page.

Each category can have its own rollover setting: Rollover Type Description None The budget resets each period -- no carry-forward Monthly Unused budget rolls forward into the next period Quarterly Unused budget rolls forward, intended for quarterly saving Annual Unused budget rolls forward, intended for saving across the year Whichever rolling type you choose, the unused amount carries into the next period when the current one closes. Overspending is not carried forward as a debt. You can also set a Rollover Cap to limit how much accumulates. For example, a clothing category might roll over monthly with a $500 cap. Common patterns: Groceries -- None (no point accumulating) Clothing -- Monthly with a cap (save for seasonal shopping) Travel -- Annual (vacation fund) Car Maintenance -- Annual with no cap (save for repairs)

For freelancers, gig workers, or anyone with variable income, you can tick Link budget to income in step 3 of the wizard. Category amounts then become percentages of your base income rather than fixed dollar amounts: If your income drops, your budget automatically tightens If your income rises, your budget grows proportionally Set a Base Monthly Income to establish the baseline. The wizard suggests it from your historical income. An income-linked budget also raises an Income Shortfall alert when actual income falls well below the base (see Alerts ).
Monize checks every active budget once a day and raises alerts before you overspend. Alerts appear under the notifications bell in the header, and the most serious ones can also be emailed to you.

Alert Type Trigger Severity Threshold Warning A category's spending reaches its warning threshold (default 80%) Warning Threshold Critical A category's spending reaches its critical threshold (default 95%) Warning Over Budget A category's spending exceeds 100% Critical Projected Overspend At the current pace, a category that is still under budget is projected to finish more than 10% over (checked from the third day of the period) Warning Flex Group Warning A flex group's total reaches 90% of its combined budget Warning Income Shortfall On an income-linked budget, at least halfway through the period, actual income is below 80% of the base income Critical Positive Milestone At least halfway through the period and under 60% of the budget spent Good news Seasonal Spike Your history shows next month is usually much more expensive for a category, so you can plan ahead Info Bill Due A scheduled bill that you pay by hand (not posted automatically) is coming due within its reminder window Info Each alert is raised once per period, so you are not reminded of the same overspend every day.

The bell icon ( Notifications ) in the top navigation bar shows the number of unread notifications. Click it to open the notifications panel. The panel lists budget alerts alongside Monize's other notifications: Severity filters -- chips for Critical , Warning , Good News , and Info (red, yellow, green, and blue badges), plus Financial and System to narrow the list Alert title and message -- What happened and the details Unread indicator -- A dot on unread alerts Mark all read -- Clears every unread indicator at once Delete all -- Removes every notification (or every one matching the current filter), after a confirmation Remind me about this -- Brings a notification back later, once or repeatedly until you stop it Dismiss -- An X button on each alert (see below) Clicking an alert takes you to the relevant budget. Bill due alerts open the Bills & Deposits page instead.

Each alert in the panel has an X button that appears on hover. Clicking it: Immediately removes the alert from the list Shows a toast notification with an Undo button for 5 seconds If you don't undo, the alert is permanently deleted after 5 seconds If you click Undo , the alert is restored to the list

Budget emails are set up in Settings > Notifications , under Budget Notifications . Email must be enabled for your account and your administrator must have configured email for the instance. Email Type Description Immediate alerts Critical budget alerts (over budget, income shortfall) are sent as soon as they are raised, regardless of digest settings Weekly Budget Digest A weekly summary of your budget alerts and status. Turn it on with the Weekly Budget Digest switch; the Digest day setting chooses the day Monthly summary Sent when a period closes, with total budget against actual spending, savings achieved, and the health score The Budgets row of the "How to notify me" grid in the same section controls whether budget reports and alerts are emailed at all.

Budgets are divided into periods (monthly for a monthly budget). Shortly after midnight on the 1st of each month, Monize automatically: Closes the current period Records the actual spending for each category Calculates rollover amounts per category Opens the next period, carrying the rollover balances forward

Once a budget has more than one period, a Period: selector appears at the top of the dashboard. Choose Current Period , or any past period by month. A closed period shows: Total Budgeted , Total Spent , and whether you finished Under Budget or Over Budget , plus Income A Rollover Summary of the amounts carried in and carried out Overall Budget Usage The final actual amount for every category, under Expense Categories and Income Categories

Nine budget-specific reports are available in the Budget category of the Reports page: Report Description Budget vs Actual Compare your budgeted amounts to actual spending over time across all categories Budget Health Score Get a 0--100 health score for your budget with detailed per-category impact analysis Seasonal Spending Patterns Discover seasonal trends and high-spending months across your budget categories Budget Trend Line chart showing total budgeted vs total actual spending over 6--12 months to track improvement Category Performance Table showing each category's budget performance over multiple months with trend indicators Savings Rate Track your savings rate (income minus expenses divided by income) over time vs your target Health Score History Line chart of monthly budget health scores showing your financial trajectory over time Flex Group Analysis Stacked bar chart for each flex group showing component categories with group limit reference Seasonal Spending Map Heatmap grid showing 12 months across all categories to identify seasonal spending patterns Additionally, a Budget Variance metric is available in the custom report builder , so you can create your own budget-related reports with flexible filters and groupings.

To edit an existing budget: Open the budget dashboard Click Edit in the top right Change the Budget Settings : Budget Name , Description (optional) , Budget Type , Strategy , Base Income (optional) , and Active Click Save Changes Below the settings, Category Allocations lists the budget's Income and Expenses categories with their amounts and rollover settings. Click a category to open its settings: Field Description Budget Amount The amount budgeted for the category each period Rollover Type None, Monthly, Quarterly, or Annual (see Rollover Rules ) Rollover Cap (optional) The most that can accumulate; shown when the category rolls over Flex Group (optional) The flex group this category belongs to Category Group (50/30/20) Need, Want, or Saving Warning at (%) / Critical at (%) This category's own alert thresholds Notes (optional) Your own notes about the category budget Click Save to keep the changes, or Remove from budget to take the category out of the budget. Removing a category also deletes its history in past budget periods (your transactions are not affected), so Monize asks you to confirm. Unticking Active stops the daily alert checks for the budget without deleting it.

Click Delete on the budget dashboard and confirm. Deleting a budget removes all of its data, including its periods and alerts; your transactions and categories are not affected. This cannot be undone.
Monize provides comprehensive investment portfolio tracking with automatic price updates, cost basis calculation, return measurement, and performance reporting.

Navigate to Investments from the top navigation bar. The Investments page gives you a complete picture of your portfolio: current market values, gains and losses, returns, allocation, value over time, and every investment transaction. At the top of the page: All Investment Accounts -- a multi-select list of your investment accounts. Tick one or more accounts to show only those; every card on the page then names the selection in its title Refresh -- fetches the latest prices for your securities (see Price Updates ). Hover over it to see when prices were last updated + New Transaction -- choose Investment Transaction (a buy, sell, dividend and so on) or Cash Transaction (a deposit, withdrawal or fee in the account's cash) Tip: You can open the Investments page already filtered to one account by clicking a brokerage account on the Accounts page or a brokerage favourite on the Dashboard .

Investment accounts in Monize are composed of two linked accounts: Component Purpose Brokerage Account Holds your securities (stocks, ETFs, mutual funds, bonds) Cash Account Tracks the cash balance within the brokerage When you create an investment account, both components are created automatically. The cash account is hidden from the main Accounts list but is managed through the Investments page.

Buying securities decreases the cash balance and adds to holdings Selling securities increases the cash balance and reduces holdings Dividends increase the cash balance Transfers move cash in or out of the investment account Microsoft Money users: In Microsoft Money, the cash and securities are combined in a single investment account. Monize separates these for cleaner transaction tracking, but the import process handles this mapping automatically.

The Portfolio Summary card shows the Total Portfolio Value (holdings plus cash), then two groups of figures. Hover over any figure for an explanation of how it is worked out. Group Figure Description Values Holdings Value The current market value of all the securities you hold Cash Balance Uninvested cash sitting in your investment accounts Total Gain Portfolio value minus net invested: realized and unrealized gains, dividends, and interest Net Invested Your own money deposited, less withdrawals Cost Basis What your current holdings cost, including purchase commissions Gain/Loss Unrealized gain or loss: market value minus cost basis Returns Simple Return (Market value - cost basis) / cost basis TWR (Time-Weighted) The return of your investments, unaffected by when you deposited or withdrew money MWR (Money-Weighted) The annual rate your own money earned, weighting each purchase, sale and dividend by when it happened CAGR Your annualized growth rate based on net invested against the current value When a holding has no current price, or an exchange rate is missing, the card says the figures are incomplete, names what is missing, and shows Portfolio Value (partial) instead of a total.

The Asset Allocation donut chart has a grouping toggle: Grouping When available By security Always By tag Only when your holdings are tagged By key Only when your holdings carry key:value tags By country Only when country allocation data exists By asset class Only when asset-class data exists (equities, fixed income, cash, and so on) Each view shows the top 10 slices plus an Other band that groups the remaining smaller holdings. Allocation percentages always reconcile against the drawn slices, so the legend and the chart agree exactly. By key charts your portfolio's value-weighted split across the values of a chosen tag key (for example, splitting by a country or strategy key). By country performs a geographic look-through : rather than grouping by an ETF's listing exchange, it looks through your funds to their underlying holdings and reports true country-level exposure -- the top 10 countries individually, with the rest collapsed into an Other Countries band. By asset class splits funds into their stock, bond and cash components, with the rest collapsed into an Other Asset Classes band. A security's country and asset-class split come from its price provider where available, or from the Geographical Allocation and Asset Allocation sections of the security's form.

The Portfolio Value Over Time chart plots the value of your investments with a range selector: 1D , 1W , MTD , 1M , 3M , YTD , 1Y , 2Y , 5Y , and All Time . The 1D and 1W ranges use intraday prices where the price provider supplies them. Hover over the chart to read the value on any day. Under the range buttons, the chart reports for the selected window: Highest Value and Lowest Value Value Change -- the value at the end of the window less the value at the start Investment Result and Return -- what your investments earned over the window, leaving out deposits, withdrawals and uninvested cash, so buying and selling do not move it A View report link opens the full Portfolio Value Over Time report for a richer breakdown.

Beside the chart, the Portfolio performance card lists how your investments did over standard periods -- 1D , 1W , 1M , 3M , YTD , 1Y , 2Y , 5Y , 10Y , and All time -- each with the amount gained or lost and a time-weighted return. Deposits, withdrawals and uninvested cash are left out, so the figures measure your investments rather than your saving. Periods longer than your history are not shown.

The Holdings by Account card lists your positions grouped by account. Each account's row shows its total market value and gain; click it to expand the positions. Each holding displays: Column Description Symbol The security's symbol and name. Click it to open the security's detail page Shares Number of shares or units held Avg Cost Your average cost per share Price Latest market price Cost Basis What you paid for the holding Mkt Value Current total value (shares x price) Gain/Loss Difference from cost basis, in money and as a percentage % Port The holding's share of the portfolio Each account also has a Cash row with its Available Balance (click it to see the cash account's transactions) and an Account Total . Gains are shown in green and losses in red. Click a column heading to sort by it, and use Columns to choose which columns to show. Holdings in a foreign currency show their value in that currency and, converted, in your home currency.

If Monize finds a share transfer that was entered twice -- once as a Transfer Out in one account and once as a Transfer In in another -- a Transfers recorded as two separate rows card lists each pair with a Link button. Until the two rows are linked, the receiving account cannot inherit the cost basis, so its gain reads as unknown.

The Recent Transactions section at the bottom of the page is the investment register. Two toggles control it: Brokerage / Cash -- the security transactions, or the transactions in the investment accounts' cash Table / Calendar -- a list, or a month calendar (see below) In the table, the Filter button filters by Symbol , Action , and date range ( From / To ); the Cash register filters by Payees , Categories , and dates. Each row shows its date, account, action, symbol, shares, price, total, and reconciliation status, with Edit and Delete buttons. + New Brokerage Transaction (or + New Cash Transaction ) adds a transaction.

Switch to Calendar to see the month as a calendar. The Layers buttons choose what each day shows: Transactions -- the investment transactions on that day Values -- the portfolio's value at the end of the day Daily change -- how much the portfolio moved that day, as a percentage Use the arrows and Today to move between months, or click the month to jump to another one. Notes you have added to days (from any calendar in Monize) appear as banners across their days. Click a day to add a note to it, or to start a new investment transaction on that date. Click a day's percentage to open What moved on that date: the Market movement for the day, then the securities that rose ( Gains ) and fell ( Losses ), each with its shares and its price before and after. Cash, distributions and trades are reported separately, so a deposit is not mistaken for a gain. For the biggest daily moves across your holdings at a glance, add the Top Movers widget to your dashboard.

Action Description Cash Impact Buy Purchase securities Cash decreases Sell Sell securities Cash increases Dividend Cash dividend received Cash increases Interest Interest income received Cash increases Capital Gain A capital gain distribution Cash increases Short-Term Capital Gain / Long-Term Capital Gain A capital gain distribution, by holding period Cash increases Return of Capital A distribution that returns part of your investment; it lowers your cost basis Cash increases Reinvest Dividend Dividend reinvested as additional shares No cash change Reinvest Interest Interest reinvested as additional shares No cash change Reinvest Short-Term Cap Gain / Reinvest Long-Term Cap Gain A capital gain distribution reinvested as additional shares No cash change Stock Split Changes the number of shares (for example 2 new shares for every 1 old) No cash change Add Shares / Remove Shares Add or remove shares without a purchase or sale (for example a gift or a correction) No cash change Redeem CD/Bond A bond or certificate of deposit paying back its principal, with any accrued interest Cash increases Transfer Move shares to another investment account, keeping their cost basis. The register shows the two sides as Transfer Out and Transfer In No cash change

Navigate to Investments Click + New Transaction and choose Investment Transaction (or use + New Brokerage Transaction in the register) Pick the Brokerage Account and the Transaction Type Fill in the details and click Create Transaction

Field Description Brokerage Account The investment account (for a transfer, From Account and To Account ) Date Transaction date Transaction Type Buy, Sell, Dividend, and so on (see above) Funds From (optional) / Funds To (optional) For a buy or sell, the account the money comes from or goes to. The linked cash account is the default Security The security involved. + Add new security creates one without leaving the form Quantity (Shares) Number of shares or units Price per Share Price per share or unit Commission / Fees Any trading commission or fee Description (optional) Optional notes Status Unreconciled, Cleared, Reconciled, or Void. A void transaction stays in the register but moves no shares and no cash Total Amount The total, calculated from quantity, price and commission; you can also type the total and Monize works out the price Some types ask for different fields: a dividend, interest or distribution asks for an Amount ; a stock split asks for New shares and Old shares ; a transfer asks for the Cost per Share ; a bond redemption asks for Accrued Interest . When the security trades in a different currency from the account, the form adds an Exchange rate and a Converted Total . Use the arrow beside Create Transaction to choose Create Transaction & New , which saves and clears the form for the next entry. To change a transaction, click Edit on its row (the form then has Update Transaction ).
Securities represent the stocks, ETFs, mutual funds, bonds, and other instruments you hold.

Navigate to Tools > Securities to manage your list of securities. The page shows the Total Securities , Types , Exchanges , and Currencies you hold, a search box, and an All / Active / Inactive filter. Each row shows the security's Symbol , Name , Type , Shares held and their Value , Exchange , Currency , price Provider , the Source of the latest price, and its Status . Click the star to make a security a favourite, or click a row to open the security's detail page .

Click + New Security , or Edit on a security's row, to open the security form. Type a symbol or name and click Lookup to fill in the details from the price provider. Field Description Symbol Ticker symbol (e.g., AAPL, VGRO.TO) Name Full name (e.g., Apple Inc.) Type Stock, ETF, Mutual Fund, Bond, Option, Cryptocurrency, or Other Exchange Stock exchange (NYSE, NASDAQ, TSX, etc.), filled in from the ticker Currency The currency the security trades in Quote Provider Where prices come from: Auto, Yahoo, MSN, LSE, Deutsche Börse, or the bond engine. Leave it on the default to use the instance's default provider Disable automatic price updates Stop fetching prices for a security no provider can price; you then enter its prices yourself Description Free-text notes, filled in from the provider's profile during lookup Website / Investor relations website Links shown on the detail page Tags Tags that drive the by-tag and by-key allocation views Geographical Allocation / Asset Allocation The fund's country and asset-class split, as percentages, where the provider does not supply it Price change alert (%) Notify you when the price rises or falls by at least this percentage from one session to the next (leave blank to turn off). Include a chart in price alerts adds a price chart to the alert Favourite Show the security first in lists Bonds also have a Bond kind and Country , which link the security to a supported government bond programme so Monize can work out its value.
Securities can be added: Manually from the Securities page From the investment transaction form ( + Add new security ) During import (mapped or auto-created from your Microsoft Money or QIF data)

A security you no longer hold can be Deactivated from its row: it disappears from the Active list but keeps its history. A security that is not used by any holding or investment transaction can be Deleted , which also deletes its price history. A security that is still referenced cannot be deleted until those transactions are removed.

When looking up securities, Monize searches its price providers and ranks results by exchange. If you primarily invest on non-US exchanges, you can set Preferred Exchanges in Settings to prioritize results from your exchanges. See Settings > Preferred Exchanges for details.

Click a security on the Securities page, or its symbol in the holdings list, to open its detail page. The header shows the latest price with the day's change ("today", or "last move" when the market has not traded today), whether the market is open, and the buttons Favourites , Edit , and Refresh . The arrow beside the name switches to another security. Below the header: Position cards -- Market value , Cost basis , Unrealized P/L , Units with the Avg. cost / unit , and the accounts the security is Held in Price chart -- switch between Price , Investment value (what your position was worth), and Return , over 1M to All Time Key information -- symbol, type, exchange, currency, provider, and last price Breakdown -- the fund's weighting by Sector , Country , and Asset class The tabs below hold the rest: Tab What it shows Overview About (the description, sector, industry, country, website, and tags), Security performance over standard periods, Position info (first and last transaction, total invested and sold, dividends, fees, realized P/L, total return), and the Accounts holding it Transactions Every transaction in this security, with + Add transaction and Adjust shares Price history Every stored price, by year and month, with the tools to manage them (see below) Documents Links to the security's paperwork: factsheet, KIID, prospectus, annual reports, tax documents, research News Recent news about the security from the price provider
Security prices are updated automatically and can also be refreshed manually.

Schedule: Weekdays (Monday-Friday) at 5:00 PM New York time Source: Each security's quote provider -- Yahoo Finance by default, or MSN, the London Stock Exchange, Deutsche Börse, or the bond engine Data: Daily prices (close, plus open, high, low and volume where the provider supplies them)
Click Refresh on the Investments page, the Securities page, a security's detail page, or the Dashboard to fetch the latest prices immediately.

You can add, edit, and delete individual price entries for any security. This is useful for: Securities no provider can price (e.g., private funds, GICs) Correcting incorrect price data Adding NAV prices for mutual funds To manage prices: Open the security's detail page and its Price history tab Click + Add Price and enter the Date and Close Price (and optionally the open, high, low, and volume) Use Edit or Delete on any row to correct or remove a price Each price shows its Source -- the provider, a manual entry, or a transaction. Manual prices take priority over provider prices for the same date. If you delete a manual price and investment transactions exist on that date, Monize backfills the price from the transaction's buy or sell price. The Price history tab also has Force Update Prices , which re-fetches the whole period you have held the security, and Add Another Year of History , which fetches one more year of older prices.

Monize can populate security prices from your investment transaction history. When you buy or sell a security at a specific price, that price can be used to fill gaps in the price history. This is especially useful for securities with automatic price updates disabled, or securities no provider can price. Transaction-based prices are created automatically during import. For existing data, an administrator can trigger a backfill from the browser console (see Issues below).

When you add a new security, Monize fetches its last year of prices so that historical valuations and charts are accurate. Use Add Another Year of History on the security's Price history tab to go further back.
Monize tracks your cost basis using the average cost method .

When you buy shares, the total cost (including commission) is added to your cost basis The average cost per share is: total cost basis / total shares held When you sell shares, the cost basis for the sold shares is calculated using the average cost Reinvested dividends add to both quantity and cost basis A return of capital lowers the cost basis
Transaction Shares Price Total Cost Total Shares Avg Cost Buy 100 100 $10 $1,000 100 $10.00 Buy 50 50 $12 $1,600 150 $10.67 Sell 75 -75 $15 $800 75 $10.67

When all shares of a security are sold, the holding is removed from your portfolio; its detail page shows the position as closed with its realized P/L. If you buy the same security again, a new cost basis starts from that purchase.

Monize includes 13 dedicated investment reports. Navigate to Reports and choose the Investment category to see them. Report Description Investment Performance Portfolio returns, gains/losses, and asset allocation Gains, Dividends & Interest Realized and unrealized capital gains plus dividend and interest income, with monthly breakdowns Sector Weightings Portfolio sector exposure from stocks and ETFs Realized Gains & Losses Tax planning with proceeds and cost basis analysis Portfolio Value Over Time Historical portfolio value trends and period returns Investment Transaction History Complete transaction log with action-type filtering Security Type Allocation Allocation by asset type (stocks, ETFs, bonds, etc.) Geographic/Exchange Allocation Geographic exposure by exchange and region Dividend Yield & Growth Yield tracking, per-security yields, and growth analysis Security Performance A single security's price chart and trades, or several securities and market indexes compared on one chart Currency Exposure Currency risk analysis across your portfolio Monte Carlo Simulation Project future portfolio outcomes with thousands of randomized return paths and a saved-scenario library GEM Strategy Track the Global Equities Momentum signal and whether your portfolio follows it You can also build your own holdings reports with the Investment Report builder. For full details, see Reports .
Importing investment data from Microsoft Money requires special handling. See the Importing from Microsoft Money guide for complete details.

The recommended method is to import the .mny file directly. Investment accounts, securities, buys, sells, dividends, reinvestments, share transfers, stock splits and price history all come across in one pass, and share counts are reconciled against Money's own open tax lots afterwards If you use the older QIF method instead, Microsoft Money exports investment accounts as two separate QIF files: "Investment" type for securities transactions and "Regular" type for cash transactions Import the investment brokerage file first, then the cash file With QIF, securities must be mapped to existing records or created during import Monize automatically creates the linked cash transactions when importing investment QIF files For the recommended QIF import order, see Recommended Import Order .

h: Backfilling historical security price info does not complete
x: You may encounter an issue where backfilling historical security price info doesn't work, possibly because of price provider rate limits. For a single security, open its Price history tab and click Force Update Prices . To re-load every security at once, press F12 to open the browser developer tools while logged in as a Monize administrator. Go to the console and run: fetch('/api/v1/securities/prices/backfill', { method: 'POST', headers: { 'x-csrf-token': decodeURIComponent(document.cookie.match(/csrf_token=([^;]+)/)?.[1]) } }).then(r => r.json()).then(console.log)

h: Backfilling historical price info from transaction info
x: Similarly, since version 1.5.8 Monize can use security transaction history to populate the security prices. This doesn't run on existing data automatically, but an administrator can trigger it from the browser console: fetch('/api/v1/securities/prices/backfill-transactions', { method: 'POST', headers: { 'x-csrf-token': decodeURIComponent(document.cookie.match(/csrf_token=([^;]+)/)?.[1]) } }).then(r => r.json()).then(console.log)
The Bills & Deposits feature lets you schedule recurring transactions so you never miss a payment or forget about regular income.

Bills & Deposits manages your recurring financial obligations and expected income. It shows a cash flow forecast built from your schedules, lists every scheduled transaction (or shows them on a month calendar), and can post transactions automatically on their due dates. The summary at the top counts your Active Bills and Active Deposits , the Monthly Net of all your active schedules converted to your home currency, and how many are Due Now (overdue or due today).

Navigate to Bills & Deposits from the top navigation bar Click + New Schedule Choose what you are scheduling with the buttons at the top: a Transaction , a Split across several categories, a Transfer between accounts, or an Investment transaction Fill in the form: Click Create

Field Required Description Name Yes What the schedule is called, for example Rent, Netflix, or Salary Account Yes Which account this transaction uses Next Due Date Yes When the next occurrence is due; later occurrences follow from it Payee No Who the transaction is with Category No Expense or income category Amount Yes Transaction amount (negative for a bill, positive for a deposit). Leave it at zero for a reminder of a bill whose amount varies. The currency button beside it lets you enter the amount in the currency the biller charges Reference Number No Cheque number, confirmation number, or another reference Frequency Yes How often the transaction recurs (default Monthly; see Frequency Options ) Remind Days Before No How many days before the due date the schedule counts as coming up, for reminders and the dashboard's Due soon list (default 3) Description No Additional notes End Condition No Stop the schedule End by date (an End Date ) or after a Number of occurrences Active No Turn off to pause the schedule without deleting it Auto-post on due date No Whether to create the transaction automatically on the due date (see Auto-Posting ) Tags No One or more tags applied when the transaction is posted

Like regular transactions, scheduled transactions support splits across multiple categories. Choose Split at the top of the form (or click Split Transaction ) to add multiple category/amount rows; the rows must add up to the Total Amount . Cancel Split returns to a single category.

You can schedule recurring transfers between accounts (e.g., a monthly transfer from chequing to savings). Choose Transfer , then the From Account , the To Account , and the Transfer Amount . You may optionally also assign a Category : the transfer is still not counted as income or expense, but it will appear in the monthly category breakdown (useful for tracking recurring investment contributions).

Choose Investment to schedule a recurring investment transaction, such as a monthly purchase of an ETF or a dividend reinvestment. Pick the Investment Account , the Action (Buy, Sell, Dividend, Reinvest Dividend, and so on), the Security , and the Quantity (Shares) , Price per Share , and Commission . The Funding Account defaults to the investment account's own cash; pick another account to model a contribution followed by a purchase. When the occurrence is posted, you can adjust the quantity, price, or total to what was actually traded.

Frequency Description One Time A single future transaction (useful for reminders) Daily Every day Weekly Once per week Every 2 Weeks Every two weeks Every 4 Weeks Every four weeks (useful for pay cycles that do not align to calendar months) Twice a Month Twice per month Monthly Once per month on the same date Every 2 Months Every two months Quarterly Every three months Every 4 Months Every four months Twice a Year Every six months Yearly Once per year Every 2 Years Every other year A monthly schedule on the 31st falls on the last day of shorter months.

Below the forecast, the list shows all scheduled transactions with: Column Description Name / Payee What the schedule is called and who it is with Account The account involved Category The category, the transfer's destination, or a Split badge Amount The amount of the next occurrence Schedule The next due date with an Overdue , Due Today , or Due Soon (within a week) badge, the frequency, and how many occurrences are left Auto-Post On when the schedule posts itself Actions Post Transaction , Skip Occurrence , Edit Occurrence , Edit Schedule , and Delete A modified badge counts the upcoming occurrences you have changed (see Overriding Individual Occurrences ), and paused schedules are marked inactive.

The All , Bills , and Deposits buttons narrow the list to one kind of schedule. Filters opens a panel to search by Name and narrow by Payees , Accounts , and Categories . The density button sets how much fits on screen.

The Table and Calendar buttons switch between the list and a month calendar of every occurrence. Move between months with the arrows, or return to the current one with Today . Click an occurrence to edit its schedule.

To record an occurrence yourself, click Post Transaction on its row. The Post Transaction dialog lets you change the Transaction Date , the Amount , the Category , the Description , and the Reference Number for this posting only, or split it with Split this transaction . It shows what the posting does to the account's balance, and warns you when posting on that date would take an account below zero or over its credit limit. Click Post Transaction to create the transaction and advance the schedule to its next due date. Clicking an item in the dashboard's Upcoming Bills widget opens the same dialog.
When Auto-post on due date is turned on for a scheduled transaction, Monize automatically creates the transaction on its due date without any manual intervention.

Every hour, Monize checks for active, auto-posting scheduled transactions that are due today or overdue in your timezone Each due occurrence is created in the designated account, with any changes you made to that occurrence The next due date is calculated based on the frequency When the end date or the number of occurrences is reached, the schedule ends A posting that fails (for example, for want of an exchange rate) raises a notification so you can post it by hand.
Fixed-amount bills (e.g., rent, subscription services) -- The amount is the same each time Regular transfers (e.g., monthly savings contribution) -- Predictable, consistent amounts

Variable-amount bills (e.g., utilities, credit card payments) -- Use reminders instead and enter the actual amount manually Bills your bank's import already brings in -- the imported row and the auto-posted one would both be recorded
You can modify or skip individual occurrences of a scheduled transaction without changing the overall schedule.

In the bills list, click Edit Occurrence on the scheduled transaction In Select Occurrence Date , choose which upcoming occurrence to change (occurrences you already changed are marked Modified ) In the Edit Occurrence dialog, change the Occurrence Date , Amount , Category , or Description for this occurrence only To split just this occurrence across multiple categories, turn on Split this occurrence and add category/amount rows (independent of whether the underlying schedule is split) Click Save Override (or Update Override for one you changed before) The override only affects that single occurrence. All other future occurrences follow the original schedule. Reset to Default removes the override. When you later edit a schedule that has overrides, Monize asks whether to Keep Modifications or Delete All Modifications .

If a recurring bill does not apply for a particular period (e.g., a holiday causes a payment to be skipped): Click Skip Occurrence on the scheduled transaction Confirm in the Skip Occurrence dialog The schedule advances to its next due date

The Cash Flow Forecast at the top of the page projects your account balances from today's balances, the transactions already dated in the future, and every scheduled occurrence. Choose how far ahead to look: 7D , 30D , 90D , 6M , or 1Y Accounts to forecast picks the accounts. With none picked, all your accounts are drawn as one line; with two or more, each account gets its own line beside a Total of Accounts line Hover over the chart to see the balance on a day and the transactions that move it Below the chart: the Starting and Ending balances and the lowest point of the period ( Min Balance for liability accounts) An occurrence that fell due and was neither posted nor skipped counts on the first day of the forecast. If an exchange rate is missing for one of the currencies involved, the forecast says so rather than showing a total that leaves it out. This helps you: Anticipate when account balances will be low Plan for upcoming large expenses Ensure sufficient funds for automatic payments The same forecast is available as a dashboard widget .
For loan and mortgage accounts, scheduled transactions track the regular payments.

The easiest way is to let Monize create the schedule: fill in the payment details when you create the loan or mortgage , or use Set Up Recurring Payments on an existing one. The schedule it creates splits each payment into a principal transfer to the loan account and an interest line booked to the loan's interest category, priced from the balance and the rate in effect on each due date. The calendar, the Upcoming Bills widget, and Edit Occurrence each show that occurrence's own payment and split. To set one up by hand, create a Split schedule from your bank account with a Transfer line to the loan account for the principal and a Category line for the interest. Tip If your bank's import brings in the payment, turn on payment matching on the loan instead of auto-posting: the imported row then settles the scheduled payment rather than being recorded twice. Note When importing from Microsoft Money, loan payment categories are automatically detected and mapped to the corresponding loan accounts. See Importing from Microsoft Money for details.

You can create a scheduled transaction from any existing transaction without re-entering its details. On the Transactions page, find the transaction you want to schedule Click the Copy dropdown on the transaction row and select Schedule as Recurring The scheduled transaction form opens pre-filled with the transaction's account, payee, amount, category, and tags Set the frequency, next due date, and other scheduling options Click Create The original transaction is not modified -- a new scheduled transaction is created based on its details. A credit card's detail page can also schedule a monthly payment with Make a Payment , and a bank account's detail page offers Create bill for recurring charges it finds in your transactions. See Account Detail Pages .

Monize reminds you of scheduled transactions as they come due, in the notification bell and, when you turn them on under Notifications , by email or push. A schedule's Remind Days Before sets how early. Reminder emails are colour-coded to help you quickly distinguish between expenses and income at a glance.

Tools > Taxes collects the tools for the deductions and taxes that shape your pay. Its first tool, Payroll Deductions , puts a yearly maximum on the deductions your paycheque takes, such as pension contributions and employment insurance premiums, so that your scheduled paycheque stops collecting a deduction once the year's maximum is reached and starts again when the year resets, and your cash flow forecast shows the larger paycheques that follow.

Open Tools > Taxes . Each tool is a card; click one to open it. Taxes is available to the account owner only: it is not in the Tools menu while you are acting for someone else through Shared Access . Tool What it does Payroll Deductions Yearly maximums on the deduction lines of your payroll bill, what each deduction has collected this year and in earlier years, and a paycheque that stops collecting a deduction once its maximum is reached

Many payroll deductions stop for the year once you have paid their maximum: in Canada, for example, CPP contributions and EI premiums, and in the United States the Social Security tax. A scheduled paycheque in Monize would otherwise keep deducting the same amount all year, so the bills you post and the forecast you plan with would be wrong for the last months of every year. A payroll deduction rule fixes that for one deduction on one paycheque.

h: Before You Start: a Split Paycheque
x: The rules work on a scheduled deposit that records your paycheque as a split (see Split Scheduled Transactions ): Line Category Amount Gross pay Salary 3,100.00 Income tax Payroll Deductions: Income Tax -512.60 Pension Payroll Deductions: CPP Contributions -176.43 Employment insurance Payroll Deductions: EI Premiums -50.84 Second pension tier, not deducted yet Payroll Deductions: CPP2 Contributions 0.00 The bill's amount is the net pay that reaches your account. Each deduction is a negative line with its own category; a line of zero is a deduction the paycheque does not take at the moment but will later (one that starts part-way through the year, or one already stopped for this year).

Open Tools > Taxes > Payroll Deductions . With no rules yet, the page explains what to do and offers Create Your First Rule . Once you have rules, each one is a row: Column Description Bill The scheduled paycheque the rule caps Category The deduction line it caps Yearly maximum The most the category collects in one year, in the bill's currency Resets on When the count next starts again from zero Per paycheque What one paycheque deducts: From the bill's line , or Entered by you when the bill's line is zero. Expected amount needed means neither is known, so the forecast cannot project the deduction Actions Edit or delete the rule Back to Taxes returns to the Taxes page.

Click + New Rule . One form creates the rules for several deductions of one paycheque at once. Field Description Payroll scheduled bill The scheduled deposit that is your paycheque. Only active bills that pay in more than they take out are offered Resets How often the count starts again: Yearly Reset date The day each year the count starts again, usually the first day of the year. A new rule starts on the next 1 January Deduction category One of the bill's deduction lines. Only the bill's own deduction lines are offered, and not those that already have a rule Yearly maximum The most this category collects in one year, in the bill's currency Expected per paycheque Shown only when the bill's line for the category is zero: what a paycheque usually deducts once it does. When the bill has a line, the form shows it instead ("The bill's line deducts ... per paycheque") + Add another category adds a row for the next deduction of the same bill, and the button beside a row removes it. All the rows are saved together or not at all. Monize fills in what it can from your history, and says so under the box: Yearly maximum : estimated from what the category has already collected. A deduction that stopped this year stopped at its maximum, so the year's total is the estimate; otherwise it is last year's total, or this year's when that is already higher. Expected per paycheque : the amount your transactions in this category most often show over the last year. When another paycheque already has a rule on the same category, the new row starts from that rule's maximum, because the two share one maximum (see Several Paycheques ). A figure you type is never replaced. Check the suggestions against the official maximums for the year: they come from your own history, not from any government source. To change a rule, click the edit button on its row: the Edit Deduction Rule dialog holds that one category. The delete button removes a rule after you confirm; transactions already posted are not changed, and the next paycheque posts its full line.

When the paycheque is posted , automatically or from the Post dialog, each deduction line with a rule is reduced to the room left under the year's maximum, down to zero, and the paycheque's amount grows by the difference. For example, with EI capped at 1,077.48 and 1,024.00 paid so far this year: Paycheque Line on the bill Room left Line as posted Net pay 24 April -64.00 53.48 -53.48 10.52 more 8 May -64.00 0.00 0.00 64.00 more First paycheque after the reset -64.00 1,077.48 -64.00 as usual What has been paid is read from your transactions at the moment the paycheque posts: every transaction in the category since the last reset date, in any account, in the bill's currency. A refund in the category lowers it. Transactions in another currency are not counted, so in that case the paycheque errs towards deducting. A rule never changes a transaction that is already posted: it only shapes the next paycheque. Lines that are not deductions (the gross pay) are left alone, and a rule never raises a deduction above the bill's line. The same reduction shows wherever Monize looks ahead: The Cash Flow Forecast on the Bills & Deposits page and the dashboard projects each future paycheque with the reduced deduction, the larger net pay that follows, and the full deduction again after the reset date. Editing one occurrence of the paycheque (see Overriding Individual Occurrences ) opens it with the lines as the posting will cap them.

h: Year to Date and Previous Periods
x: Two buttons under the list open the figures behind the rules. Show year-to-date opens Paid this period : for each category, the bills that cap it, the current Period , what it has Paid so far, the Yearly maximum and what is Remaining . Paid counts every transaction in the category, across every account, in the bill's currency; when some were in another currency, the row says how many were left out. Show previous periods opens Previous Periods : what each category collected in each of its last five completed years, newest first. It is a quick check of last year's maximum when you confirm this year's. For a full year-by-year and paycheque-by-paycheque view, use the Payroll Deductions report under Reports; see Tax Reports .

When two paycheques deduct to the same category (a mid-month and a month-end paycheque, or two jobs) and each has a rule on it, they share one maximum: the room is spent in date order across both bills, and where their maximums differ the lower one applies. The year-to-date table shows such a category once, naming both bills.

Two months before a rule resets, Monize sends a notification asking you to confirm next year's maximum, since most maximums change every year. Nothing changes if you do not act: the rule keeps its values and resets on its date. Open the notification to go to Payroll Deductions and edit the rule. Where the notification is delivered is set under Notifications . Tip Set the rules up early in the year, before any maximum is reached. Rules created later still work: the paid figure always comes from the transactions already in the category, so the next paycheque is capped correctly from the day you save.

Monize can read order confirmations from a mailbox and turn them into itemized transactions: it finds the bank transaction the email belongs to, fills in the line items, and shows you what it proposes before anything changes. A bank row says how much and when, not what you bought. An order email says both, so a single Amazon.ca charge can become a split with one line for each thing you bought, each with its own category, and the order number in the description. This page covers the Email Receipts hub (its tabs, the emails it has read, the profiles that read them and the proposals waiting for you), then connecting the mailbox -- a Gmail account above all, since Google's rules decide how you should connect, then Microsoft 365 and any other IMAP server -- and what to do when the connection fails.

Where it lives. Email Receipts is under Tools in the main menu, with four tabs: Overview , Mailbox , Profiles and Emails . The Settings page has an Email Receipts card that leads to it, and Settings > Email Receipts opens the Mailbox tab. What it reads. Order confirmations are read from a dedicated mailbox over IMAP.
