Monize only reads it: it never changes, moves or deletes a message, and it opens the folder read-only. Old emails can also be uploaded as files (see Importing Archived Emails ). How often. With Read the mailbox automatically on, the folder is read every 15 minutes. Poll now reads it on demand at any time. Use a dedicated mailbox. Every message in the folder is read, so it should hold nothing but order confirmations. With Gmail the natural "dedicated mailbox" is a label : create a filter that applies a label such as Receipts to the shops' confirmations, and point Monize at that label. Gmail labels appear to IMAP as folders (a nested label is written Parent/Child ). Forwarded emails count. An email you forward from your main mailbox is read by its original sender and date, so forwarding the shops' confirmations to the dedicated mailbox works. Who can use it. The account owner only. A delegate sees neither the hub nor the mailbox settings. In demo mode, connecting a mailbox and writing profiles are turned off. What it needs on the server. ENCRYPTION_KEY must be set: a mailbox password or sign-in is stored encrypted, and cannot be saved without it.

Each email goes through the same steps: Read. The profile for the email's sender reads the total, the line items, the order number and so on (see Profiles ). An email with no profile can still be read when it carries an order as structured data (schema.org markup that mail clients use for their order cards); many large shops include it. With AI mode set to Automatic , the AI can also help (see Mailbox Settings ). Match. Monize looks for the bank transaction the email paid for: by the order number or a reference in the transaction's text, by the amount and the payee, or by the amount within a few days of the purchase. Propose. It proposes a change to that transaction: a split with one line per item and a category for each, the payee and a description. The proposal waits in the AI review inbox . Approve. Nothing changes in your register until you approve the proposal, unless you turned on Apply proposals automatically and the email met its strict conditions.

The Overview tab sums up the state of things: Mailbox : whether it is Polling , Polling is off , its Last poll failed or it is Not connected , how it signs in, and its last successful poll or last error. Emails : how many are stored, and how many can be processed again. Proposals : how many wait for your approval, with Review the proposals . Profiles : how many are approved, and how many drafts wait for your approval. Senders without a profile : each sender domain whose emails no profile reads, with Create a profile , which opens the profile wizard for it. Until a mailbox is connected, emails are stored and a profile is approved, the tab opens with Get started with email receipts : four steps (connect a mailbox, fetch the emails, create a profile for a sender, review the proposals), each with a link to where it is done.

The Emails tab lists every email Monize has read, newest first, with the transaction it matched and its State : State Meaning Waiting to be read Stored, not processed yet No profile No profile reads this sender, and the email carries no structured order Could not be read Its profile found no total, no items, or items that do not add up No transaction found No bank transaction fits it (yet: the bank may post it later) Several transactions fit More than one transaction fits equally well; choose the right one Another request is open The transaction already has an open review request Waiting for approval A proposal waits in the review inbox Waiting for the AI The email was handed to the AI and its answer has not arrived Applied , Dismissed , Expired What became of its proposal Waiting for its repayment A purchase email waiting for the repayment that pays for it (see Linked Profiles ) Ignored , Skipped Ignored by you or by its profile; skipped because it was too large or could not be decoded Above the list: Search emails by subject, sender or content ( Search in ), and by From date and To date . Filter by state , each state with its count ( In review groups the emails with an open proposal). Sender domain narrows the list to one sender and its sub-domains. Each row's actions depend on its state: Approve a proposal from here, Choose transaction for an email with none, Prepare a profile with AI or Create profile for a sender without one, View the email, and under More actions : Reprocess , Recognize with AI , Ignore and delete. A reprocessed email is read again with the profiles as they are now. Selecting emails. Tick emails (or Select all emails on this list , then Select all N matching this filter ) to act on many at once: Reprocess , Restore ignored , Approve proposals , Ignore or Delete . Deselect by takes emails out of a large selection by state, by sender, or by the day they arrived. Deleting a stored email does not touch the mailbox, and a later poll does not fetch it again. View opens the email: its sender, the day it arrived (and the day the shop sent it, for a forwarded email), its State , the Profile that read it (or Structured data ), how the transaction was Matched by , and the transaction itself. What the profile read lists the order number, the items with their categories, and the total. The email can be shown as HTML (remote images are not loaded), as Text , or as the numbered Lines a profile's patterns are matched against. When several transactions fit, the dialog lists them under Transactions that fit with Link to this transaction . For an email with no transaction, Choose transaction opens the email with a Choose the transaction section: your transactions between From and To (at first the days around the purchase), with a search by payee, description or amount. Click Link on the one the email paid for, or change the dates to look further, and Monize proposes the change for it as if it had found it itself. Recognize with AI (or Recognize as a trade with AI for a brokerage email) hands one email to the AI assistant in the chat, with the transaction it should describe. The assistant's answer is a proposal you approve like any other. It needs an AI provider (see AI ); without one, the request waits in the review inbox for an agent such as an MCP client.

A profile tells Monize how to read the order confirmations of one sender: which emails it reads (the sender domains, and optionally words the subject must contain), the patterns that find the total, the items and the order number, the categories the items get, and how the bank transaction is found. Once approved, a profile runs on its own, without the AI. The Profiles tab lists every profile with its Status ( Draft or Approved , Written by you or Drafted by AI ), its Payee and its actions: Edit , Approve (for a draft), View JSON and Delete . Deleting a profile keeps what it already read. After you approve or change a profile, Monize offers to process the stored emails of its senders again ( Process now ). Create a profile for a domain lists the senders whose emails no approved profile reads; choose one (or Create a profile on the Overview) to start the wizard: Samples. Click an email to read it and choose the transaction it paid for, then tick up to five emails to write the profile from. For a broker's emails, tick These emails are brokerage trade confirmations : they need no transaction. Generate. Send to AI : the assistant reads the samples and their transactions and writes a draft profile. Not happy? Write what to change under Requested Changes and Send note to AI . Without an AI provider in Monize, the request waits in the review inbox for your AI agent, and the wizard says so. Preview and accept. The draft is run over the samples and the other emails of the sender, read-only: for each, the transaction you expected, what the draft read, whether they agree, and the outcome. Accept and process approves the profile and reads the sender's stored emails with it. Prepare a profile with AI on the Emails tab does the same from emails you select there. Create a new profile manually , or Edit on a profile, opens the editor: Which emails it reads : the Name , the Payee the transactions get, the Sender domains (a sub-domain of a listed domain also matches) and Subject contains . Profile kind : an order confirmation, or a brokerage trade confirmation (see Trade Confirmations ). Matching emails can also make a profile ignore or delete every email of a sender you never want to deal with. Patterns : Order number patterns , Total patterns , Shipping , Discount and Fees patterns , and the Line items (where the items start and stop, and the Item patterns ). Each pattern is matched against one whole line of the email, ignoring case; * stands for any text and a name in braces, such as {amount} , captures a value. A profile can read the email's text or the lines of its HTML part ( Lines source ). Categories : a Default category for items no rule covers, the Shipping category and the Fees category , and rules that give a category to items whose name matches. Matching : the Strategies, in the order tried (order number, reference, amount and payee, amount and date), where to look for the order number or reference, the Days before the purchase and Days after the purchase a transaction may be dated, and the Amount tolerance . Proposal : a tag to add to the transactions the profile splits, and whether the AI may choose the category of items no rule matches. Form and JSON at the top switch between the form and the profile's JSON definition (a definition that uses something the form cannot show opens as JSON). The test panel runs the profile, as it is in the editor, over a stored email you choose: what it read, line by line, and which transaction it would match. When a purchase is paid later or in instalments, the shop's itemized email and the bank transaction are linked by a third email from the payment provider. A purchase profile stores the shop's email, and a repayment profile reads the provider's email and matches the bank transaction. When the repayment arrives, its transaction is split into every item of the purchases it pays, spread proportionally over the instalments; a purchase email that arrives later updates the proposal. Linked proposals always wait for your approval. To draft both profiles, select up to five emails from each sender together on the Emails tab and choose Prepare a profile with AI . A trade profile reads a broker's "order filled" email and proposes the investment transaction it reports: a buy, a sell, a cash dividend or a reinvested dividend, with the symbol, the number of shares, the total or price, the commission, the date and the account. Accounts the broker prints alike (a CAD and a USD account) are told apart by currency. A trade already in your ledger is not proposed again, and one that pays a scheduled investment transaction posts that occurrence. A trade is applied without asking only when Apply proposals automatically is on and the price agrees with the shares and the total.

Every proposal waits in the AI review inbox ( AI > AI Review Inbox , or Review the proposals on the Overview); the Email receipts filter shows only these. Each request names the email it came from ( View email receipts opens it) and the transaction it would change, and its Apply this transaction edit? card lists the result: the account, amount, date and payee, the split lines with their categories, the new description (the old one followed by the profile's name and the items) and the order number as Ref # . A proposal on a reconciled transaction says so. Approve rewrites the transaction as shown. Approve on the Emails tab does the same. Dismiss leaves the transaction as it is. Approve selected and Approve all shown apply several proposals at once; each is checked against its transaction as it is now, and one that no longer fits is skipped and reported. Proposals that nobody approves expire after 30 days. The Email receipts row of Settings > Notifications tells you when emails need a profile or a fix, and the AI review proposals row when proposals are waiting or about to expire.

The Mailbox tab's Import archived emails reads exported emails: .eml , .mbox , .msg or .zip files, several at once. A file keeps the shop's own sender and purchase date, unlike an email forwarded later, so it is the way to read old order confirmations. How to export emails from your provider explains how to get them out of Gmail (Google Takeout for a label, or one email at a time), Outlook, Apple Mail and other providers (Thunderbird with ImportExportTools NG). A Google Takeout .zip can be uploaded as it is. The import needs a mailbox to be set up, stores each email once (importing the same file again adds nothing) and processes them straight away.

There are two ways to connect a Gmail mailbox, and Google's policies -- not Monize -- decide which one fits you. IMAP has no narrower Google scope than https://mail.google.com/ , which Google classes as restricted : an app that asks for it must either be verified by Google (an annual, paid security assessment) or live with the limits Google puts on unverified apps. Path What you need Limits Best for A. App password through the manual IMAP form A personal Google account with 2-Step Verification on Not available for Google Workspace ("work, school or organization") accounts, accounts in Advanced Protection, or accounts whose 2-Step Verification uses security keys only Personal Gmail. Start here. No Google Cloud project, nothing to verify, no expiry. B. Connect with Google , audience External , status Testing A Google Cloud project with an OAuth client (set up by the administrator) Only the test users listed on the project (up to 100) can connect, and every grant expires after 7 days -- the mailbox then stops and asks to be reconnected Trying the feature out, or a tiny group that accepts a weekly Reconnect C. Connect with Google , audience Internal A Google Workspace organisation, with the Cloud project inside it Only accounts in that Workspace domain can connect A family or business on Google Workspace. No verification, no 7-day expiry. D. Connect with Google , External , In production Google's restricted-scope verification (about 6 weeks) plus a CASA Tier 2 security assessment by a Google-authorised lab, repeated every year, costing hundreds to thousands of dollars None after verification Not realistic for a self-hosted deployment. Monize does not offer this. Both Google paths give Monize the same access: a scope that could write to the mailbox. Monize still opens the folder read-only and exposes no write operation, so the mailbox is never changed.
An app password is a 16-character passcode that lets one app sign in to your Google account without your real password. It is the simplest way to connect a personal Gmail account.

h: 1. Create the app password in Google
x: Turn on 2-Step Verification for the Google account if it is not already on (Google Account > Security). App passwords exist only on accounts with 2-Step Verification. Open myaccount.google.com/apppasswords , give the password a name such as Monize receipts and click Create . Copy the 16 characters shown. Google shows them once; spaces are ignored. Advanced Protection: app passwords are not available on an account enrolled in Google's Advanced Protection Program , and enrolling later revokes any app password already created, so a mailbox saved with one stops working. Use a separate Gmail account for receipts instead. If the page says app passwords are not available, the account is a Workspace account, is in Advanced Protection, or uses security keys only. Those accounts connect with Google instead (see below) or, for Workspace, ask the administrator for the Internal path.

Go to Tools > Email Receipts and open the Mailbox tab. In the manual form, fill in: Field Value IMAP server imap.gmail.com Port 993 Connection security TLS (usually port 993) User name the full Gmail address Password the 16-character app password Folder INBOX , or the label you dedicated to receipts (a nested label is Parent/Child ) Click Test connection . Monize logs in and reports "The connection works. The folder holds N messages." or the error the server returned. Click Save mailbox . Once saved, the password is never shown again. Editing the mailbox with the password left blank keeps the stored one.

With this path the user never types a password into Monize: they sign in at Google, approve the access, and Monize stores a refresh token (encrypted with ENCRYPTION_KEY ) that it trades for a short-lived access token every time it reads the mailbox. The IMAP host is always Google's own imap.gmail.com:993 ; the user does not choose a host or port. The Connect with Google button appears only after the administrator has registered an OAuth client and set both of its environment variables. One client serves every user of the deployment.

Decide the audience first, using the table above: Internal if your deployment belongs to a Google Workspace organisation and everyone who will connect is in it; otherwise External , which stays in Testing with its 7-day expiry. Sign in to the Google Cloud console and create a project (or pick one). No billing account is needed, and no API has to be enabled: IMAP sign-in uses only the OAuth scope. Open Google Auth Platform (the former "OAuth consent screen"; search for it in the console). Branding : give the app a name such as Monize and a support email. Add your deployment's domain under Authorized domains if the console asks for one. Audience : choose Internal or External . For External, add every Google account that will connect under Test users (up to 100). Leave the publishing status on Testing . Data Access : click Add or remove scopes and add https://mail.google.com/ (it is listed under Gmail API or can be pasted manually), plus openid and .../auth/userinfo.email . Save. Open Clients > Create client . Application type Web application , any name, and under Authorized redirect URIs add exactly: https://your-monize-host/settings/email-receipts/oauth-callback That is PUBLIC_APP_URL (no trailing slash) followed by /settings/email-receipts/oauth-callback . It must match character for character. Copy the Client ID and Client secret into the backend environment: PUBLIC_APP_URL=https://your-monize-host ENCRYPTION_KEY=... # already required for other secrets EMAIL_RECEIPTS_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=1234567890-abc.apps.googleusercontent.com EMAIL_RECEIPTS_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=GOCSPX-... Restart the backend. The Mailbox tab now shows Connect with Google under Connect an account , above the manual form. A provider with only one of the two variables set is not offered at all. What Monize sends and stores: the authorization request asks for https://mail.google.com/ openid email with access_type=offline and prompt=consent , so Google returns a refresh token on every connection. The login name is the email address from the ID token. The refresh token is the only credential kept, encrypted; the access token lives in memory for one poll.

Go to the Mailbox tab of Tools > Email Receipts and click Connect with Google . Choose the Google account. On an External client in Testing, Google warns "Google hasn't verified this app" : click Continue (this is expected; the administrator's project is unverified by design). An account that is not on the test-user list is refused here. Approve the access Google lists. The browser returns to Monize's Connecting the mailbox page, then to the settings with Connected to Google as you@gmail.com . Set the Folder to read ( INBOX or your receipts label), turn on Read the mailbox automatically , choose the AI mode , and click Save settings . See Mailbox Settings . Click Poll now to read the folder straight away and follow View the saved emails .

Reconnect runs the Google sign-in again and replaces the stored token. Use it when the panel says "The connection to Google is not active, so the mailbox is not being read. Connect again to resume." -- on an External/Testing client that happens every 7 days. Disconnect deletes Monize's stored token and stops reading the mailbox. Emails already stored are kept. Disconnecting does not withdraw the permission you granted. To do that, remove Monize on Google account permissions ; the panel links there. Revoking at Google without disconnecting in Monize is fine too: the next poll records "The mailbox's sign-in was revoked or has expired" and stops until you reconnect.

Microsoft 365 works the same way as Google: the administrator registers one app, and users click Connect with Microsoft . In the Microsoft Entra admin center , open App registrations > New registration . Platform Web , redirect URI ${PUBLIC_APP_URL}/settings/email-receipts/oauth-callback . Under Certificates & secrets , create a client secret and copy its value. Under API permissions , add the delegated permission IMAP.AccessAsUser.All (Office 365 Exchange Online) plus the OpenID permissions openid , email and offline_access . An organisation may still need to enable IMAP for the mailbox and allow users to consent to the app. Set the environment: EMAIL_RECEIPTS_MICROSOFT_CLIENT_ID=... EMAIL_RECEIPTS_MICROSOFT_CLIENT_SECRET=... EMAIL_RECEIPTS_MICROSOFT_TENANT=common # optional, default shown EMAIL_RECEIPTS_MICROSOFT_TENANT decides who may sign in: common (work, school and personal accounts), organizations , consumers , or one tenant's GUID or domain. A value that is not a valid tenant disables Microsoft sign-in and logs a warning. The IMAP host is fixed to outlook.office365.com:993 .

The manual form takes any IMAP server: host, port, TLS (usually 993) or STARTTLS (usually 143), user name and password. Most providers require an app password rather than the account password. The server's certificate is always verified; there is no "accept any certificate" switch. Two server-side rules apply to the host: Private addresses. A host that is a private, loopback or link-local address ( localhost , 192.168.x.x , a container name, .local , .internal ) can be used only by an administrator , unless the operator lists it in EMAIL_RECEIPTS_PRIVATE_HOST_ALLOWLIST (for example mail.lan:993,192.168.1.30:993 ). The check runs when the mailbox is saved and again on every connection. How much one poll reads. EMAIL_RECEIPTS_MAX_MESSAGES_PER_POLL (default 50) caps the messages read per poll; the rest wait for the next one. EMAIL_RECEIPTS_MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES (default 2,000,000) is the largest message downloaded; a larger one is recorded as skipped and never fetched.

The Mailbox tab holds the connection and these settings. They are the same for a password mailbox and a connected one. Setting What it does Folder The folder to read. It is opened read-only. Changing it starts reading the new folder from the beginning. Read the mailbox automatically When on, Monize reads the mailbox every 15 minutes. Turning it off does not disconnect the mailbox, and Poll now reads it whether this is on or off. AI mode Off : the poll never calls the AI for receipts. On demand : the poll never calls the AI, but you can ask the assistant yourself with Recognize with AI or Prepare a profile with AI . Automatic : the poll asks the AI about a matched receipt that no approved profile could read completely, and drafts a profile for a sender that has none. Every AI answer is a proposal you approve. Apply proposals automatically Off by default. A proposal is applied without asking only when an approved profile read the whole email, the transaction was found by an order number or reference, or by exact amount and payee with a single candidate, and the proposal adds up to the cent. A trade confirmation is booked without asking only when its approved trade profile read the whole trade, the price agrees with the shares and the total, and your ledger does not already hold the trade. Everything else waits for your approval. Count profile proposals toward the daily AI limit On by default. Turn it off when a large batch of stored emails would otherwise use up the daily limit of AI-proposed changes. Every proposal still waits for your approval. The status block shows the Last poll , the Last successful poll and the Last error , and offers Poll now and Delete mailbox . Poll now reports how many emails it saved, skipped and processed, with View the saved emails . Deleting the mailbox removes the settings and every stored email from Monize; the emails in the mailbox itself are not touched.

Message What it means No Connect with Google button, only the manual form The server has not set both EMAIL_RECEIPTS_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID and EMAIL_RECEIPTS_GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET , or was not restarted after setting them. "Sign-in with this provider is not set up on this server." Same cause, reached by an old page or a stale link. Ask the administrator. Google: Error 400: redirect_uri_mismatch The redirect URI registered on the client does not equal PUBLIC_APP_URL + /settings/email-receipts/oauth-callback . Check the scheme ( https ), the host, the port, and that PUBLIC_APP_URL has no trailing slash. Google: Error 403: access_denied or "has not completed the Google verification process" The client is External in Testing and this account is not on its Test users list; or the client is Internal and the account is outside the Workspace domain. "Google hasn't verified this app" Expected for an unverified (Testing) client. Click Continue . "The provider did not grant lasting access. Remove this app's access in your account's security settings and connect again." Google returned no refresh token. Remove Monize on Google account permissions and click Connect with Google again. "The mailbox's sign-in was revoked or has expired. Connect the mailbox again in the mailbox settings." On an External/Testing client this is the 7-day expiry; otherwise the grant was revoked or the account password changed. Click Reconnect . To stop it recurring, move to the Internal audience or to an app password. "This sign-in link is not valid any more. Start connecting the mailbox again." The sign-in took too long or the callback was opened twice. Start again from the settings. "The provider did not accept the sign-in, so the mailbox was not connected." The code exchange failed, most often a wrong client secret or a secret that has expired. The administrator should check the client's credentials. "This server has no encryption key configured, so a mailbox sign-in cannot be stored." The deployment has no ENCRYPTION_KEY . Nothing can be saved until the administrator sets one. "The stored sign-in cannot be read on this server. Connect the mailbox again in the mailbox settings." The token was stored under a different ENCRYPTION_KEY , typically after a restore onto another instance. Reconnect. Test connection: "Application-specific password required" or "Invalid credentials" The account password was used instead of an app password, or the account cannot have one (Workspace, Advanced Protection, security keys only). Create an app password, or use Connect with Google . "This mail server address is a private or local network address..." A non-administrator entered a private host. Only an administrator can use one, unless the operator allows it in EMAIL_RECEIPTS_PRIVATE_HOST_ALLOWLIST . Connected, but the folder reads 0 messages The Folder does not match: Gmail labels are case-sensitive, and a nested label is Parent/Child . Test connection on the manual form reports the count; on a connected mailbox use Poll now .

Monize keeps track of money you spend together with other people : a trip, a shared apartment, a club. You record who paid for each purchase and who it was for, and Monize works out each person's position and the fewest repayments that settle the group. Shared entries stay separate from your personal accounts . Adding an expense or recording a repayment here does not move money between bank accounts, and nothing in a group appears in your balances, budgets or reports.

Shared Expenses is in the Tools menu on a computer, and in the navigation menu on a phone. It belongs to your own profile: a delegate viewing your data does not see it, and you switch back to your own profile to open your groups. The page has two tabs: Groups lists your groups with your position in each. Above the list, Owed to You and You Owe add up your positions across every group, per currency. Switch between Active and Archived groups, or use Search groups . People holds your private list of people (see Keeping the Same Person Across Groups ). Click a group to open it.

Choose New Group . Group Name , for example "Ski trip" or "Apartment bills". Your Name is how you appear to the others in this group. Settlement Currency is the currency balances and repayments are worked out in. Purchases can still be in other currencies (see Foreign Currencies ). The currency is fixed once the group has its first entry. People : one row for each person taking part; Add Person adds another row. Nobody needs a Monize account. You can record expenses for everyone and invite them later, or never. Choose Create Group . Keep one group for the whole trip: each purchase can involve a different selection of its people.

Across the top, Group Expenses is what the group spent, Your Cost is your share of it and You Paid is what you paid, all in the settlement currency. Your position, what you are owed or owe once repayments are counted, is on the Balances tab and in the group list. The switcher beside the group's name jumps to another group. The tabs below are: Tab What it holds Expenses Every entry, with search and filters Balances Each person's position and the suggested repayments Files Receipts, tickets and photos for the group Activity Who changed what, and when Settings People, access, invitations and the group itself On Expenses , Search descriptions and notes finds an entry by its text, and the filters below it narrow the list by Entry Type (expenses, refunds, income or repayments), by one of the People , or by a From and To date. Each active filter shows as a chip you can remove. Export CSV downloads the whole group: the entries, every person's share and payment, and the positions.

Choose Add Expense , then Expense . Description , Amount and its currency, and Date . Paid By : who paid. Choose More than one person paid to enter how much each payer contributed; the amounts must add up to the total. Split Between shows who the purchase was for. It starts as an equal split between everyone; choose Change Split to change it. More Options holds a Note , a Group Label (a free-text tag such as "Food" that the group sees), and the Agreed Exchange Rate when the purchase is in another currency. Add a receipt or photo under attachments if you have one. It is shared with the group when you save. Check the amounts in the preview and choose Save . A person can pay without having a share: a friend who paid for your concert ticket is owed the whole amount. Choose Add Expense , then Income , for money the group received rather than spent, such as a deposit returned to the group or winnings shared between you. It works the same way: Received By replaces Paid By , and the split says who it belongs to.

Each person has a switch. Turn someone off when they did not take part; they are left out of this expense only. For the people left in: Leave every amount blank to split equally . Enter a fixed amount or a percentage for a person; whatever is left is split equally between the people whose fields are blank. Zero keeps a person in the split without charging them. Use Shares for relative portions: shares of 2, 1 and 1 give the first person half and the others a quarter each. The line at the top says whether the split is complete, or how much is still to allocate or over-allocated. Split Equally starts again. Choose Apply Split to go back to the expense. Percentages shown while you type may be rounded; the saved amounts are worked out by the server and add up exactly to the total.

When a group always shares costs the same way, such as a 60/40 split of the rent, the owner saves it under Default split in the group's Settings . New expenses start from it. Existing entries keep the split they were saved with, and someone added to the group later is not in the default until you edit it. Use Equal Split For Everyone removes it.
An expense dated in the future is Planned : it is listed, but does not affect balances until its date. Open it on that day to record it.

Click an entry to open it. Edit changes any part of it. Balances follow the change, and the entry's earlier version stays in its history. Record Refund records money returned for an expense, such as a cancelled booking. The refund follows the original split, takes earlier refunds into account, and uses the original expense's exchange rate. Cancel Entry removes an entry recorded by mistake. Give a reason; its effect is removed from the balances, and it stays in the list and the activity as Cancelled . Entries are never deleted, so everyone in the group can see what changed.

The Balances tab shows where everyone stands. Each Person's Position is what each person is owed (positive) or owes (negative). Review under a name breaks it down into what they paid, their share, their income share, and the repayments they sent and received. Suggested Repayments are the fewest transfers that would settle everyone. They use each person's net position across all purchases, so you may be asked to repay someone who did not pay for your particular expense; that is still correct. Settling once at the end of a trip is usually simpler than repaying after every purchase.

Monize does not send money. After the money has changed hands, choose Record Repayment beside the suggestion, or Record Other Repayment for any other payment between two people. From , To and Amount are filled in from the suggestion; change the amount for a partial repayment. A repayment larger than the current suggestion is refused unless you turn on I understand this payment may exceed the current suggestion , which protects you from recording the same payment twice.

When someone who has joined the group with their own Monize account owes money, Remind under their suggestion, then Send Reminder , sends them a notification that opens the group's balances. You can remind the same person once every 24 hours, and the reminder respects their notification settings and whether they have muted the group.

A purchase can be in any currency. Its amount is converted to the settlement currency with: the Agreed Exchange Rate you entered under More Options (the rate stays with the expense), or the historical market rate for the purchase date, when you did not enter one. When Monize has no rate for that currency pair and date, the expense is marked and the group shows a notice: the positions and suggestions wait until the rate is known, and Known position shows your position without that expense. Open the marked expense from the notice to enter the rate you agreed, or retry the lookup. See Currency Management for where market rates come from.

Files collects every document in the group: files uploaded straight to the group (tickets, bookings, a photo of the bill before anyone has entered it) and the attachments of individual expenses. Upload Files adds documents; each can be renamed and given a document type. Create Expense From This File opens a new expense with the file already attached, for a receipt uploaded first. Open Related Entry opens the expense a file belongs to. Share a Private Document copies a document from one of your own transactions into the group. The copy is separate: the original stays private. Activity lists every change to the group: entries added, changed or cancelled, people added, invitations, access changes and documents, each with who made it and when.

Anyone in a group can stay a name only. To let a person see the group and add expenses themselves, invite them from Settings . They need a Monize account on the same server. Choose Invite beside the person. Optionally enter Restrict to email (optional) so that only that account can use the link. Choose Create Invitation , then Copy Link and send it to them however you like. Monize does not email it. They open the link, sign in, and choose Join Group . They join as the person already in the group, with that person's history. A link is valid for 7 days, and creating another one for the same person replaces it. Remove Access under Invite at the bottom of Settings revokes a link nobody has used yet. Joining shows the other person the group's expenses, people and documents. Your personal finances stay private : nobody in the group sees your accounts, categories, payees or bank records.

Access Can Owner Everything: edit people, invite, change access, archive or delete the group Can add expenses Add, edit, refund and cancel entries, record repayments, upload files Can view Read the group, its balances and files Change a joined person's access with the list beside their name. Remove Access ends their access but leaves them and their history in the group.

To hand the group over, pick Ask To Take Ownership in the list beside a joined person. They see Accept Ownership in their Settings; once they accept, you choose Complete Handover . The new owner manages access and the group's settings, and you stay on as someone who can add expenses.

The owner can, from Settings : Edit a person's name. Add Person to an existing group. Deactivate a person who has not joined, for example someone who left the household. Their earlier expenses and balances stay; they are left out of new expenses. Reactivate brings them back.

h: Keeping the Same Person Across Groups
x: The People tab on the main page is your own list of the people you share costs with; nobody else sees it. Save a person there, optionally linked to one of your payees, then use Link to a private person in a group's Settings to connect their appearance in that group. New Group then offers Add someone from your people , so you do not retype names. Groups stay separate: linking does not merge balances.

Archive Group (owner) closes a finished trip. An archived group stays readable and its balances still count on the main page; Reopen Group before adding or editing entries. Leave Group (anyone but the owner) ends your access. Your recorded history stays in the group. Delete Empty Group (owner) is only offered while a group has no entries. A group with entries, documents or bookings is archived instead. Mute Group Notifications stops notifications from one group; Enable Group Notifications turns them back on.

When someone else changes a group you are in, or changes your access, Monize sends you a notification that opens the group. Choose how they reach you under Settings > Notifications , in the Shared expenses row (see Settings and Security ).

Open Settings > Guided tours and choose Start beside Shared expenses . The walkthrough points out navigation, group creation, expenses and balances. It does not create sample records for you. When asked to open a group, select one from the list. If you have none yet, choose Skip this step ; the tour finishes without opening a group. You can create your group afterwards and use Retake in Guided tours to see the remaining steps. Use End tour or Escape to leave at any time.

Monize keeps track of what you bought and when its warranty ends : the purchase, the receipt, manual and photos that prove it, its serial and model numbers, any claims you made, and a reminder before the coverage runs out. Most warranties start from a transaction that is already in your register, so the purchase and its proof stay together. A warranty never moves money . Its purchase price is there for reference only and is never added to a balance, a report or a total.

Warranties is in the Tools menu. Above the list, four cards count your Expiring soon (within 30 days), Active , Expired and Lifetime warranties; click a card to show only those. Below them: Filter by status : All , Expiring , Active , Expired or Lifetime , each with its count. Search warranties matches the name, the vendor, the model number and the serial numbers. Show archived lists the archived warranties instead of the current ones. Export CSV and Import CSV (see Importing From Warracker and Exporting ). The list shows each warranty's Name (with the vendor under it), Status and days left, the date it Expires , the date it was Purchased , the Price , the number of Documents and of Open claims . Click the Name , Expires or Purchased header to sort by it (on a phone, the sort is a row of chips). Each row has Edit , Archive and Delete ; click anywhere else on the row to open the warranty.

The detail page shows the warranty's end date and days left, its purchase date, its Purchase Price and its Open Claims , then: Details : the Purchase it was bought with, the Warranty type , the Vendor (with the payee's logo when Monize has one), the Model number , the Serial numbers , the Product page and the Notes . Documents and Claims (see below). Click the Purchase to edit that transaction right there, in the same window the register uses. View in register opens the Transactions page with the purchase highlighted. Switch warranty in the header jumps to another warranty without going back to the list. Archive a warranty you no longer care about: it disappears from the list, the widget, the reminders and the AI assistant, but nothing is deleted and Unarchive brings it back. Delete removes the warranty together with its claims and documents.

Click Add warranty and fill in: Field Notes Name What you bought. Required, up to 200 characters. Vendor Pick a payee or type a name. Warranty type Manufacturer (the default), Extended , Store or Other . Model number , Serial numbers Click Add serial number for each one, up to 10. Purchase date Required. Coverage ends On a date , After a duration (years, months and days from the purchase date; Monize shows the date it works out), or Never for a lifetime warranty. A new warranty starts at After a duration of 1 year. A lifetime warranty has no end date and no reminder. Purchase price Optional, with its currency. Product page , Notes Optional. Documents Optional. Add attachment or Scan document for the receipt, manual or certificate while creating the warranty; they upload when you save it. A duration that lands on a day the month does not have ends on the month's last day: 1 month from January 31 is February 28. When you edit a warranty later, Coverage ends shows the end date it was saved with.

Most warranties start from a purchase in your register. Open the transaction's edit window on the Transactions page: its Warranties section lists the warranties already linked to it, each with its status and end date, and offers Add warranty . Add warranty takes you to the Warranties page with the form pre-filled from the transaction: the name (the payee, or the description), the vendor, the purchase date, the price and the currency. A form with unsaved changes asks first; a new transaction is saved before you leave it. A split transaction fills in its whole amount, so edit the price before saving if the warranty covers only one item. One transaction can carry several warranties (three items on one receipt are three warranties). After you save, the Warranties page shows only that transaction's warranties ( Warranties for one transaction ); Show all warranties clears it. In the register, a row with a warranty shows a shield with the number of warranties beside its paperclip, and the search box accepts has:warranty . Click a warranty in the edit window's Warranties section to open it. Deleting the transaction keeps the warranty and its own documents; the detail page then says No linked transaction .

Status Meaning Active More than 30 days left Expiring soon 30 days or fewer, including the day it expires ( Expires today ) Expired The end date has passed Lifetime Never ends Days are counted in your own timezone, and the status is worked out by the server, so every screen agrees.

The Documents section works like a transaction's attachments: upload a file, or scan a paper receipt with your phone's camera, and preview images and PDFs in the app. Each document has a Document type : Receipt , Manual , Photo , Warranty or Other . A new document starts as Other ; choose its type from the Document type picker on its row, and change it there whenever you like. A warranty holds up to 10 documents of up to 10 MB each. A document belongs to the warranty, and when the warranty is linked to a transaction it is one of that transaction's attachments too: it appears in the transaction's attachments (labelled with the warranty's name), in the register's paperclip count and in the has:attachment search, even after the warranty is archived. Deleting the warranty removes its documents everywhere.

The Claims section logs what you claimed and how it ended, newest first. Click Add claim and enter the Claim date , a Status ( Open , Approved , Denied or Resolved ), a Description of what went wrong, and, once it is settled, the Resolution and the date it Closed on (only for a resolved or denied claim; it cannot be before the claim date). Each claim has Edit and Delete . Open claims are counted on the list and on the detail page. A claim never changes the warranty's status.

Monize reminds you 30 days and 7 days before a warranty ends, and on the day it expires. Each reminder is sent once; nothing is sent after the day of expiry, or for an archived or lifetime warranty. If you change the end date, the reminders start again for the new date. A reminder opens the warranty's detail page, and like any notification it can be snoozed or repeated from the notification centre. How a reminder reaches you is set on the Warranty reminders row of How to notify me in Settings > Notifications : it is always in the bell, it is in the email report by default, and alert email, push and UnifiedPush are off until you turn them on.

Warranties expiring soon is an optional widget. Add it from the dashboard's Customize dialog (see Dashboard ). It shows up to five warranties expiring within 30 days, soonest first, and its title opens the Warranties page.

In Shared Access , the Warranties toggle on the delegate's Sections tab lets them see your warranties, their documents and their claims, and gives them the Warranties link in their Tools menu and the dashboard widget. A delegate can read and export, but cannot add, edit, archive, delete, import, upload or record a claim. The linked purchase is shown only when its account is one the delegate may read. Otherwise the detail page says The purchase is in an account you cannot read.

Import CSV on the Warranties page reads a file in the column set of Warracker , so a Warracker export, or a file exported from this page, imports directly: ProductName , PurchaseDate , WarrantyDurationYears , WarrantyDurationMonths , WarrantyDurationDays , ExpirationDate , IsLifetime , PurchasePrice , SerialNumber , ProductURL , Vendor , Tags , Notes , Currency , ModelNumber , WarrantyType ProductName and PurchaseDate (as YYYY-MM-DD ) are required. Headers match regardless of case. Each row needs one way to end: ExpirationDate , a WarrantyDuration column, or IsLifetime ( true , false , yes , no , 1 or 0 ). When a row gives both a date and a duration, the date is used and the row says so. SerialNumber takes several serial numbers separated by commas, or a JSON array when a serial number itself contains a comma. WarrantyType is manufacturer , extended , store or other ; anything else imports as other , with a note. A price with a blank or unknown Currency uses your default currency. Tags is read and reported as not imported (a warranty has no tags). Choose the file and Monize checks it first: a table shows every row as Ready or Invalid , with the problem and any note, and the columns it did not import. Nothing is saved until you click Import . A file with invalid rows imports nothing unless you tick Skip the invalid rows and import the rest .

Export CSV downloads every warranty the page's current status filter, search, Show archived setting and transaction filter match, in the same Warracker columns. The end date goes in ExpirationDate and the duration columns stay empty.

The AI assistant and MCP clients can list your warranties with the read-only list_warranties tool ("Which of my warranties expire this year?"): status, days left, end date, vendor, open claims and documents, filtered by status or a search, up to 50 at a time. Neither can create or change a warranty.

Limit Value Documents per warranty 10 (up to 10 MB each) Serial numbers per warranty 10, of up to 100 characters each Import file 1 MiB and 1000 rows Expiring window and reminders 30 days; reminders at 30, 7 and 0 days (fixed)
