Categories and payees are the organizational backbone of your financial data. Categories classify what the money was for, while payees track who the money went to or came from.

Categories are used to classify transactions by purpose (e.g., "Groceries," "Rent," "Salary"). They form a hierarchical tree structure with parent and child categories. Note A fresh account has no categories. The Categories page then offers Import Default Categories or Create Your Own . The import asks for a Country (Canada, the United Kingdom and the United States add their own tax and benefit categories; Generic adds none) and the Language the names are created in, from any of the languages Monize is translated into. The result is an ordinary set of income and expense categories with subcategories, which you can rename, recolour or delete like any other. The import is only possible while you have no categories of your own.

Categories support parent-child relationships for detailed tracking: Food & Dining (parent) |- Groceries (child) |- Restaurants (child) |- Coffee Shops (child) Housing (parent) |- Rent (child) |- Utilities (child) |- Maintenance (child) When viewing reports, you can see totals at the parent level (all "Food & Dining") or drill down to individual children (just "Groceries"). A child is shown as Parent: Child wherever its parent matters, such as in the category picker.

Navigate to Tools > Categories to access the category management page. Four cards at the top count your Total Categories , Income Categories , Expense Categories and Top-Level categories. Below them, Search categories finds a category by name (a matching subcategory brings its parent along, and a matching parent brings all of its subcategories), and the All , Expenses and Income buttons narrow the list by type. The list shows each category's icon and colour, its Name , its Type , its transaction Count and its Description . Click a column header to sort by it. Click a row to open the category's detail page ; click the category's name to see its transactions instead (see Viewing a Category's Transactions ). Edit and Delete are at the end of each row (on a phone, press and hold the row, or right-click it, to open its actions). Click + New Category Enter the category details: Field Description Category Name Category name (e.g., "Groceries") Parent Category Optional parent for nesting; leave it on No parent (top-level) for a top-level category Type Expense or Income . A subcategory always has its parent's type ( Type inherited from parent ) Automatic sign Whether an amount you type is given the category's sign (see Automatic Sign ) Colour A colour for reports and charts, picked from the palette, or none. A subcategory can Inherit from parent Icon An icon drawn beside the category's name, or No icon Description (optional) A note about what belongs in the category Click Create Category A category's colour and icon appear in the category list, on its detail page, in the transaction register and in charts. A subcategory with no colour or icon of its own uses its parent's (the list says Inherited from parent when you point at it), so you can colour a whole branch by colouring its parent. In the category list at the Dense row density, the icon is reduced to a coloured dot. Click Edit on a category's row, or Edit on its detail page, to change any of the fields above, then click Update Category . Changing a top-level category's type changes the type of all of its subcategories too. A category cannot be moved under itself or under one of its own subcategories. Click Delete on a category's row or detail page. Monize first checks how many transactions and scheduled bills and deposits use the category: If none do, the dialog says the category can be safely deleted. If some do, choose where they go under Reassign to: another category, or Leave uncategorized . They are moved before the category is deleted. A category that still has subcategories cannot be deleted: move or delete its subcategories first. Payees that used the deleted category as their default category are left without one. Deleting cannot be undone from the dialog. There is no separate merge for categories: to merge one category into another, delete it and reassign its transactions to the category you keep.

Each category has a detail page with its history and analytics. Click a row on the Categories page to open it. The header shows the category's name, icon and type (and System for a system category), with View Transactions , Edit and Delete . The name is also a switcher: click it to filter your categories and jump to another without going back to the list. Below it, the page has these tabs: Overview : Spent This Year (or Received This Year for an income category) compared with the same period last year, the Monthly Average , the Average Transaction , the number of Transactions and the Last Transaction ; a chart of the monthly totals; Top Payees over the last 12 months or all time; the Subcategories breakdown with each one's share; the accounts it was Paid From ; the Upcoming Scheduled bills and deposits in the category; a Tag Breakdown of the category's spending by the values of a tag key ; the category's Key Information (type, parent, subcategories, payees, first and largest transaction, the payees that use it as their default category); and its Seasonality , the typical cost of each month of the year once there is enough history. Transactions : every transaction in the category, editable in place, with Open in the register to see them on the Transactions page. Subcategories (for a category that has some): each subcategory with its total and its number of transactions. Amounts in another currency are converted to your default currency, and the page says so.

Click a category's name on the Categories page (or View Transactions on its detail page) to open the Transactions page filtered to that category, so you can review every transaction assigned to it without setting up the filter by hand.

Each category is marked as either Income or Expense : Income categories -- Salary, freelance income, investment returns, etc. Expense categories -- Groceries, rent, utilities, entertainment, etc. This classification determines how transactions are counted in reports (income vs. expenses charts).

With Automatic sign on, an amount you type for a transaction in the category is made negative for an expense category and positive for an income category, so you never have to type the minus sign. Turn it off ( Disabled ) for a category that holds money in both directions, such as refunds you file under the same category as the purchase; the amount is then kept exactly as you enter it. A subcategory can Inherit from parent , and the form shows which state it inherits.

Transfers move money between your own accounts, so they are never counted as income or expense. You can still optionally assign a category to a transfer. When you do, the transfer appears under that category in the monthly category breakdown, giving you visibility into where transferred money goes, while remaining excluded from income and expense totals.

A category marked (System) cannot be edited or deleted; the list and the detail page mark it as such. The categories you create, and the ones the default import creates, are ordinary categories that you can change freely.
Payees represent the people, businesses, or entities you transact with. Every transaction can optionally be assigned a payee.

Navigate to Tools > Payees to access the payee management page. Four cards at the top count your Total Payees , the Active and Inactive ones, and those Without Category . Below them: Search payees finds a payee by name. Status : All , Active or Inactive . Default Category : All Payees , No Default Category , or Uncategorized Txns (payees that have transactions without a category). The list shows each payee's logo, Name , Default Category , transaction Count , number of Aliases , Last Used date, Created date, Status and Notes ; which columns fit depends on the width of the screen. A payee with uncategorized transactions shows how many beside its name. Click a column header to sort by it. Click a row to open the payee's detail page ; click the payee's name to see its transactions instead. Each row has Merge , Edit and Delete ( Reactivate in place of Merge for an inactive payee). The Maintenance menu beside + New Payee holds the bulk tools: Auto-Merge Payees , Deactivate Unused , Auto-Assign Categories , Apply Default Categories and Payee Lookup settings , each described below. Click + New Payee Enter the payee details: Field Description Payee Name Payee name (e.g., "Amazon", "City Hydro") Default Category Auto-assigned category for new transactions with this payee Website The payee's website (see Payee Contact Details ) Address The payee's address Email The payee's email address Phone The payee's phone number, with its country code Notes (optional) Optional notes about the payee Aliases Wildcard patterns for matching imported transaction names (see Payee Aliases ) Click Create Payee You can add aliases directly during payee creation -- there is no need to save the payee first and then edit it to add aliases. Payees can also be created inline when creating a transaction -- if you type a name that does not exist, you can create it on the fly. If the name you type belongs to a payee you deactivated, Monize offers to Reactivate it instead of creating a duplicate. Click Edit on a payee's row, or on its detail page, to change its name, default category, contact details, notes or aliases, then click Update Payee . When you set or change the default category of a payee that already has transactions, Apply this category to existing transactions lets you choose what happens to them: Don't change existing transactions , Only transactions without a category , or All transactions (each with its count). Transfers and split transactions are never changed. Click Delete on a payee's row and confirm. Only a payee that no transaction or scheduled transaction uses can be deleted; for one that is still in use, merge it into another payee, or deactivate it to hide it from the payee lists while keeping its history.

Each payee has a detail page with its history, its contact details and its aliases. Click a row on the Payees page to open it. The header shows the payee's logo and name (the logo links to its website), Inactive for a deactivated payee, and View Transactions , Merge , Edit and Deactivate (or Reactivate ). The name is also a switcher: click it to filter your payees and jump to another. Below it, the page has three tabs: Overview : Spent This Year (or Received This Year ) compared with the same period last year, the Average Transaction , the number of Transactions , the Last Transaction , the Recurring charge Monize detects (its cadence and usual amount, and whether the price went up or down), and the number of Uncategorized transactions (click it to apply the default category to them, or to set one); a chart of the monthly totals; Top Categories over the last 12 months or all time; the accounts it was Paid From ; Bills & Recurring , the pattern detected over the last 12 months and the next scheduled bill; the payee's Key Information (default category, status, first, last and largest transaction, aliases, website, address, phone, email and notes, with Look up contact details ); and its Seasonality . Transactions : every transaction with the payee, editable in place, with Open in the register . Aliases : the payee's aliases , to add or remove.

Payees show a brand logo beside their name: in the payee list, on the detail page, in the register and on warranties. Monize finds it from the payee's website , fetching the site's icon on the server and keeping a copy, so your browser never contacts the business to draw it. A payee without a website, or whose site has no usable icon, shows its initial instead.

One of the most powerful features of payees is the default category . When you assign a default category to a payee: The next time you create a transaction for that payee, the category is automatically filled in This saves time and ensures consistent categorization You can always override the default for individual transactions During import , the default category is applied automatically when the payee is matched For example, if you set "Loblaws" with a default category of "Groceries," every new transaction to Loblaws will automatically be categorized as Groceries. Maintenance > Apply Default Categories catches up on the past in one step: it categorizes every uncategorized transaction with its payee's default category, across all payees, after telling you how many transactions and payees it will change. Manually categorized transactions, transfers and split transactions are left unchanged. To fill in a category by something other than the payee (an amount, an account, a word in the description), use a rule; see Tags and Rules .

A payee can carry a website , address , email and phone number alongside its name. They appear on the payee form and on the payee's detail page, and an address is clickable -- it opens in your device's map app, or on a desktop in the map service you chose under Settings > Preferences > Map provider for addresses . Phone numbers are stored in one international form, so the same payee reads the same way whichever country you looked it up in. A number without a country code is refused with an example ( +1 206 448 8762 ). You can type them in yourself, or let Monize find them (see below).

Rather than typing a payee's contact details in, Monize can look them up for you. The lookup buttons appear once a lookup source is switched on (see Configuring the Lookup ). On the payee form (and on the transaction page when you create a new payee), click Look up details . The fields it fills in are listed under Suggested by lookup (and the ones it changed under Replaced by lookup ); Undo lookup changes puts them back. Nothing is saved until you save the form. On a payee's detail page, click Look up contact details . A Confirm contact details dialog shows each proposed value marked Add or Replace , and nothing is saved until you click Save . Where the name matches more than one business, it asks you to choose the one you pay. Monize sends the payee's name, together with any notes, website, address, email and phone it already has, so the lookup can tell the right business and the right branch apart. A lookup that fails says so, rather than reporting that nothing was found. A lookup can also run automatically when you create a new payee -- see Automatic payee contact lookup . The lookup is answered by one of two sources -- Google Places (directory facts, no email address) or an AI provider you have configured (can find an email address, costs a model call). You can reach the same settings panel from either place: Tools > Payees > Maintenance > Payee Lookup settings Settings > Payee Lookup They render the same controls, so it does not matter which you use. The full reference -- the two sources, their on/off switches, source ordering, pinning a particular AI provider, and the automatic-lookup toggle -- is on the settings page: Payee Lookup . Google Places answers a payee lookup from Google's business directory. It needs an API key from a Google Cloud project with Places API (New) enabled, restricted by IP address rather than by HTTP referrer -- Monize calls Google from the server, not from your browser. The step-by-step setup, the monthly request limit and its 1,000-request default, the server-wide GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY alternative, and troubleshooting are documented on the settings page: Setting up Google Places -- on the Settings and Security page. Once a key is saved, the Payee Lookup settings panel shows how many of this month's requests you have used. When the limit is spent, lookups fall back to your AI provider if you have one switched on; the payee form says so directly -- "This month's Google Places lookups are used up. Raise the limit in Payee lookup settings, or wait until next month."

Payee aliases let you map multiple variations of a payee name to a single canonical payee. This is especially useful for imported transactions, where banks often append location codes, reference numbers, or other suffixes to payee names. When a transaction is imported (via CSV, OFX/QFX, or QIF), Monize resolves the payee name in this order: Exact name match -- If a payee with the same name exists, use it Alias match -- If a payee alias pattern matches the imported name, use the canonical payee Create new -- If no match is found, create a new payee When an alias matches, the transaction is assigned to the alias's parent payee, and that payee's default category is applied. Aliases are managed in the Aliases section of the payee form, or on the Aliases tab of the payee's detail page: Navigate to Tools > Payees Click Edit on a payee (or open the payee and choose the Aliases tab) In the Aliases section, type a pattern and click Add (or press Enter) Aliases support the * wildcard character, which matches zero or more characters. Matching is case-insensitive. Pattern Matches Does Not Match STARBUCKS* "STARBUCKS", "STARBUCKS #1234", "STARBUCKS MAIN ST" "MY STARBUCKS" *Amazon* "Amazon", "Amazon AWS", "Pay Amazon" -- SHELL*STATION "Shell Fuel Station", "SHELL GAS STATION #45" "Shell" Tim Hortons "Tim Hortons" (exact, case-insensitive) "Tim Hortons #1234" Tip Set up aliases for your most common payees before importing transactions. For example, create a "Starbucks" payee with alias STARBUCKS* to catch all Starbucks locations in your bank file. Aliases are displayed alphabetically below the alias input field Click Remove next to any alias to delete it Each payee can have multiple aliases, and one alias belongs to only one payee

If you have duplicate payees (e.g., "Amazon" and "Amazon.com"), you can merge them to consolidate all transactions under a single payee. Navigate to Tools > Payees Click Merge on the payee you want to eliminate (or Merge on its detail page) In the Merge Payee dialog: The payee being merged away is shown under Merge from (will be deleted) , with how many transactions will move Select the payee to keep under Merge into (target payee) Leave Add "..." as an alias on the target payee ticked (the default) so future imports with the old name match the payee you keep The dialog lists what will happen under This will: Click Merge Payee Action Detail Transactions reassigned All transactions from the source payee are moved to the target payee Scheduled transactions reassigned All scheduled transactions from the source are moved to the target Alias created (optional) The source payee's name is added as an alias on the target payee Source deleted The source payee and all its aliases are permanently deleted Example: You have "Tim Hortons" (50 transactions) and "TIM HORTONS #1234" (3 transactions). Merge "TIM HORTONS #1234" into "Tim Hortons" with the alias option ticked. Result: "Tim Hortons" now has 53 transactions and an alias TIM HORTONS #1234 that will catch future imports with that name. Only an active payee can be merged; reactivate an inactive one first.

While Merging Payees handles duplicates one at a time, Auto-Merge is a bulk tool that scans your entire payee list and groups the name variants that build on one another (for example "Lidl", "LIDL sp. z o.o." and "LIDL WARSZAWA 0421") so you can consolidate them all in a single pass. Payees that merely share a common word (like "Royal Electric" and "Royal City Nursery") are kept apart. Choose Maintenance > Auto-Merge Payees on the Payees page Configure how the scan finds groups: Setting Description Minimum Group Size The smallest number of payees a group must contain to be suggested (2 to 10, default 2) Similarity Threshold Spelling tolerance: lower it to also group near-matches like LIDL / LIDI; 100% requires an exact keyword match (50% to 100%, default 85%) Minimum Keyword Length Keywords shorter than this are ignored when grouping (2 to 6, default 3) Include inactive payees When on, deactivated payees are included in the scan Only merge payees in the same category Keeps payees apart when their categories differ, at the Category or Subcategory level, to reduce false matches Ignore common words Does not anchor groups on generic words (Restaurant, Cafe, country names) or on a leading word many different payees start with; Common-word sensitivity sets how many variants make a word common Click Preview Groups to see the suggested groups Tip Auto-Merge makes sweeping changes across many payees at once. The dialog recommends creating a backup first, so you can roll back if a group merges more than you intended. Groups start de-selected, so you opt in to each merge deliberately. For every group you want to apply: Tick Include this group Choose which payee to keep ( Keep this payee ); the rest are merged into it Optionally untick individual members you do not want merged ( Include in merge ) Edit the name to Keep as payee and the Alias for future imports (a wildcard such as *LIDL* ) if you wish Pick a Default category (optional) for the resulting payee Optionally tick Also categorize N existing uncategorized transactions to back-fill that category Click Merge N Groups . Each selected group is merged into its chosen payee, the alias is created, and the default category (and optional back-fill) is applied. Groups are merged independently, so if one group fails (for example an alias is already in use) the rest still succeed, and you are told exactly what conflicted.

Over time, you may accumulate payees that are no longer relevant. Rather than deleting them, you can deactivate them. Deactivated payees are hidden from the payee dropdowns but remain on existing transactions. Choose Maintenance > Deactivate Unused on the Payees page Configure the criteria: N or fewer transactions -- Include payees with this many transactions or fewer (0-20, default 3) Last used more than ... ago -- Include payees not used since this long ago, or never used (6-120 months, default 12) Click Preview Unused Payees to see candidates Review the list, which shows each payee's name, transaction count, and last used date (or Never used ) Use Select all / Select none or tick individual payees Click Deactivate N Payees A single payee can also be deactivated with Deactivate on its detail page. To reactivate a deactivated payee: Set the payee list's Status filter to Inactive Click Reactivate on the payee's row The payee is active again straight away. You can also click Reactivate on its detail page, or type its name in a transaction, where Monize offers to reactivate it.

Monize can analyze your transaction history to suggest default categories for payees. Choose Maintenance > Auto-Assign Categories on the Payees page Configure the criteria: Minimum Transactions -- Only consider payees with at least this many transactions (1-50, default 10) Category Match Percentage -- The category must be used in at least this percentage of the payee's transactions (50-100%, default 75%) Only payees without a default category -- On by default Click Preview Suggestions to see candidates Each suggestion shows the payee name, suggested category, and match percentage (colour-coded: green for 90%+, blue for 75%+, yellow for below 75%) Select the suggestions you want to apply Optionally tick Also categorize N existing uncategorized transactions to apply the chosen categories to the selected payees' uncategorized transactions; without it, the category only affects new transactions going forward Click Apply to N Payees

When typing a payee name in the transaction form, Monize suggests existing payees matching your typed text, with the payees you use most and most recently first. Inactive payees are left out. This makes data entry faster and more consistent. The payee list's Last Used column shows the date of each payee's most recent transaction, making it easy to identify stale payees.

Sort preferences on the Payees, Categories, Tags, Currencies, and Securities pages are saved in your browser. Your chosen sort column and direction persist between visits so you do not need to re-sort each time you open the page.

Tags provide a flexible, cross-cutting way to label and organize your transactions. Unlike categories (which assign a single classification per transaction), tags let you apply multiple labels to any transaction or split -- making it easy to track concepts that span categories.

Tags are user-defined labels with an optional colour and icon. They complement categories by allowing you to group transactions across different categories and accounts. Example use cases: Tag Purpose Vacation 2026 Track all spending on a specific trip across dining, travel, lodging Tax Deductible Flag deductible expenses across multiple categories Reimbursable Mark work expenses to be submitted for reimbursement Home Renovation Group project costs across hardware, labour, permits trip:Lisbon A key:value tag : one value of the trip key Each tag has: Property Description Name The tag label (unique per user, case-insensitive) Colour Optional colour for visual identification in lists and filters Icon Optional icon shown beside the name Tags can be put on transactions, on the lines of a split transaction, on scheduled transactions and on securities.

Navigate to Tools > Tags to access the tag management page. Three cards at the top count your Total Tags , the Tags with Colour and the Tags with Icon . Search tags... narrows the list by name. The list shows each tag's Name with its colour, its Icon and the number of Transactions that carry it; click a column header to sort by it. Click a tag's name to see its transactions on the Transactions page; click anywhere else on the row to edit it. Edit and Delete are at the end of each row (on a phone, press and hold the row, or right-click it).

Click + New Tag Fill in the tag form: Field Required Description Tag Name Yes Tag label (1-100 characters, must be unique) Colour No Red , Orange , Yellow , Green , Teal , Blue , Purple , Pink or Grey , or No colour Icon No Choose an icon for visual identification Click Create Tag
Click Edit on a tag's row (or the row itself) to modify its name, colour, or icon, then click Update Tag . Renaming a tag updates it on all associated transactions.

Click Delete on a tag's row and confirm. When the tag is in use, the confirmation says on how many transactions; the tag is removed from them, and the transactions themselves are not otherwise affected.

Open the transaction form (create new or edit existing) In the Tags field, select one or more tags from the dropdown. The tags you used most recently are listed first. Save the transaction Tags appear as coloured chips in the transaction form, showing the tag name and its colour, and as chips on the transaction's row in the register.

When a transaction is split across multiple categories, each split row can have its own set of tags. This allows fine-grained tagging -- for example, tagging only the business portion of a mixed-use purchase as "Reimbursable." Open the split editor Each split row has its own Tags dropdown Select tags for individual splits as needed

If you need a new tag while entering a transaction, you can create one without leaving the form: In the Tags dropdown, click Create new tag... Enter the tag name, optional colour, and icon Save the tag -- it is immediately available and selected The same is possible in the scheduled transaction form and the security form.
Select several transactions on the Transactions page and use the bulk update to give all of them the same tags in one step. The bulk update replaces the tags the transactions had; see Transactions .

Scheduled transactions (bills and deposits) support tags. When a scheduled transaction is auto-posted or manually posted, the tags are carried over to the created transaction. Open a scheduled transaction form Select tags in the Tags field When the transaction is posted, the tags are applied automatically This is useful for tagging recurring transactions -- for example, tagging a monthly gym membership as "Health" without needing to remember to tag each posted occurrence.

Rules ( Tools > Rules ) fill in tags, categories and payees automatically when a transaction is created or imported. A rule has three parts: When it runs (a transaction is created, imported, or both), If the transaction matches its conditions (payee, amount, account, day of the month, description, tags and more), and Then what it changes. Tags take part on both sides of a rule: Add tags and Remove tags are actions: for example, a rule that adds Coffee run to every transaction with Tim Hortons or Starbucks. Tags is a condition, with has any of , has all of and has none of : for example, a rule that sets a category on every transaction tagged Reimbursable . Other actions set the category, the payee or the description, or ask for an AI review; a rule never changes an amount or moves money. The editor's Test rule lists the existing transactions the conditions match before you save, and Run on existing transactions applies a saved rule to the transactions you already have, with an undo. Rules run in the order of the list, and Stop processing other rules keeps the later ones from touching a transaction this rule matched. A rule that uses a tag you later delete is marked invalid until you repair it.

Tags understand a key:value naming convention. Name a tag country:poland , strategy:dividend , or account-owner:sam and Monize treats the part before the colon as a key and the part after as its value . There is no migration and no separate data model -- it is simply a convention parsed from the tag name, so any tag you name this way works immediately, and tags without a colon behave exactly as before. Grouping tags under a shared key lets you slice your data by that key's values -- for example, tag several securities country:poland , country:canada , and country:usa , then chart how your portfolio splits across countries.

On the Investments page, the Asset Allocation chart gains a By key grouping mode when your holdings carry key:value tags. Pick a key (e.g. country or strategy ) and the chart shows your portfolio's value-weighted split across that key's values , with holdings that lack the key rolled into an untagged band.

The transactions filter panel can match on a tag key rather than a specific tag. Choose the Tag key (or Any (no key filter) ), then a Condition : Condition Matches Has a value Any tag with that key, whatever its value Has no value Transactions with no tag using that key Value contains The key's value contains the text you type Value does not contain The key's value does not contain the text you type Key filters cover split rows too, so a split line tagged project:reno is found the same way a whole transaction would be.

Income vs Expenses and Cash Flow offer Break down by tag key : pick a key and the report shows a figure for each of its values, plus Untagged . With Include tagged transfers , transfers that carry the key (for example money drawn from a savings account for a trip) appear as their own figure, never counted as income or expenses. A row tagged with more than one value under the key counts toward each of them, so per-value shares can add up to more than 100%. On a category's detail page , the Tag Breakdown panel splits the category's spending by the values of a key you choose.
Tags integrate with the transaction filter panel, letting you find all transactions with specific tags.

Open the Filters panel on the Transactions page In the Tags filter, select one or more tags The transaction list updates to show only transactions (or splits) matching the selected tags Tag filters work alongside other filters (accounts, categories, payees, date range, search). Active tag filters appear as coloured chips above the transaction list for easy visibility. The search box understands tags too: tag:lisbon finds transactions with a tag whose name contains "lisbon", and has:tag finds the transactions that carry any tag.

On desktop, tags displayed on transaction rows are clickable. Click a tag directly in the transaction list to instantly filter the list to all transactions with that tag. On mobile, tap a transaction and select the tag from the action sheet to apply the same filter.

Tags can be used in custom reports : filter a report to transactions with chosen tags, group it by Tag , or show a Tag column -- for example, total spending tagged "Vacation 2026" broken down by category. Several built-in reports, among them Spending by Category, Income by Source and Budget vs Actual, can also count tagged transfers as available funds.

Rules fill in your transactions for you. A rule watches the transactions you create and the ones you import, and when one matches its conditions it sets the category, the payee or the description, adds or removes tags, asks for an AI review, or reshapes the transaction into a transfer or a split. You can test a rule on your existing transactions before you save it, and run a saved rule over the transactions you already have, with an undo.

Every rule has three parts, the same three sections you see in the rule editor: Part What it decides When Which transactions the rule looks at: the ones you create, the ones you import, or both, optionally only those dated inside a window If The conditions a transaction must meet: its payee, amount, account, category, description, tags, date and more Then What the rule changes on a transaction that matches, in order Some examples: Rule If Then Coffee runs Payee is any of Tim Hortons, Starbucks Set the category to Coffee Shops (only if empty), add the Coffee run tag Costco receipts Payee text as received matches the pattern *costco* Set the payee to Costco, set the category to Groceries Dinners out over $100 Category is Restaurants and Amount (ignoring sign) is at least 100 Add the Date night tag A rule fills in; by default it does not overwrite. Set the category , Set the payee and Set the payee from text start with Only if empty switched on, so a category you typed yourself, or one that came from the payee's default category, is kept.

Open Tools > Rules . The list shows your rules in the order they run, one row each, with its Order , an Enabled switch, the rule's name and a Summary of when it runs and how many conditions and actions it has. A switched-off rule is shown dimmed and does nothing until you switch it on again. Click a row, or Edit , to open the rule. Create rule starts a new one; with no rules yet the page offers Create your first rule instead. The menu at the end of each row (on a phone, press and hold the row) holds the other actions: Action What it does Duplicate Makes a copy named " name (copy)". The copy is switched off until you enable it, so the two do not both run Run on existing transactions Applies the saved rule to transactions you already have; see Running a Rule on Existing Transactions Move up , Move down Changes where the rule runs in the list Delete Deletes the rule after you confirm. Transactions it already changed stay as they are

A rule that can no longer run is marked Invalid , and hovering the mark says why: a tag, payee, category or account it uses no longer exists, it has no actions, or its definition is otherwise not valid. An invalid rule is skipped until you open it, repair it and save it; it cannot be run on existing transactions meanwhile.

A rule runs once on each new transaction, at the moment it is written: Trigger Covers A transaction is created Transactions and transfers you enter, transactions posted from a scheduled bill or deposit (by hand or automatically), and those the AI assistant or an MCP client create for you A transaction is imported CSV, OFX/QFX and QIF imports, a Microsoft Money import, and transactions arriving through Bank Sync Editing a transaction later does not run the rules again, and neither does anything a rule changes: each transaction gets one pass. Restoring a backup, undoing or redoing a change, and the cash side of an investment transaction do not run them either. To apply a rule to transactions that already exist, run it on them (see Running a Rule on Existing Transactions ).

Rules run in the order of the list, top to bottom. A later rule sees what the earlier ones changed: if the first rule sets the category, a later rule's Category condition reads that category. Use Move up and Move down to put the rule that should decide first at the top. When a rule has Stop processing other rules switched on and it matches a transaction, the rules after it in the list are skipped for that transaction.

h: Rules and the Payee's Default Category
x: On a new transaction, the values you typed come first, then the payee's default category, then the rules in order. With Only if empty on, a rule fills a category or payee only when the transaction has none at that point; with it off, the rule replaces whatever is there. See Categories and Payees for default categories.

Click Create rule , or open an existing rule. The editor shows the rule's Name and a Rule enabled switch, then the When , If and Then sections, the Test panel and, for a saved rule, its History . Nothing is stored until you click Save rule ; Cancel leaves without saving.

Option Description A transaction is created Run on transactions you create. At least one of the two stays selected A transaction is imported Run on imported and bank-synced transactions Stop processing other rules When this rule matches, the rules after it are skipped for that transaction Active between A First date and a Last date . The rule only applies to transactions dated inside this window: when they are created or imported, and when the rule is tested or run. Leave a date empty for no limit The window is useful for a rule that should not reach back into older, already reconciled history: give it a First date and a later run on existing transactions leaves everything before it alone.

The conditions are a group of cards. Each condition picks a Field , an Operator and a Value ; + Add condition adds one. At the top of the group, All of these means every condition must hold and Any of these means one is enough. + Add group puts a group inside the group, with its own All of these or Any of these , so you can write "this and that, and either of these two". Negate Group turns a group around: it matches when its conditions do not. A rule with no conditions applies to every transaction, and the editor warns you about it. Field Operators Notes Account is, is not, is any of, is none of The account the transaction is in From account (transfers) , To account (transfers) is, is not, is any of, is none of, is empty Set only on a transfer; empty on anything else Type is, is not, is any of Expense , Income or Transfer , from what the transaction is rather than from the account Payee is, is not, is any of, is none of, is empty The payee after alias matching Payee text as received is, contains, starts with, matches the pattern, is empty The payee text exactly as the file or the bank sent it, or as you typed it, before alias matching Category is, is not, is any of, is none of, is empty, is in, or under "is in, or under" includes the subcategories Description is, contains, starts with, matches the pattern, is empty Amount (with sign) is, is less than, is at most, is greater than, is at least, is between Negative for money going out Amount (ignoring sign) is less than, is at most, is greater than, is at least, is between So "at least 100" does not depend on the direction Currency is, is any of The account's currency Tags has any of, has all of, has none of The tags the transaction has when the rule runs, including those added by an earlier rule Has splits is Yes or No Reference number is, contains, starts with, matches the pattern, is empty The cheque or reference number Day of the month is, is less than, is at most, is greater than, is at least, is between, is any of 1 to 31 Day of the week is, is any of Monday to Sunday Status is, is not, is any of Unreconciled, cleared, reconciled or void Has an attachment is Yes or No Date is, is less than, is at most, is greater than, is at least, is between The transaction's date Text comparisons ignore case and the spaces at either end. A field that does not apply to a transaction (the from-account of something that is not a transfer) only ever matches is empty . A group can be nested up to four levels deep, and a rule can hold up to 50 conditions. matches the pattern compares the whole text against a pattern in which * stands for any text: *coffee* matches any text containing "coffee", while coffee without a star matches only the text "coffee" itself. Regular expressions are not supported, and the editor refuses a pattern that looks like one; to match one of several texts, use a group of Any of these with one condition for each. A pattern can also keep part of the text for the actions: put a name in braces where the text should be kept, for example *PRINCIPAL: {principal} INTEREST: {interest}* . A name is lowercase letters and digits, starting with a letter, and a pattern can keep up to five. The text actions can then use {principal} as a placeholder, and a split can use it as the amount of a part. Visual and Expression at the top of the If section switch between the cards and the same conditions written as text, for example transaction.absAmount >= 50 && (transaction.weekday in ["FRI", "SAT"] || transaction.tagIds.hasAny([tag("Date night")])) . Both views edit the same conditions. In the expression, && means all of these, || any of these and !( ... ) not; items are written by name, such as payee("Tim Hortons") or category("Food: Restaurants") . A list of Suggestions under the box offers the fields, operators and names that fit where you are typing. While the text has a mistake, the editor names the line and column, and you cannot save or switch back to Visual until it is fixed.

+ Add action adds an action card; pick its Action type and fill in what it needs. The actions run in the order shown, and each card's menu can duplicate it, move it up or down, or delete it. A rule needs at least one action and can have up to ten. Action What it does Add tags Adds the chosen tags; the transaction's other tags are kept Remove tags Removes the chosen tags if the transaction has them Set the category Sets the category. Not applied to a transfer, which has no category, or to a split transaction, whose categories belong to its lines Set the payee Sets the payee to one of your payees Set the payee from text Builds a payee name from placeholders and sets the payee with that name. With Create the payee if it does not exist , a new payee is created when no payee matches the name (by name, alias or a close match) Set the description Writes a description built from placeholders. Description Mode is Replace the description , Add after the description or Add before the description Convert to transfer Turns a matched expense into a transfer to another account, or a matched income into a transfer from one ( Direction ). The other account must use the same currency. Clear the category removes the category the transaction had Split transaction Turns the transaction into a split; see Splits from the Bank's Text Settle a loan installment Books a bank debit as the installment of a mortgage or loan; see Settling a Loan Installment Ask for an AI review Puts the transaction in the AI > AI Review Inbox with your Review Instructions , for example "split this purchase by the receipt". The rule changes nothing itself; a person approves any change the AI proposes Set the category , Set the payee , Set the payee from text and Set the description have the Only if empty switch: on, the rule fills the field only when the transaction has none; off, it replaces it. The text in Set the payee from text and Set the description is plain text with placeholders in braces, which you can insert from the Placeholders list under the box: {payeeText} is the payee text as received, {description} is the description as it stands when the action runs, and the other placeholders are the captures named in the rule's patterns. With Add after the description and Add before the description , the text is joined exactly as written, so include any space or separator you want. A rule can hold one Ask for an AI review , and one of Convert to transfer , Split transaction and Settle a loan installment , which cannot be combined with Set the category . Split transaction is for a bank line that names its own parts, such as a loan payment the bank describes as PRINCIPAL: 1200,50 INTEREST: 300,25 . In If, add a condition on the payee text or the description with matches the pattern , capturing each amount ( *PRINCIPAL: {principal} INTEREST: {interest}* ). In the action, each part takes its Amount from a capture, or The rest , and goes either to a Category or, as a Transfer , to an Account , with an optional Memo ; Payee of the transaction (optional) sets the payee of the whole transaction. A split has 2 to 10 parts, and they must add up to the transaction's amount; otherwise the rule leaves the transaction alone. The card's How to use this guide walks through this example. Settle a loan installment is for a bank debit that pays a mortgage or loan installment as one amount. Choose the Loan account and how many Days before the due date and Days after the due date the bank may take the payment. A matched debit pays the installment due in that window: it becomes a split, with the principal transferred to the loan account and the interest booked to the loan's interest category (or the Interest category you choose), both priced by Monize for that installment. Debit Above the Installment and Debit Below the Installment decide what happens when the amounts differ by more than a few cents: pay the difference as extra principal, pay the interest first, or leave the transaction alone. Turn off automatic posting on the loan's scheduled payment so the installment is not paid twice; the editor warns you when it is on. The Payment matching option on a mortgage or loan creates a rule like this for you; see Payment Matching .
The editor can show what a rule would do before you save it. Neither test changes anything.

Test rule at the bottom of the If section lists your existing transactions that the conditions match, inside the rule's Active between window, ten to a page, in the same list as the Transactions page. It looks only at the conditions, so it works before you have added an action.

h: The Test Panel: What Would Change
x: The Test panel below the actions tries the whole rule, saved or not, on your existing transactions. Choose the Accounts (all by default), a From and To date, and how many of the Newest transactions to examine (200 by default, up to 1,000), then click Test rule . The result says how many transactions would change out of how many were examined, lists each one with its Planned change , and lists the transactions the rule would leave alone with the reason (for example, it is a transfer, which has no category). When the dates hold more transactions than the number examined, the result says so: only the newest are included, so raise the number or narrow the dates to reach older ones. When you change the rule or the filters after a test, the result stays on screen but is marked out of date until you test again. If the last test found that the rule matches none of the transactions examined, the editor says so beside Save rule ; a common cause is a pattern without * , which matches only the whole text.

h: Running a Rule on Existing Transactions
x: A saved rule can be applied to the transactions you already have: choose Run on existing transactions in its row's menu on the Rules page, or click Run on existing transactions in the editor (save your changes first). Choose the Accounts , the From and To dates and how many of the Newest transactions to examine . Click Preview . The dialog lists every transaction the rule would change and how, and the ones it would leave alone with the reason. Nothing has changed yet. Click Confirm and run to apply exactly what the preview showed. If your transactions or the rule changed between the preview and the confirmation, nothing is written and the dialog shows a new preview to confirm instead. A run can be undone as one step from the action history; see Undo and Redo . A run that only queued AI reviews has nothing to undo. A run leaves some transactions alone and says why: a transfer has no category to set, a split's categories belong to its lines, and with Lock reconciled transactions on (see Settings ) a reconciled transaction is not changed. The rule's Active between window applies to a run too.

The History section of a saved rule lists the latest transactions it changed, newest first: each one's Date , Payee and Amount , the Source of the change ( Created , Imported or Manual run ), the Change it made and when it was Applied . View opens the transaction on the Transactions page. The history keeps the latest 50 changes and holds them for a year.

Imports. Rules set to run on import apply to every imported transaction; they see the payee text as it was in the file. See Importing Transactions . Bank Sync preview. Expanding a row in the preview of a bank account's first sync shows which of your import rules match it and what they would change. See Previewing and Syncing . Tags. See Tags and Rules for rules that add, remove and test tags. The AI assistant. The assistant and MCP clients can list, create, change, test and run rules for you, always with a confirmation. See Making Changes . Tip Start a new rule with Only if empty on and test it on your existing transactions first. When the Test panel shows what you expect, save it, then run it on your history if you want the older transactions to match.

Navigate to Reports from the top navigation bar. The Reports page lists every built-in report and every custom report you have saved, each as a card with its category, name, and a one-line description. Click a card to open the report. Search reports by name or description... -- narrows the list as you type Category -- buttons for All Reports and each category, each with the number of reports in it. Monize remembers the category you picked Density -- the button showing Normal , Compact , or Dense cycles between three layouts; Dense shows the reports as a table. On a phone the reports are a two-column grid of tiles New Report -- create a custom report (see Custom Report Builder )

A report that needs data you do not have yet -- an investment account, a budget, a loan -- opens with a message saying so.

Every report page has a Back to Reports link and, beside its title, an arrow ( Switch to another report ) that opens a searchable list of every report -- your favourites first, then each category -- so you can move between reports without going back to the list.

Most reports have a row of range buttons above the chart. Each report offers the ranges that suit it, from 1D , 1W , MTD , and 1M through 3M , 6M , YTD , 1Y , 2Y , 5Y , and 10Y to All Time . Many also have Custom , which shows Start Date and End Date fields for any range you like.
Reports that can be limited to some of your accounts have an accounts selector. Monize remembers your selection for each report between visits.

You can click most data points -- a bar, a pie segment, a Sankey flow, or a table row -- to open the Transactions page with filters pre-applied, so you can drill down from a summary to the transactions behind it. A payee opens exactly that payee's transactions. On the Income vs Expenses report, clicking an income or expense bar filters by the corresponding category type (income categories or expense categories), so you see exactly the transactions that contributed to that bar.

When a figure cannot be worked out completely -- for example an amount in a currency with no exchange rate -- the report says which figures are partial and what is missing (such as the currency to add a rate for on the Currencies page) instead of showing a wrong total.

Report Description Spending by Category See where your money goes with a breakdown of expenses by category over time Spending by Payee Track how much you spend with each merchant or vendor over time Monthly Spending Trend View your spending patterns month over month to identify trends Monthly Breakdown Expense and income by category, month by month, with subtotals, a total, and an average per month. Switches turn on Include current month , Show percentages , and Highlight deviations (months well above or below the category's average). Choose a key in Break down by tag key (for example project ) and the report adds a breakdown with a tab for each of the key's values (and one for untagged rows), showing that value's income, expenses, tagged inflows and outflows, Balance , and Balance % . Tick Include tagged transfers to count transfers that carry the tag as well. Spending by Category , Income by Source , Budget vs Actual , and Monthly Breakdown can instead focus on a single Tag value : they then show the Available funds for that value (its income plus the transfers tagged with it) next to what was spent.

The Bar style switch shows each month as one Net worth bar or stacked By account type Account Balances See what every account was worth on any date you pick ( Balance as of ), grouped by assets and liabilities, account type, institution, open or closed, or favourite, and sorted by name or balance. Pick the Year to show. Until you have set up a payroll deduction rule, it offers Open Payroll Deductions

Report Description Debt Payoff Timeline Visualize your debt reduction progress with projections for payoff dates. Shows balance over time with historical payments and projected payoff, payment breakdowns (principal vs interest), and summary metrics including estimated payoff date. Supports multiple payment frequencies and Canadian mortgage calculations. Loan Amortization Schedule Detailed payment schedules for mortgages and loans with principal vs interest breakdown for each payment period Credit Utilization See how much of your available credit you are using across credit cards and lines of credit. Loan Overpayment Simulator Pick a loan and model extra payments to see how much sooner it would be paid off and how much interest you would save. Includes an account selector across all your debt accounts and mirrors the loan detail page's simulator (rendering the revolving view for a line of credit). Note: The debt and loan reports work with Loan, Mortgage, and Line of Credit accounts; Credit Utilization also covers credit cards. Beyond the reports above, each loan, mortgage, and line of credit has a dedicated account detail page with interactive planning tools. (The Loan Overpayment Simulator report embeds these same tools with an account selector.) Tool What it does Overpayment Simulator Model extra payments and see how much sooner the loan would be paid off and how much interest you would save. Supports a recurring extra payment (with optional start and end dates, at a chosen frequency) plus up to 50 one-off lump sums, and surfaces a detected-extra-principal hint from your payment history that you can apply with one click. A payoff timeline chart compares the baseline projection against your overpayment scenario. Simulations never change your scheduled payments. Goal-Seek Work backwards from a target instead of guessing an amount. Choose "save $X of interest" or "be paid off by this month" , and the simulator solves for the recurring extra payment that hits it -- the solved amount drops straight into the simulator so the schedule, chart, and savings cards all recompute at once. Targets already met report zero needed; unreachable targets say so. Saved Scenarios Save and name overpayment scenarios per loan so you can revisit and compare different payoff plans over time. Scenarios can be loaded (click a row), renamed, and deleted. Once you have saved more than one, a scenario comparison chart draws each as an arc from today to its payoff date, its height being the interest it saves versus paying the minimum (narrower and taller is better) -- with an interactive legend and a tooltip reporting each scenario's real interest saved and payoff date. The panel exports CSV and a PDF report (headline cards, the chart, and the comparison table). Impact of Overpayments Made A past-impact section showing how the payments you have already made compare to the original contractual schedule -- extra principal already paid, time already saved, and interest already saved. Rate History Track interest-rate changes over the life of the loan. Add, edit, and delete rate changes with an effective date; when a rate changes you can keep the current payment (shifting the payoff timeline), set a new payment amount, or recalculate the payment to stay on schedule. A Detect button infers past rate changes from your payment history -- including loans where the bank books interest separately from principal -- and entries are badged as Manual , Inferred , or Initial . Detection is non-destructive : your account's own rate and payment are set only in the edit form and are never silently overwritten, and when a rate change would affect a linked scheduled payment, Monize shows a before/after preview and asks permission first. Exports: The Loan Schedule, Rate History, and scenario comparison export to CSV from the loan detail page, and the payoff comparison chart exports to PNG .

Monize includes 13 investment reports for comprehensive portfolio analysis. Report Description Investment Performance Track portfolio returns, gains/losses, and asset allocation over time. Shows current portfolio value, cost basis, total gain/loss, and return percentage with holdings and allocation views. Gains, Dividends & Interest Track capital gains and losses (realized and unrealized) alongside dividend and interest income, by month, by day, or by security Sector Weightings Analyze portfolio sector exposure from individual stocks and ETFs, with drill-down showing direct stock vs ETF exposure per sector Realized Gains & Losses Track realized gains and losses from sold securities for tax planning and performance review, with proceeds, cost basis, and transaction counts Portfolio Value Over Time Visualize total investment portfolio value with historical trends, period returns, and portfolio breakdown. Offers a Total view and a By-security stacked-area view (each holding plus a cash band and a rolled-up "other securities" band), a per-security table view , CSV export , and works across intraday 1D/1W/1M ranges as well as longer periods. Like the Investments page chart, it separates the Value Change from the Investment Result , which leaves out your deposits and withdrawals. Investment Transaction History Complete history of all investment transactions with filtering by action type (buy, sell, dividend, etc.), account, and date Security Type Allocation View portfolio allocation by asset type (stocks, ETFs, mutual funds, bonds) with drill-down into individual holdings Geographic/Exchange Allocation Analyze portfolio geographic exposure by region, by exchange, or by country (looking through funds to their holdings), with bar chart and pie chart views Dividend Yield & Growth Track portfolio dividend yield, per-security yields, year-over-year growth, and payment frequency analysis Security Performance Deep dive into a single security with price history chart (including buy/sell markers), transaction history, and dividend history. You can also select multiple securities and market indexes (such as the S&P 500 or the S&P/TSX Composite) to compare , or switch to an All securities view that draws every active security's cumulative percent return on one chart -- each rebased to 0% at its first available price, so holdings at different price levels and currencies share a single axis. The comparison chart exports to PDF , and the report supports account-type and text filters. Currency Exposure Understand currency risk with portfolio allocation by currency, showing native and converted values with exchange rate details Monte Carlo Simulation Project future portfolio outcomes with thousands of randomized return paths and a saved-scenario library (see below) GEM Strategy Track the Global Equities Momentum signal, why it changed, and whether your portfolio matches it (see below) Investment reports have a Refresh button beside the export button to fetch the latest security prices first. The Monte Carlo report projects how a portfolio could grow (and be drawn down) by running thousands of randomized market paths. Pick a saved scenario from the Scenarios list, or click New Fill in the scenario inputs: Scenario name and the Investment accounts to model Starting value , or tick Use current balance on each run to start from the accounts' value Contribution phase -- Years , Annual contribution , and Contribution growth Withdrawal phase -- Years , Annual withdrawal (in today's money, grown with inflation), and an optional Target (today's value) Additional cash flows -- + Add cash flow for one-time or recurring inflows and outflows, such as a pension or a home purchase, optionally adjusted for inflation Return assumptions -- Specify expected return (with Expected return and Volatility ), or Use historical returns from selected accounts ; plus Inflation and the number of Simulations Click Run simulation The results show the Median final value, the 10th–90th percentile range, the Probability of Depletion , and, with a target, the Probability Above Target , over a fan chart of the projected portfolio value (switch to Table for the figures by year) and a Performance Summary . Tick Show in today's value to adjust for inflation. Click Save scenario to keep the inputs, or Save as... to keep them under a new name. After a run, Edit inputs reopens the inputs and Run again reruns the scenario. To compare scenarios, click Compare under the Scenarios list, tick two to four scenarios, and click Compare selected : the comparison page runs them side by side and offers Download CSV . The GEM Strategy report follows the Global Equities Momentum strategy: at each evaluation it compares the 12-month returns of US equities (the S&P 500), developed markets outside the US, emerging markets, and a safe asset, and names the one asset to hold. Assign an instrument to each role and one or more of your investment accounts in Settings ; the tabs then show the Overview (the current signal, your portfolio against it, and what to transfer), the Signals history, My portfolio , and a Backtest . You can keep several scenarios and switch between them. A change of signal can also send you a notification.

PDFs embed a Roboto font subset so non-Western text -- Polish, Cyrillic, Greek, and currency symbols -- renders correctly, and chart images are compressed so files stay small.

Mark frequently used reports as favourites for quick access: On the Reports page, click the star ( Add to favourites ) on a report Favourite reports appear first in the list, and at the top of the report switcher Favourites are saved to your account, so they follow you to every device, and the Dashboard's Favourite Reports widget lists them.

Open a custom report and click Edit at the top right. The builder opens with the report's settings; click Update Report to save. Built-in reports cannot be edited, but you can create a custom report with similar parameters if you need a variation.
Open the custom report, click Edit , then Delete Report , and confirm. Built-in reports cannot be deleted.

Monize supports multiple currencies for international users or anyone with accounts, securities, or purchases in different currencies. Every figure is converted to your home currency at the exchange rate for its own date.

Monize knows every ISO 4217 currency. You choose which ones you use: your home currency when you first sign in, and any others you add from the Currencies page, from the transaction form, or through an import. A currency you have not added stays out of your lists.

Navigate to Tools > Currencies to view and manage your currencies. The page shows the number of Total Currencies , Active , and Inactive , a search box, and an All / Active / Inactive filter. A line under the buttons names where the exchange rates come from. Each row shows: Column Description Code The three-letter currency code. Your home currency is marked Default Name The currency's name Symbol The symbol shown with amounts, such as $, €, or £ Decimals How many decimal places amounts in this currency have (2 for most, 0 for the yen) Usage How many of your accounts and securities use the currency Rate What one unit of the currency is worth in your home currency, from the latest stored rate (N/A when none is stored yet) Status Active or Inactive Actions Rate history , Edit (for currencies you created), Deactivate / Activate , and Delete A currency that is in use, and your home currency, cannot be deactivated or deleted. Deactivating a currency hides it from the currency lists without deleting it.

Click + New Currency Type the Currency Code (for example SEK ) or its name, and click Lookup to fill in the Name , Symbol , and Decimal Places Check the details and click Create Currency If the code is already in your list but inactive, the form offers Reactivate instead. You can also add a currency without leaving a transaction: the transaction form's currency picker has Add currency... .

Your home currency (the Default Currency ) is the primary currency used for: Dashboard totals -- All account balances are converted to your home currency Net worth calculations -- All assets and liabilities are expressed in your home currency Reports -- Financial reports use your home currency for aggregation Portfolio totals -- Holdings in other currencies are converted for the Investments page totals You choose it when you first sign in, and can change it at any time in Settings > Preferences under Default Currency . The Rate column on the Currencies page then shows every rate against the new home currency.

Monize fetches the latest exchange rates for the currencies you use every weekday at 5:05 PM New York time, after the markets close, and stores them so that every past date keeps its own rate. Click Refresh Rates on the Currencies page to fetch them immediately; the button shows how long ago the rates were last updated. Rates come from Frankfurter (the European Central Bank's reference rates) first, then Yahoo Finance for any currency Frankfurter does not cover. An administrator can change the providers and their order for the whole instance.

Click Rate history on a currency's row to see the rates Monize holds for it against your home currency: Stored history -- the first and last dates stored, and the number of observations Fill gaps in rate history -- fetches the daily rates your reports are missing, from the first date your data uses the currency up to today Stored rates -- every stored rate, newest first, with its Date , Rate , and Source (Yahoo Finance, Frankfurter (ECB), or Money import) Reports dated before the first stored rate cannot convert that currency, so after importing years of history, use Fill gaps in rate history for each foreign currency you use.

When Monize converts an amount, it uses the exchange rate for the transaction's own date -- the newest stored rate on or before that date -- not today's rate. This keeps historical reports accurate. If no rate close enough to that date is stored, Monize does not guess: the figure is shown as partial, and the page names the currency pair that needs a rate.

A transaction that records its own exchange rate -- a cross-currency transfer, a purchase in a foreign currency, or an investment trade in a currency other than the account's -- is always converted at that rate, rather than the market rate of the day.

To record a purchase made in another currency, for example a hotel bill in euros paid with a Canadian-dollar card: In the transaction form, click the currency picker beside the amount ( Entry currency ) and choose the currency you paid in Enter the amount in that currency Monize shows the Total in the account's currency, converted at the day's rate (shown as "1 EUR = ... CAD" with its date). If no rate is stored for that day, enter the converted amount yourself -- for example from your statement The register can show such transactions in the account's currency or the original one.

Many credit cards add a fee to purchases in a foreign currency. Set the account's Foreign Currency Conversion Fee (optional) in the account's settings, and Monize includes the fee in the converted total of each foreign purchase ("Includes a 2.5% foreign transaction fee"). The account's page then shows a Foreign Currency Transaction Fees section, and the Foreign Currency Transaction Fees report totals the fees across your accounts over time. See Accounts for the account settings.
When you transfer money between accounts that use different currencies, Monize handles the conversion:

You create a transfer from Account A (e.g., USD) to Account B (e.g., CAD) Enter the Transfer Amount in the source account's currency The Amount Received in the destination currency is calculated from the exchange rate; correct it to the amount that actually arrived if your bank used a different rate Both transactions are linked

Cross-currency transfers imported from QIF files require special handling because the QIF format does not record exchange rate information: The first side of the transfer is imported as a pending transaction When the other account's file is imported, the system matches the pending transfer You may need to manually adjust the destination amount to match the actual exchange rate used This is noted in the transaction with a memo: "PENDING IMPORT: Amount may need adjustment..." Importing a Microsoft Money .mny file brings across Money's own exchange rate history as well (shown with the source "Money import").
All reports automatically convert amounts to your home currency using: The exchange rate on the transaction date for historical accuracy The latest rate for current balance reports

When a report includes accounts in different currencies, the amounts are all converted to your home currency before aggregation. This means: A spending report correctly compares a $100 USD purchase with a $130 CAD purchase Net worth reports accurately combine assets across currencies If a rate is missing for some amounts, the report says which figures are partial and which currency needs a rate, rather than leaving the amounts out silently or counting them unconverted.
The Currency Exposure report (under Investment on the Reports page) shows how much of your portfolio is held in each currency, with its native value, the exchange rate, and the converted value.

Each security trades in its own currency, which is filled in when you look the security up (for example USD for a NYSE or NASDAQ listing, CAD for the TSX, GBP for the London Stock Exchange). You can change it in the security's form. If you hold securities that trade in a different currency than your investment account, the market values are converted to the account's currency for display, and to your home currency for portfolio totals. An investment transaction in a foreign security records its own Exchange rate and Converted Total . See Investments .

Monize includes an AI assistant that can answer natural language questions about your finances, generate insights about your spending habits, and integrate with external AI clients via the Model Context Protocol (MCP). You bring your own API key -- Monize supports Anthropic Claude, OpenAI, Ollama (local or Ollama Cloud), and any OpenAI-compatible provider -- or your own AI subscription through the MCP Relay .
Before using AI features, you need at least one configured AI provider -- either a central provider set up by the administrator, or a personal provider you configure yourself.

An administrator can configure a shared AI provider at the server level so that all users have access to AI features without needing their own API keys. This is done by setting environment variables on the server. Variable Description AI_DEFAULT_PROVIDER Provider type: anthropic , openai , ollama , or openai-compatible AI_DEFAULT_API_KEY API key for the provider AI_DEFAULT_MODEL Optional -- specific model to use (falls back to the provider's default) AI_DEFAULT_BASE_URL Optional -- custom base URL for OpenAI-compatible or Ollama providers For example, in your .env file: AI_DEFAULT_PROVIDER=anthropic AI_DEFAULT_API_KEY=sk-ant-... When a central provider is configured, all users can use the AI assistant and financial insights immediately, and AI Settings says "System Default AI Provider Available" . Users who configure their own provider use their personal provider instead of the central one. How much work the central provider may do to answer one question is set with AI_QUERY_MAX_ITERATIONS (default 5), AI_QUERY_MAX_TOOL_CALLS (15), AI_QUERY_TIMEOUT_MINUTES (20), AI_QUERY_MAX_INPUT_TOKENS (200,000) and AI_QUERY_MAX_TOOL_RESULT_CHARS (50,000). A personal provider sets its own limits in its form (see Query Limits ).

Navigate to Settings > AI Settings Click Add Provider Select a Provider type, and optionally give it a Display Name Enter your API Key (not needed for Ollama or the MCP Relay) Optionally choose a specific Model (or leave it blank for the default), and enter a Base URL for Ollama or an OpenAI-compatible provider Set its Priority Click Add Provider You can configure multiple providers (up to 10 by default; AI_MAX_PROVIDERS_PER_USER changes it) and assign priority levels: a lower number is a higher priority. Monize will fall back to the next provider if the primary one is unavailable. Each provider card shows its status ( Active or Inactive ), priority, model, a masked key and any cost rates, with Disable / Enable , Edit and Delete . Deleting a provider removes its saved API key with it. When ENCRYPTION_KEY is not configured on the server, cloud providers cannot be added, because their API keys could not be stored securely; Ollama still works.

Provider Default Model Description Anthropic (Claude) claude-sonnet-4-20250514 Claude models via the Anthropic API OpenAI (GPT) gpt-4o GPT models via the OpenAI API Ollama (Local) (user-configured) Local, self-hosted models -- your data never leaves your machine. Point its Base URL at your Ollama server, such as http://localhost:11434 (see the note below). Ollama Cloud (user-configured) Models hosted by Ollama, with an API key. Model names must include the -cloud suffix (for example gpt-oss:20b-cloud ). OpenAI-Compatible (user-configured) Any API that follows the OpenAI format (Groq, Together, LM Studio, etc.) MCP Relay -- Answers chat prompts with your own MCP agent and subscription instead of a server-side model (see MCP Relay ) For OpenAI-compatible providers, you can set a custom Base URL to point at your preferred endpoint. Note A private or local base URL ( localhost , 192.168.x.x , a container name) works only for an administrator, or when the server operator lists that address in AI_PRIVATE_BASE_URL_ALLOWLIST . Otherwise the provider must use a public address. This stops any signed-up user from making the server call machines on its own network.

Click Test beside the Model field while adding or editing a provider, or Test on a saved provider's card, to verify that your API key and configuration are working. The test sends a minimal request to the provider and reports "Connection successful. Model ... is ready." , that the model is not available on this provider, or the error the provider returned.

Under Cost rates (optional) , enter your provider's published Input cost / 1M tokens and Output cost / 1M tokens , and the Rate Currency they are quoted in. They are used only to show an estimated cost on the Usage dashboard; leave them blank to skip cost estimates. When the rate currency differs from your default currency, the estimate is converted with your saved exchange rates.

Under Query limits (optional) you decide how much work this provider may do to answer one question. Leave a field blank to use the default shown.
