Floating chat bubble at the top of AI Settings puts a chat button on every page, so you can ask the assistant from anywhere. It opens as a panel (a bottom sheet on a phone) that you can expand to full screen. It is off until you turn it on, and is offered once an AI provider is available.
The AI Assistant lets you ask questions about your finances in plain language. It uses tool calling to query your actual financial data and return accurate, sourced answers.

Navigate to AI > AI Assistant (or open the floating chat bubble) Type a question in the chat input. Press Enter to send, Shift+Enter for a new line. The assistant streams its response in real time, showing each lookup it makes as it goes The conversation is saved in your browser, so it is still there when you come back; Clear conversation starts a new one. Without any configured provider the page says "AI Not Configured" and links to the settings. Example questions: "How much did I spend on groceries last month?" "What are my top 5 expense categories this year?" "Compare my spending this month vs last month" "What's my net worth trend over the past 6 months?" "How much can I still spend this month within my budget?" "What's my income breakdown by category?" The assistant has access to the following financial tools: Tool Description List Transactions Search and summarize transactions with filters List Accounts Account balances and net worth, with foreign accounts converted to your default currency List Categories and List Payees Your category tree and payees Compare Periods Side-by-side comparison of two time periods Generate Report A built-in report: spending by category or payee, income vs. expenses, trends, anomalies, month comparison, net-worth history Budget Status Current budget vs actual spending Upcoming Bills Scheduled bills and deposits Portfolio Summary , Investment Transactions , Capital Gains Holdings, performance, trades and realized gains Warranties Your warranties and when they expire Calculate Arithmetic over supplied values, including converting an amount between currencies at the rate on a date Render Chart Draws a chart in the chat
The AI page displays suggested query buttons to help you get started quickly: Monthly spending , Top categories , Account balances , Compare months , Net worth trend and Savings rate .

When the assistant returns data that lends itself to visualization, an inline chart is rendered directly in the chat. For example, a spending-by-category query may display a bar or pie chart alongside the text response. A chart can be downloaded as a PNG and a table as a CSV.

When the assistant mentions one of your accounts, categories, payees, or transactions by name, that name is rendered as a clickable in-app link. Clicking it takes you straight to that item -- or to a transaction list filtered to it -- so you can jump from an answer to the underlying records in one click. The same links appear on insight cards .

Beyond answering questions, the assistant can make changes on your behalf -- creating, updating, and deleting transactions, transfers, payees, securities, investment transactions and transaction rules ( Tools > Rules ), changing a transaction's category, and running a rule on existing transactions. Nothing is saved until you approve it. Each proposed change is presented as an on-screen confirmation card showing exactly what would be written, which you Approve or Cancel : 1-5 items -- each item gets its own confirmation card. 6 or more items (up to 25) -- the batch is grouped into a single bulk confirmation card that you approve or reject as a whole ( Approve all ). Ask for "individual" review to get one card per item at any size. A card also says what your rules would do to a new transaction, warns when a change touches a reconciled transaction, and expires if left too long (ask again to retry).

You can attach files to a chat message with the Add attachment button, or by dropping them on the chat. Supported types are images (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP), PDF, CSV, and plain text -- up to 5 files per message , each up to 5 MB and 20 MB in total. PDFs are text-extracted so the assistant can read their contents. On a phone, a file shared to an installed Monize can be sent straight to the assistant.

On desktop, the floating chat panel can be moved by its header: drag it, nudge it with the arrow keys, or click to snap it to the next corner. Its position is remembered per device. Expand to full screen and Collapse to panel switch between the two sizes.

Monize's AI automatically analyzes your financial data daily and generates actionable insights. Insights appear on the AI > Insights page ( Spending Insights ) and highlight patterns, anomalies, and opportunities you might otherwise miss. The page shows how many insights are active and how many are alerts and warnings, and lets you narrow the list by Type and Severity . Show dismissed brings back the ones you dismissed, and Refresh Insights analyzes your data again on demand.

Type Description Severity Anomaly Unusual spending -- significantly higher than your historical average for a category Warning / Alert Trend A sustained increase or decrease in spending over 3+ months Info / Warning Subscription A recurring charge that has changed in price or a consolidation opportunity Info Budget Pace You're on track to exceed your budget for the current period Warning Seasonal Seasonal spending patterns detected (e.g., holiday months, annual renewals) Info New Recurring A newly detected recurring charge that wasn't previously flagged Info Insights are regenerated daily. A maximum of 50 insights are retained per user, and each insight expires after 7 days. Note In MCP Relay mode, insights are generated by your connected agent rather than a server-side provider, so your agent must be online for generation to succeed. The daily background job skips relay-only users; you can instead generate insights on demand from the Insights page, which shows a live relay status bar indicating whether your agent is connected.
Click Dismiss on any insight card to remove it. Dismissed insights will not reappear unless you turn on Show dismissed .

Monize can project your finances forward using AI. The forecast analyzes your historical income and spending -- at least 2 months of transaction history is required -- and produces a month-by-month projection for up to 12 months ahead. Like insights, forecast prose is written in your chosen language. In MCP Relay mode the forecast is generated by your connected agent rather than a server-side provider, so your agent must be online to generate one. Note The AI forecast has no screen of its own in the web app yet; it is available through the API. The Cash Flow Forecast on Bills & Deposits and on the dashboard is a separate, non-AI projection from your scheduled transactions.

The Model Context Protocol (MCP) allows external AI clients -- such as Claude Desktop -- to connect to Monize and access your financial data directly. This means you can ask Claude Desktop questions about your finances without opening Monize in a browser.

Monize supports two ways to authenticate an MCP client. Pick based on whether your Monize instance is reachable from the public internet. Method Best for Requires public HTTPS URL? Setup effort OAuth ("Add Connector") Public deployments Yes Click-through Personal Access Token + local bridge Self-hosted / LAN-only / VPN-only No Manual config file Important Claude Desktop's built-in Add Connector flow only works when your Monize instance is exposed on the public internet behind HTTPS. The connector handshake requires Claude Desktop to reach your Monize URL directly, and self-signed certificates or non-routable hostnames (e.g., http://localhost:3001 , http://192.168.x.x , or *.local mDNS names) are rejected. If your instance is private, use the Personal Access Token + Local Bridge method instead.

This is the easiest method when your Monize instance is publicly reachable. Tokens are issued through a browser-based consent flow and managed automatically by Claude Desktop -- you never copy or paste a token, and revocation is per-app rather than per-token. What you'll need: Monize running behind a public HTTPS URL (e.g., https://monize.example.com ). The PUBLIC_APP_URL environment variable on the backend set to that same URL. The OAuth issuer, MCP resource URL, and consent redirects are all derived from PUBLIC_APP_URL , so it must match exactly what Claude Desktop will see in the browser. Claude Desktop signed in to your Monize account in a browser tab on the same machine. The consent flow piggybacks on your existing web session. Steps: In Claude Desktop, open Settings > Connectors . Click Add custom connector (or Add Connector ). Enter your Monize URL: https://monize.example.com (no trailing path -- the connector resolves the MCP and OAuth metadata endpoints automatically via /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource and /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server ). Claude Desktop opens your browser to Monize's consent screen. Review the requested scopes ( monize:read , monize:write ) and click Allow . The browser redirects back to Claude Desktop, which stores the access + refresh tokens internally. After consent, Claude Desktop automatically refreshes tokens (default access-token lifetime is 1 hour, refresh-token lifetime is 14 days). You can revoke access from either side: From Claude Desktop: remove the connector in Settings > Connectors . From Monize: an admin can disable the user account or reset their password in Admin > User Management -- both revoke every active OAuth token, refresh token, and authorization grant for that user immediately. Security notes: All grants are PKCE-protected (S256). The OAuth flow rejects the legacy implicit and password grant types entirely. Tokens are audience-bound to your Monize MCP URL. A token issued for https://monize.example.com/api/v1/mcp cannot be replayed against a different Monize instance. Disabling a user in Admin > User Management immediately invalidates every existing OAuth access token, refresh token, and grant for that user, in addition to refresh tokens and PATs.

h: Option 2: Personal Access Token + Local Bridge
x: Use this method when your Monize instance is private (LAN-only, behind a VPN, accessed via Tailscale/Cloudflare Tunnel, etc.) and Claude Desktop's connector flow can't reach it. This method works because Claude Desktop spawns a local subprocess (the "bridge") on your machine, and that subprocess connects to your private Monize URL using whatever network access your machine has. Nothing has to be publicly exposed. Step 1: Generate a Personal Access Token In Monize, navigate to Settings > API Access . Click Create Token . Give the token a name (e.g., Claude Desktop ), select scopes ( Read , Write ) and an expiration, and click Create Token . Monize asks you to confirm it is you first. Copy the token -- it begins with pat_ and is shown only once. Tokens are stored as SHA-256 hashes in the database. You can revoke a token at any time from the settings page. The same section shows the instance's MCP Server URL with a Copy button. See Personal Access Tokens for the details. Step 2: Configure Claude Desktop Edit your claude_desktop_config.json file. The location depends on your operating system: OS Path macOS ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json Windows %APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json Linux ~/.config/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json Add the following entry under mcpServers . The mcp-remote package (from @modelcontextprotocol ) acts as a stdio-to-HTTP bridge, accepting your PAT as an Authorization: Bearer header: { "mcpServers": { "monize": { "command": "npx", "args": [ "-y", "mcp-remote", "https://monize.lan/api/v1/mcp", "--header", "Authorization: Bearer pat_your_token_here" ] } } } Replace https://monize.lan/api/v1/mcp with your Monize URL (LAN, VPN, tunnel -- whatever your machine can reach) and pat_your_token_here with the token you generated. Step 3: Restart Claude Desktop Fully quit and relaunch Claude Desktop. The Monize tools should appear in the tool picker once the bridge connects. Notes for self-hosted users: If you use a self-signed TLS certificate, you may need to add NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS to the entry's env block pointing at your CA bundle. PATs do not auto-rotate. Set a reasonable expiry when you generate the token, or rotate manually on a schedule. You can revoke a PAT instantly from Settings > API Access without restarting Claude Desktop -- the next request from the bridge fails authentication and Claude Desktop surfaces the error.

Read tools require the read scope; write tools require the write scope and are additionally gated by an approval step and the daily write limit . MCP Relay -- "bring your own assistant" -- lets the in-app AI chat run on your own MCP agent and subscription instead of a server-side API key. The MCP Server lets an external client pull your Monize data; the relay flips that direction: the Monize web chat pushes each prompt out to your agent (Claude CLI, Codex, or any MCP client), the agent answers it using the Monize tools, and the answer streams back into the browser chat. Use it when: You already pay for a Claude or Codex subscription and don't want to also configure a metered API key in Settings > AI Settings . No central AI provider is configured and you'd rather not paste an API key into the server at all. You want the answer computed on your own machine with your own model choice. Note In relay mode no LLM API key lives on the server . Monize only routes the prompt text and your agent's answer; your subscription does the thinking. The agent reaches your data through the same authenticated MCP tools as any other MCP client.

The relay is a broker between two long-lived connections -- the browser waiting for an answer and your agent waiting for work: You type a prompt in the Monize web chat. The browser opens a streaming request and the prompt is queued for your user. Your agent, sitting in a poll loop, calls the get_next_prompt tool. It claims the queued prompt (with prior conversation history for context). The agent does the work using the normal Monize MCP tools ( list_accounts , list_transactions , etc.), calling report_progress with short status lines as it goes. Live tool activity and progress narration stream back into the web chat -- the same "Looking up ..." chips and running text the native AI Assistant shows. The agent calls post_response with the final answer, which is delivered to the waiting browser and persisted as the assistant's chat message. The agent loops back to get_next_prompt and waits for the next one. Three relay control tools drive this loop: Tool Direction Purpose get_next_prompt Monize -> agent Long-poll for the next chat prompt. Returns { hasPrompt: false } if none arrives in the poll window -- call it again immediately to keep listening. report_progress agent -> Monize Stream a one-line status update shown live in the chat while you work. Optional but recommended. post_response agent -> Monize Deliver the final answer for a claimed prompt back to the browser. Timeouts: a prompt waits up to 5 minutes for an agent to pick it up. Once your agent has claimed it, the browser keeps waiting as long as the agent shows signs of life (polls, progress, tool calls), giving up after 3 minutes of silence or 20 minutes in all. Each get_next_prompt long-poll parks for about 25 seconds, then returns empty so the agent polls again. If your agent isn't connected and listening when you send a prompt, the chat reports that your assistant did not respond.

Step 1 -- Add the relay as a provider. In Settings > AI Settings , click Add Provider , choose MCP Relay and click Add Provider . The relay needs no key, model or URL. It is the active provider while it has the highest priority (the lowest number) of your providers. The exact commands (with your instance URL pre-filled, and Copy buttons) appear in that form and in the chat's How to connect panel. Step 2 -- Create an access token. In Settings > API Access , create a Personal Access Token (starts with pat_ , shown once). The relay authenticates with the same PAT as any MCP client. Give the agent a token of its own: a token shared with another MCP client sends that client's confirmations to the chat too. Step 3 -- Connect the agent. With Claude CLI: claude mcp add --transport http monize https://monize.example.com/api/v1/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer <your-token>" Restart Claude with auto-approval so it doesn't prompt for every Monize tool call: claude --allowedTools "mcp__monize__*" Or with Codex -- add this to ~/.codex/config.toml , set MONIZE_TOKEN to your token, then run codex : [mcp_servers.monize] url = "https://monize.example.com/api/v1/mcp" bearer_token_env_var = "MONIZE_TOKEN" default_tools_approval_mode = "auto" Replace https://monize.example.com/api/v1/mcp with your own instance URL. Step 4 -- Start the agent loop. Give the agent this instruction so it listens for prompts from Monize: Loop forever: call get_next_prompt; if hasPrompt is false, call it again; otherwise handle the request with the Monize tools and call post_response with the answer; then repeat. Once the loop is running, the chat's connection indicator turns to MCP Agent listening and anything you type in the web chat is answered by your agent.

Once connected, use the AI chat exactly as you would with a server-side provider -- ask questions in natural language, get charts and visualizations, and approve any writes via the in-chat confirmation card. The difference is purely behind the scenes: your subscription answers, and progress narration reflects your agent's real tool calls.

The chat shows a tunnel status so you know whether your agent is reachable: State Meaning MCP Agent offline No agent has polled recently. Start your agent loop. MCP Agent listening An agent is connected and idle, ready for prompts (blinking green). MCP Agent working Your agent is currently handling a prompt. Disconnected after inactivity No prompt arrived for 10 minutes, so Monize told the agent to stop its loop. Start the loop again to continue. If you send a prompt while offline, it queues briefly and then times out with a message to make sure your MCP agent is connected and listening.

Your agent must be running. The relay only works while your agent's poll loop is active. Close the terminal and the chat goes offline. The loop stops when you are idle. After 10 minutes with no new prompt, the agent is told to stop polling, so an idle agent does not fill its own context with empty polls. Restart the loop when you want to continue. One agent per user. Prompts are queued in order per user and handed to whichever agent polls first. Answer budget. Long, multi-tool agent runs must keep reporting progress, and finish within 20 minutes, or the prompt times out.

The Usage card on Settings > AI Settings shows how much you have used your AI providers over the last 7 days , 30 days , 90 days or All time : the total requests, input tokens and output tokens, and an Est. Cost once you have entered cost rates on a provider. By Provider breaks the totals down per provider, and Recent Activity lists each request with its date, provider, feature, tokens, duration and estimated cost. The relay is the exception: it generally runs on a fixed-cost monthly subscription, so token counts and costs for relayed answers aren't exposed and aren't available.

Monize takes several measures to protect your financial data when using AI features: Measure Description Aggregated Data First The AI receives aggregated summaries by default; individual transactions are sent only when a question asks for them Encrypted API Keys Provider API keys are encrypted at rest using AES-256-GCM with per-key random salts Local Provider Option Use Ollama to run models locally -- your data never leaves your machine Rate Limiting AI endpoints are rate-limited (10 queries/min, 5 test connections/min); MCP requests are limited to 30/min. AI and MCP write operations are additionally capped per user per day (default 50, configurable via MCP_DAILY_WRITE_LIMIT ) SSRF Protection Custom base URLs are validated to prevent server-side request forgery; private addresses are refused unless allowed by an administrator Prompt Injection Prevention Financial data is delimited to prevent prompt injection attacks Scoped MCP Tokens Personal access tokens have configurable scopes (read, write) and can be revoked at any time Write Approval Every change the assistant or an MCP client proposes is shown for your approval before anything is saved Masked Keys API keys are masked in all API responses, showing only the last 4 characters
Monize provides comprehensive security features and configurable user preferences.

Click Settings (the gear icon with your first name, in the top-right corner) to configure your preferences. The Settings page uses a sidebar navigation on desktop (or a section picker on mobile) to organize sections, making it easy to jump directly to the area you need. Some entries in the sidebar open a page of their own; the rest scroll to their section.

Section What it covers Profile Your name and email address (see Profile ) Preferences Language, appearance, dates and numbers, investments, transactions, default views, application behaviour (see Preferences ) Notifications Email, browser push, per-notification delivery and cooldown (see Notifications ) Security Password, two-factor authentication, backup codes, trusted devices Shared Access Delegated users (see Shared Access ) Emergency Access Dead-man's switch for trusted contacts (see Emergency Access ) API Access Personal access tokens and the MCP server URL (see Personal Access Tokens ) AI Settings AI providers, the floating chat bubble, and usage (see AI ) Bank Sync Import booked transactions straight from your bank (see Bank Sync ) Email Receipts A mailbox for order confirmations and the profiles that read them (see Email Receipts ) Payee Lookup Where a payee's contact details come from (see Payee Lookup ) Backup & Restore Your own manual export and restore (see Backup and Restore ). Scheduled backups are configured by an administrator on Admin > Backups Help & Support Documentation links and the support backup (see Help and Support ) Guided Tours Every walkthrough Monize offers (see Guided Tours ) About Version, update status, release notes, licence (see About ) Danger Zone Delete data or delete your account (see Danger Zone ) Delegates: While you are acting as a delegate for someone else, the Settings page shows only the Security section, which manages your own password and 2FA. Every other section would reflect or alter the account owner's settings, so it is hidden. See Shared Access . Demo mode: On a demo instance, profile editing, password changes, two-factor authentication and account deletion are disabled, and the sections for them are hidden.

The Profile section holds your First Name , Last Name and Email . Click Save Profile to keep a change. Changing your email address asks for your Current Password as well. When the server can send email, the change does not take effect straight away: Monize sends a confirmation link to the new address (and a notice to the old one), and the section shows "A confirmation link was sent to ... Your email address changes once you follow it." Follow the link, then sign in again with the new address. A newer request replaces a pending one, so only the latest link works. On a server without email, the change applies as soon as you save.

Preferences are grouped into seven blocks. They save as you change them -- there is no Save button; each change is written immediately and confirmed with a toast. You can always reopen it from the version number in the About section or on the login screen. Email notifications moved. Monize is built for multiple languages. Choose your preferred display language from the Language picker under Language & Region , and the interface -- menus, labels, buttons, messages, and email notifications -- is shown in that language. Pick once, applied everywhere -- Your language is saved to your account preferences, so it follows you across devices and browser sessions when you sign in. Automatic detection -- Before you set a preference, Monize detects a suitable language from your browser's settings. If your browser's language is not available, it falls back to the default language. Locale-aware formatting -- Your language drives how dates, numbers, currency amounts, and percentages are formatted throughout the app, so they read naturally for your region. (Date and number formats can also be overridden independently -- see Date Format and Number Format above.) Right-to-left support -- The layout adapts automatically for right-to-left languages. Email notifications -- All transactional emails -- password reset, email verification, delegation invites, admin notifications, and bill reminders -- are sent in the recipient's stored language. AI assistant responses, insights, and forecasts are written in your chosen language; data values (account/category/payee names, currencies, numbers) are left as-is. The set of available languages grows over time. Whichever languages are installed appear in the Language picker; if a particular language is not yet listed, the interface falls back to the default language.

Appearance is two independent settings. Theme decides light or dark: System follows your device setting and switches with it, or you can pin Light or Dark . Colour theme decides the palette used within that light or dark mode. The picker shows a swatch preview of each palette rendered in your current mode rather than only naming it. Palette Default Monize's standard palette Latte , Burgundy , Forest , Nord , Midnight Warm and cool alternatives MS Money , Newspaper Familiar looks for people arriving from Microsoft Money, and a high-legibility print-like palette Solarized , Gruvbox , Dracula , Tokyo Night , Rosé Pine Well-known developer palettes High contrast Maximum separation between foreground and background for low-vision use Colour-blind safe Tinted so that the red/green pairs Monize uses for gains and losses remain distinguishable

When you look up a security by name or symbol, Yahoo Finance may return results from multiple exchanges around the world. The Preferred Exchanges setting lets you specify up to 3 exchanges in priority order so that results from your preferred exchanges are ranked first. For example, if you primarily invest on the London Stock Exchange and the Toronto Stock Exchange, setting your preferred exchanges to LSE and TSX ensures that when you search for a security, matches from those exchanges appear before results from NYSE or other exchanges. Select up to 3 exchanges using the Priority 1 , Priority 2 , and Priority 3 dropdowns Priority 1 has the highest preference, followed by Priority 2 and Priority 3 Results from preferred exchanges are boosted above all other results An exact symbol match on a preferred exchange always wins If no preferred exchanges are set, Monize uses its default exchange ranking (major US exchanges first) Preferred exchanges are used whenever Monize looks up a security from Yahoo Finance: Securities page -- When adding or editing a security and using the Lookup button Import wizard -- When mapping securities during a QIF, OFX, or CSV import (both individual lookups and the "Lookup All" bulk operation) Security creation -- When creating a new security from the import mapping screen Without preferred exchanges, searching for "Barclays" might return BCS (NYSE) as the top result. With LSE set as Priority 1, the search returns BARC.L (London Stock Exchange) instead.

The Notifications section decides what Monize tells you about and how it reaches you. It has five parts: email, the per-notification delivery matrix, the investment movement alert, browser push devices, and a diagnostics report for when push is not working. Every notification is always written to the bell in the header, whatever you choose here; these settings decide which ones also reach you by email or push.

Setting Description Email Notifications The master switch for email. With it off, nothing is sent by email regardless of the matrix below. Weekly Budget Digest A weekly summary of budget alerts and status Digest day Monday or Friday Send Test Email Sends a test message to your account's email address so you can confirm delivery works Critical budget alerts (over budget, income shortfall) are sent immediately regardless of the digest settings. Email is only available when an administrator has configured SMTP on the server. Without it the section reads "Email notifications are not available. SMTP has not been configured by the administrator."

Monize can deliver notifications to a phone or desktop even when the app is closed, using Web Push. No Firebase, Google Play or Apple Developer account is involved -- the instance generates and holds its own key pair. Navigate to Settings > Notifications > Browser push Click Enable on this device . Your browser asks for permission to show notifications; nothing is sent until you allow it. Click Send test notification to confirm delivery. The result is shown per device under Last test, per device . Monize also offers this from a "Turn on notifications?" banner under the header; Not now hides it on that device. Each registered device is listed with the transport that delivers it (Web push or UnifiedPush), the address it registered from, when it was registered, when it was last active, its browser, and its last delivery. Remove revokes a device immediately. Signing out does not turn push off for that browser: the device is held, receives nothing while you are signed out, and resumes when the same account signs in there again. The list marks such a device "Signed out on this device." Platform What to know iPhone / iPad Push works only once Monize is installed to the Home Screen. Use Share > Add to Home Screen and open Monize from there. If no permission prompt appears, allow notifications in iOS Settings > Notifications > Monize . Android A granted browser permission is not always enough -- the system can still hide notifications. Press and hold the Monize icon on your home screen, tap App info , then Notifications , and make sure they are turned on. Brave Brave blocks the push service by default. Open Brave Settings > Privacy and security , turn on "Use Google services for push messaging" , restart the browser and try again. Blocked in the browser If notifications are blocked for Monize, allow them in the browser's site settings and reload the page. A device can stop being reachable on its own. Monize says which of the three happened, and the repair is the same in each case -- turn push on again in that browser: Reason Meaning No longer reachable The browser's push service dropped the subscription Retired when this instance rotated its push key pair An administrator rotated the instance key pair (see Instance Notification Settings ) Retired after repeated delivery failures Deliveries kept failing, so the registration was retired Browser push has to be switched on for the whole instance by an administrator before any of this is available, and the server needs ENCRYPTION_KEY set so it can store its push key pair.

The same encrypted push can be delivered to a self-hosted UnifiedPush distributor -- ntfy , NextPush and similar -- instead of Google's or Apple's infrastructure. It shares the instance's push key pair and its on/off switch. To use it, register an endpoint in your UnifiedPush distributor app, then turn on the UnifiedPush column for the notification categories you want in the matrix below. Devices delivered this way are labelled UnifiedPush in the device list.

Under Notification diagnostics Monize shows what your browser and device report about notification support -- permission state, service worker registration, transport, and platform quirks. Refresh re-reads it after you change a setting, and Copy report puts the whole thing on the clipboard to paste into a bug report.

The preference matrix chooses which channel carries each kind of notification, and how often it may interrupt you. Categories (rows) Category What it covers Bills and scheduled Upcoming and overdue bills, scheduled transactions Budgets Budget alerts and digests System alerts Infrastructure problems (backup failures, provider outages, SMTP). Push channels only -- its email side is a severity-driven administrator fan-out, not a personal setting. Account balances Balance thresholds and watched accounts Investment value Portfolio movement (see below) Strategy signals Signals from investment strategies Bank connections A bank sync consent that is about to expire or has expired Bank sync results The outcome of each daily bank sync Email receipts Activity from your email receipts mailbox Bonds Government bond events: maturity in 14 days, interest paid, a new rate period, a matured series with no redemption, a rate change AI review proposals Proposals waiting in the AI review inbox, and proposals that expire in 3 days Warranty reminders Warranties about to expire (see Warranties ) Channels (columns) Channel Behaviour Email (report) The batched/digest email. Live and never suppressed by the cooldown. Email (alert) An immediate email, one per event Push Browser push to your registered devices UnifiedPush Push to your own UnifiedPush distributor A cell whose channel does not apply to that category renders as not applicable rather than as a dead toggle. A channel that cannot deliver says why: "Turn on email notifications above to send these by email" , or "No device is registered for push, so this channel cannot deliver." Cooldown Each category carries its own cooldown: Off , 5 minutes, 15 minutes, 30 minutes, 1 hour, 6 hours, or 24 hours. Within the window, a second alert or push from the same group is skipped. It gates the two interrupting channels (alert email and push) and never the report email, and never the bell. Every cell and cooldown saves as you change it.

Investment value movement sends one notification a day when your investment accounts move beyond a threshold you set. The movement is measured from market changes and dividends only -- deposits and withdrawals are excluded, so moving money in does not read as a gain. Turn it on with Enable investment movement alerts , then set the threshold under Notify when the daily move is at least ; it saves as you change it.

Monize can fill in a payee's website, address, email and phone number for you. The Payee Lookup section decides where those details come from and whether the lookup runs by itself. Looking a payee up is described on the Categories and Payees page. Two sources can answer: Source What it gives you Google Places Directory facts, cheaper per lookup. Google holds no email address. Existing AI Provider Can find an email address, and costs a model call for every lookup. Uses a provider you configured under AI Settings . Each source has its own on/off switch on its title line ( Use Google Places for payee lookups , Use an AI provider for payee lookups ), so you can leave a provider configured for the assistant while switching it off for payee lookups. When both sources can answer, use the Move up and Move down arrows (or drag) to choose which source answers first ; if the first source cannot answer -- its monthly limit is spent, or it found nothing -- the next one is tried. With more than one active AI provider you can also pin which provider answers a lookup under Provider to use , or leave it on "Any provider, in priority order."

Below the sources, Enable automatic payee contact lookup looks a new payee up as you create it, instead of waiting for you to ask. The payee's name is sent, along with any notes, website, address, email and phone it already has, so the lookup can tell the right business and the right location apart -- "Starbucks 483 Bay St Toronto" resolves a branch where "Starbucks" alone resolves whichever one ranks first. With every source switched off the toggle is shown off and disabled: nothing could answer, so it does not claim a behaviour that cannot happen.

Google Places answers a payee lookup from Google's business directory. You supply an API key from your own Google Cloud project; Monize sends the payee's name (and the address you already have) and stores nothing with Google. Sign in to the Google Cloud console and create or select a project. Google requires a billing account on the project even to use the free monthly allowance. Enable Places API (New) for the project. This is not the legacy "Places API" -- Monize calls the new places:searchText endpoint, and a project with only the legacy API enabled returns no results. Go to APIs & Services > Credentials > Create credentials > API key and copy the key. This is the step that is easiest to get wrong. Monize calls Google from the server, not from your browser. Application restriction: IP addresses. List your deployment's outbound (egress) IP addresses. This is the restriction that actually constrains a server-side key. API restriction: limit the key to Places API (New) . An HTTP referrer restriction is the wrong choice here. A referrer restriction only protects a key that is public -- shipped inside browser JavaScript, where the browser sets the Referer header and page script cannot forge it. This key lives encrypted in Monize's database and never reaches a browser, so anything holding it can send any referrer it likes; the restriction filters nobody. If your deployment has no stable egress IP (a home server on a dynamic address, a cluster with variable egress), a referrer restriction is still workable as a weak filter: Monize sends the origin of PUBLIC_APP_URL as the Referer header, so add exactly that origin to the allowed referrers. Note that a pattern like *.example.com/* does not match a bare example.com . Google reports a referrer mismatch as Requests from referer <empty> are blocked . If the Test button returns that, the allowed referrer does not match the origin Monize sends. Navigate to Settings > Payee Lookup On the Google Places row, click Set up Paste the key into API key Click Test . Monize runs a real search (for "coffee shop") against Google with that key and reports "Google accepted the key" or the error Google returned. A refused test costs nothing against your monthly limit. Click Save , then turn on Use Google Places for payee lookups Once saved, the key is never shown again -- the field displays a mask, and leaving it blank when you edit keeps the stored key. Remove key deletes it. Limit requests each month is on by default with a limit of 1,000 ( Requests per month ). That number is deliberate. A payee lookup asks Google for websiteUri and internationalPhoneNumber , which puts every call in Google's Text Search Enterprise SKU , whose free allowance is 1,000 requests per calendar month . The widely quoted 10,000 belongs to the Essentials SKU, which returns neither a website nor a phone number and so cannot answer this lookup at all. The count resets on Google's calendar month -- the first of the month, midnight US Pacific time -- so Monize's counter and Google's allowance roll over together Your usage is shown on the Google Places row as "Used this month: N of 1000" Once the limit is spent, lookups fall back to your AI provider if you have one switched on; with no fallback, lookups are unavailable until the month rolls over You can raise the limit (1 to 1,000,000) or switch it off entirely, but past the free allowance Google bills you Message What it means "The stored API key cannot be read by this server." The key is stored but cannot be decrypted -- typically after a backup is restored onto a different instance, or after ENCRYPTION_KEY changed. Enter the key again to fix it. "This server has no encryption key configured, so an API key cannot be stored securely." The deployment has no ENCRYPTION_KEY . Ask your administrator to set one; a key cannot be saved until then. Test fails with a referrer or IP error See step 2 -- the key's application restriction does not match how Monize calls Google. Test succeeds but no results The project likely has the legacy Places API enabled instead of Places API (New) .

An administrator can supply one key for the whole deployment instead, through environment variables: GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY=your-google-places-key GOOGLE_PLACES_MONTHLY_CAP=1000 # optional, default 1000 When this is set, Google Places is available to every user on the instance and the operator's limit is the only one that applies. Users then see only "Configured by this server's administrator" and an on/off switch -- they cannot enter or see a key, and cannot change the limit. Every user's lookups spend the operator's allowance. Leave GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY unset and each user configures their own key and their own limit, as described above.

Settings > Bank Sync imports the booked transactions of your bank accounts straight from the bank, so you do not have to download and import statement files. Each bank account is linked to one Monize account, and its transactions arrive there with your import rules applied. Access is read-only: Monize can never move money. Two data providers are offered in the Data provider picker: Provider Where it works What you need Enable Banking Banks in the European Economic Area, through Open Banking (PSD2) Your own free Enable Banking application (see below) SimpleFIN Banks you connect in SimpleFIN Bridge A SimpleFIN Bridge account and a one-time setup token Nothing is configured on the server for either one: each person brings their own credentials, which are stored encrypted, so the server needs ENCRYPTION_KEY .

Enable Banking is a company licensed in the EU as an account information service provider. You sign in at your own bank; neither Monize nor Enable Banking ever sees your bank password. For personal use, a free application in restricted production mode is enough. The page walks you through it under Show setup help , with every value to paste into Enable Banking's form shown beside a Copy button: Create an account at Enable Banking, sign in to its control panel and open API applications Choose Production (a Sandbox application only shows demo data from test banks) and keep Generate in the browser for the private key Paste the values Monize shows -- the application name, the Redirect URL , a description, your email, and privacy and terms URLs -- and click Register . Your browser saves the private key file ( .pem ); keep it secret. Click Activate by linking accounts , choose your country, bank and usage type, and authorize the accounts at your bank Back in Monize, click Set up credentials , enter the Application ID and load the private key ( Load key file , or paste the PEM), then Save Click Test connection . Monize reports that the application works, or that the redirect URL is not registered for it. The redirect URL does not have to be reachable from the internet -- only your browser opens it -- but the Monize server must be able to reach api.enablebanking.com over HTTPS. A Production application accepts only an https redirect URL, so PUBLIC_APP_URL must be an https address.

Click Connect a bank Choose the Country , search for your Bank , and pick the Account holder type (Personal or Business, the same as in the control panel). The dialog shows how long this bank allows access before it must be renewed, and for some banks a note on how that bank's data behaves. Click Continue to bank and authorize read-only access at your bank. You come back to Monize when it is done. Each bank account the bank reports is listed under Bank accounts . Monize links an account automatically when its account number matches one of yours; Match by account number tries again later. Otherwise pick the Monize account under Monize account , or Create a new account , which opens the account form already filled in. When you link an account, choose the date to Import transactions from . Transactions the bank booked before that date are never imported; a date earlier than the newest transaction in the account may duplicate entries you already made. If the bank calls an account a card but the Monize account is not a credit card (or the other way round), Monize warns you before linking.

The first import of a newly linked account is always confirmed from a Preview : every row the bank reports, with what Monize would do with it -- New , Already imported , Refused (with the reason, such as no date or another currency), Pending , or Before the start date -- and the payee and category after your rules. Expand a row to see which rules match it and the bank's operation type. Untick a row to skip it this time, or add it to the Exceptions so it is never imported. The preview also compares the bank's balance with the Monize balance after the import. Nothing is written until you click Import . After that, Sync now on an account, or Sync all for the connection, fetches new rows. Each connection can also: Sync automatically once a day Notify after the daily sync -- after every sync, only when transactions were imported, or never (see the Bank sync results category under Notifications ) Tag transactions with the bank's operation type , such as Card payment or Incoming transfer , so rules and reports can use it A row arrives once: a transaction you delete in Monize is not imported again by a later sync.

Open Banking access expires after the period the bank allows, which the connect dialog states. The connection shows Access valid until and Expires soon , and Monize notifies you 30, 14, 7, 3, 2, 1 and 0 days before it ends and once after (the Bank connections notification category). Renew consent sends you back to the bank; the accounts you linked are kept. Disconnect stops syncing that bank and asks it to end the access. Transactions already imported stay, and connecting the same bank again does not import them a second time. Remove credentials deletes your Enable Banking application ID and key from Monize.

Choose SimpleFIN in the Data provider picker, connect your banks in SimpleFIN Bridge ( Open SimpleFIN Bridge ), then paste the one-time Setup token and click Connect SimpleFIN . The card shows how many requests remain and when the next one is available. Refresh accounts reads the account list again, Stop syncing pauses one institution ( Resume syncing reconnects it), and Remove SimpleFIN from Monize stops all SimpleFIN syncing while keeping your history; revoke the app token in Bridge to end remote access as well. Bank sync is disabled in demo mode. An administrator can set BANK_SYNC_LOG_RAW=true to log the raw data the bank sends while diagnosing a problem; the log then contains bank data, so turn it off afterwards.
The login page includes a Remember me checkbox that extends your session duration from the default 1 day to a configurable period (default 30 days).

Setting Without Remember Me With Remember Me Access token 15 minutes 15 minutes Refresh token 1 day 30 days (configurable) When "Remember Me" is checked, the refresh token cookie is set with a longer expiry The access token still expires every 15 minutes and is silently refreshed using the refresh token Both tokens rotate on refresh (old tokens are revoked) Tokens are stored as httpOnly cookies and are never accessible to JavaScript

The duration can be configured via the REMEMBER_ME_DAYS environment variable: REMEMBER_ME_DAYS=14 # 14-day sessions instead of the default 30 If not set or set to an invalid value, the default is 30 days.

When two-factor authentication is enabled, the "Remember Me" preference is preserved through the 2FA verification step. After entering your TOTP code, the extended session duration is applied as expected.

Monize supports Time-based One-Time Password (TOTP) authentication for an additional layer of security. It lives in Settings > Security . SSO accounts: Two-factor authentication is not available for accounts that sign in through an identity provider -- authentication security is managed by that provider. See Single Sign-On . The exception is a deployment that lets SSO accounts keep a fallback password ( OIDC_ALLOW_PASSWORD_LOGIN ): there 2FA is offered, and recommended, to protect that password.

Navigate to Settings > Security Click Enable 2FA Re-enter your Current password and click Continue Scan the QR code with your authenticator app (Google Authenticator, Authy, 1Password, etc.). If you cannot scan it, Can't scan? Enter key manually shows the key to type in. Enter the 6-digit code from your app and click Verify and Enable Save your backup codes in a secure location (see Backup Codes below), tick I have saved these backup codes and click Done New accounts are also offered 2FA right after registering ( Secure Your Account ), with Skip for now unless the administrator requires it.

After enabling 2FA: Enter your email and password as normal You will be prompted for a 6-digit Verification Code Enter the code from your authenticator app, or click Use a backup code instead Optionally check Don't ask again on this browser to skip 2FA on this device for future logins (see Trusted Devices ) Click Verify

When you enable 2FA, Monize generates 12 single-use backup codes . These are your fallback if you lose access to your authenticator app. Each code is two groups of four hexadecimal characters (for example a1b2-c3d4 ) Codes are displayed only once at generation time -- Copy codes or Download them and keep them somewhere safe Each code can only be used once; after use, it is permanently removed During 2FA verification, click Use a backup code instead to enter one. After signing in with a backup code Monize reminds you to replace a lost authenticator with Reset 2FA . To regenerate backup codes, navigate to Settings > Security > Backup Codes and click Regenerate codes . You must enter a current 6-digit code to confirm, and regenerating invalidates every existing code. Security Note: Backup codes are hashed with bcrypt before being stored in the database. The plain-text codes are never stored on the server.

Reset 2FA replaces your authenticator. Use it if your authenticator app or backup codes may have been exposed, or if your authenticator codes stopped working (for example after a server secret changed). Enter your Account Password and a code from your authenticator -- or a backup code if the authenticator no longer works. Your current authenticator, backup codes and trusted devices stop working, you are signed out on every other device, and you set up a new authenticator straight away. If you have lost both your authenticator and your backup codes, an administrator can reset 2FA for you from User Management .
Navigate to Settings > Security Click Disable 2FA Enter your current 6-digit code, or one of your backup codes, to confirm

An administrator can make two-factor authentication mandatory for the whole deployment: FORCE_2FA=true With this set, a new account must set up 2FA before using Monize, the Security section shows Required by administrator , and 2FA cannot be disabled (it can still be reset). For OIDC logins the requirement is pushed up to the identity provider: a sign-in is rejected unless the provider actually asserts that multi-factor authentication happened (via the amr / acr claims), because app-level 2FA does not apply to an SSO account.

When logging in with 2FA, you can mark a device as "trusted" to skip the TOTP prompt on future logins from that device. A device is trusted by checking "Don't ask again on this browser" during a 2FA login. A device stays trusted for 14 days; the list shows when each one expires.

Navigate to Settings > Security Scroll to the Trusted Devices section View all currently trusted devices, with the address they signed in from and when each was added, last used and expires -- the one you are using is marked Current Click Revoke to remove trust for a single device, or Revoke All to clear every one Revoking all devices means you will be asked for your 2FA code on your next login from any device. Security Note: Trusted device tokens are stored as SHA-256 hashes in the database. The actual token is stored only in the browser cookie.

Navigate to Settings > Security Enter your Current Password Enter and confirm your new password ( New Password , Confirm New Password ) Click Change Password A password must be at least 12 characters and contain an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter, a number, and a special character. Password changes immediately revoke all existing refresh tokens, logging you out of all other sessions. When an administrator has given you a temporary password, Monize asks you to change it ( Change Your Password ) before you can continue.

Monize checks new passwords against the Have I Been Pwned database to prevent you from using passwords that have appeared in known data breaches. Checked during registration and password reset Uses the HIBP k-anonymity API -- only the first 5 characters of the password hash are sent, so your full password is never transmitted If the password has been found in a breach, you will see: "This password has been found in a data breach. Please choose a different password." If the HIBP service is unavailable, the password is allowed (availability over security)

On the login page, click Forgot your password? Enter your email address and click Send reset link Check your email for a reset link Click the link and set a new password Security Note: Password reset tokens are hashed with SHA-256 before being stored in the database. The token expires after a set time period.

Monize protects against brute-force login attacks with automatic account lockout. Setting Value Max failed attempts 5 consecutive failures Base lockout duration 30 minutes Escalation Doubles with each further lockout (30 min, 60 min, 120 min), up to 4 hours

After 5 consecutive failed login attempts , the account is locked The lockout duration doubles with each subsequent lockout cycle, up to a ceiling: 1st lockout (5 failures): 30 minutes 2nd lockout (10 failures): 60 minutes 3rd lockout (15 failures): 120 minutes 4th and later lockouts: 4 hours The escalation is forgotten 24 hours after a lockout has expired, so the next failure after that counts as a first one again If email is configured, a lockout notification is sent to the account owner A successful login resets the failure counter and clears any lockout Ten wrong two-factor codes in a row also lock the account for 30 minutes. Note: Login attempts for non-existent accounts return a generic "Invalid credentials" message and do not reveal whether the account exists.
Monize supports OpenID Connect (OIDC) for single sign-on integration with identity providers.
Authentik Authelia Pocket-ID Any OpenID Connect-compatible provider

OIDC is configured via environment variables: OIDC_ISSUER_URL=https://your-identity-provider.com # the provider's base URL, not its .well-known URL OIDC_CLIENT_ID=monize OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET=your-client-secret OIDC_CALLBACK_URL=https://monize.example.com/api/v1/auth/oidc/callback When OIDC is configured, a Sign in with SSO button appears on the login page (and Sign up with SSO on the registration page). Variable Default Effect LOCAL_AUTH_ENABLED true Set to false for SSO-only sign-in, with no email and password form REGISTRATION_ENABLED true Set to false to stop new accounts being registered OIDC_ALLOW_PASSWORD_LOGIN false Lets an SSO account that also has a local password sign in with it when the identity provider is down. Enable 2FA on those accounts, or the password is a single factor. OIDC_REQUIRE_VERIFIED_EMAIL true Trusts the provider's email only when it asserts email_verified ; an SSO sign-in then joins an existing password account only after an email confirmation (needs SMTP). Turn off only if you trust your provider to verify email ownership. An administrator can turn an SSO account back into a local one with Unlink SSO in User Management .
Personal Access Tokens provide API access for external integrations such as MCP clients. Tokens are managed in Settings > API Access .

Each token is created with one or more scopes that control what operations it can perform: Scope Description Read View accounts, transactions, categories, payees and financial reports Write Create transactions, payees and categories, and update or delete resources Scopes are enforced by the server on every request: a token without the Write scope cannot change anything. The same two scopes are used for OAuth/MCP clients, so a token cannot be granted a scope the server does not define.

Navigate to Settings > API Access Click Create Token Give it a Token Name (for example, Claude Desktop ), choose at least one scope, and pick an Expiration : 30 days , 90 days , 1 year , or No expiration Click Create Token . Because a token can reach your account without signing in, Monize first asks you to confirm it is you -- with your password, your authenticator code, or a fresh sign-in at your identity provider. Copy the token from the Token Created dialog -- it is not shown again The section also displays the MCP Server URL for this instance, with a Copy button, for configuring MCP clients such as Claude Code or Claude Desktop. Each token in the list shows when it was created, when it expires, and when it was last used.

Tokens are prefixed with pat_ for easy identification The full token is displayed only once at creation time Tokens are stored as SHA-256 hashes in the database Tokens can have an optional expiration date Revoke a token at any time from the settings page; it stops working immediately and any MCP connection using it is disconnected Tokens are rejected if the owning user account is locked or disabled For MCP integration details, see AI > MCP Server .

Monize ships short in-app walkthroughs of its features. Settings > Guided Tours lists every tour in one place, grouped by area (Getting started, Transactions, Investments, Reports, Settings): how many steps it has, which release added it, and whether you have taken it, left it early, or not seen it yet. Start runs a tour; Retake runs one you have already finished Press Escape to leave a tour at any point, and pick it up again from this page A tour that needs data you do not have yet says so instead of failing -- for example, "Add an account first -- this tour walks through recording a transaction." Reset tour progress (under Start over ) clears every recorded tour so they are offered again from the dashboard and after an update Tours are also offered from the dashboard, from the Getting Started flow, and from the What's New notes after an upgrade.

Settings > Help & Support collects the places to get help: Link What it is Create a support backup A de-identified, encrypted copy of your data for a maintainer (see below) GitHub The source code Open an Issue Report a bug or request a feature Discussions Ask questions and share ideas with the community Documentation These guides Most pages also carry a help icon beside their title that opens the matching part of this documentation.

A support backup lets you hand a maintainer a file that reproduces your bug without handing over your finances. It is a normal backup with the identifying content removed: Names are masked -- the first and last two characters are kept Notes, descriptions and account numbers are removed Every private amount is multiplied by a single hidden factor , while public values (exchange rates, security prices, interest rates) are left intact so the data still behaves correctly Dates, frequencies and structure are preserved , which is what makes bugs still reproduce The file is always encrypted with the password shown in the dialog, and restores like any other backup Options before generating: Option Description What to include Investments, scheduled transactions, budgets, reports and projections, import column mappings, auto-backup settings Include security price history Off by default -- a full price series matches public market data and can identify a masked ticker. Turn it on only when the bug concerns prices or valuations. Limit to specific accounts Leave everything unchecked to include every account. Picking a subset also pulls in the accounts and payees they reference. Date range Optional. Opening balances are adjusted so the trimmed file still reconciles. Amount multiplier Any non-integer greater than 1. Regenerate picks a new one. Encryption password Filled in for you; Regenerate picks a new one, or type your own of at least 8 characters. Monize asks you to confirm you saved it before generating -- it is stored nowhere and cannot be recovered. Preview shows a before/after sample of the masking so you can see exactly what a maintainer would receive. Do not share the multiplier. It is the key that reverses the hidden amounts. Send the encryption password through a separate channel from the file itself. This protects against casual exposure, not against someone who already knows you -- dates, frequencies and structure are preserved.

Settings > About reports what this instance is running: Item Description Version and API version The web app's and the backend's versions. Click the version to read its release notes. If the two differ, Monize warns you -- it usually means an upgrade only partly rolled out and the lagging service needs a restart or redeploy. Updates Whether a newer release exists, with a link to it. Controlled by UPDATE_CHECK_ENABLED on the server. What's new This version's release notes, read without leaving the app All releases Every release and its notes on GitHub Licence Monize is free software under the GNU AGPL v3 Security policy How to report a vulnerability privately Copy diagnostics Copies version, browser and locale details to paste into a bug report
If the Monize backend becomes unavailable (e.g., during a server restart or network issue), the frontend automatically detects the outage and displays a notification banner.

When any API call receives a 502 status or no response (network error), the frontend enters "backend down" mode A red banner appears at the top of the page: "Connection Lost -- Unable to reach the server. Retrying automatically..." The frontend polls the backend health endpoint ( /health/live ) every 5 seconds When the backend responds successfully, the page reloads automatically to restore normal operation This prevents false logouts during temporary backend outages -- instead of being redirected to the login page, you see a clear status message and automatic recovery.
Monize implements comprehensive security measures:

Feature Implementation Password Hashing bcrypt with salt rounds Password Breach Check HaveIBeenPwned k-anonymity API on registration and password reset Account Lockout 5 failed attempts triggers lockout with exponential backoff, capped at 4 hours Access Tokens JWT with 15-minute expiry Refresh Tokens Rotating tokens with family-based replay detection. 1 day by default, or REMEMBER_ME_DAYS (default 30) with Remember Me. TOTP Encryption Per-user unique salt (not shared secret) 2FA Backup Codes 12 single-use codes, bcrypt-hashed, generated on 2FA setup Trusted Devices 14-day device trust, SHA-256 hashed, revocable Personal Access Tokens Scoped (read/write), SHA-256 hashed, revocable Rate Limiting 100 req/min global, 3-5 per 15 min on auth endpoints Forced 2FA FORCE_2FA=true makes 2FA mandatory; OIDC logins must assert MFA at the provider Step-Up Re-Authentication High-sensitivity actions (creating an access token, emergency access) re-prompt for your strongest factor (password, TOTP, or a fresh OIDC sign-in) and issue a short-lived token scoped to that action alone Secrets at Rest ENCRYPTION_KEY encrypts AI provider keys, Google Places keys, bank sync credentials, mailbox credentials, emergency-access credentials, the push key pair, and the key automatic backups are encrypted with

Feature Implementation User Isolation All database queries filter by userId Input Validation DTO validation with whitelist mode (rejects unknown fields) SQL Injection Parameterized queries via TypeORM Row-Level Security Optional database-enforced per-user isolation beneath the app-level filtering ( RLS_MODE=off|shadow|enforce ) XSS Protection No dangerouslySetInnerHTML, HTML escaping in emails CSRF Token validation with httpOnly cookies

Header Value Content-Security-Policy Restrictive CSP with style-src and script-src whitelist Strict-Transport-Security max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains X-Content-Type-Options nosniff X-Frame-Options DENY Referrer-Policy strict-origin-when-cross-origin Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy same-origin Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy same-origin Permissions-Policy Restrictive policy If you are running Monize over plain HTTP without a reverse proxy such as Traefik, set the DISABLE_HTTPS_HEADERS environment variable to true : DISABLE_HTTPS_HEADERS=true This disables two headers that require HTTPS to function correctly: Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS) -- Forces browsers to use HTTPS; invalid over HTTP Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy (COOP) -- Can cause issues with HTTP-only deployments It also disables the Secure flag on authentication cookies so they work over plain HTTP. Do not use in production with HTTPS. Only set this when HTTPS is not available at the application level.

Everything Monize stores encrypted at rest -- AI provider API keys, Google Places API keys, bank sync and mailbox credentials, emergency-access credentials, the instance push key pair, and the key that automatic backups are encrypted with -- is protected by a single deployment secret: ENCRYPTION_KEY= # minimum 32 characters; generate with: openssl rand -hex 32 This is strongly recommended and will be required in a future release . Today the backend starts without it and warns on every boot; while it is unset, automatic backups are written unencrypted , AI and Google Places keys and bank sync credentials cannot be stored, emergency access cannot be enabled, and browser push cannot be configured. Keep this value safe, and keep it the same. Changing or losing it does not re-encrypt anything -- every secret already stored becomes unreadable, and automatic backups stop until each user signs in again. Back it up wherever you keep your other deployment secrets. ENCRYPTION_KEY was formerly called AI_ENCRYPTION_KEY . The old name is still read (and still wins if both are set), so an existing deployment upgrades without re-keying anything; set ENCRYPTION_KEY to the same value to move over.

Monize lets you grant another person scoped access to your accounts without sharing your password. Delegates have their own login and see only the accounts, sections, and shared data you have explicitly granted. While viewing your data, a delegate sees an always-visible "Viewing: [Your Name]" banner with a context switcher. Navigate to Settings > Shared Access to invite a delegate, configure per-account and section permissions, reset a delegate's password, or remove access. For complete documentation -- including the invitation flow, permission tabs, the delegate's view, and how Shared Access interacts with two-factor authentication -- see the dedicated Shared Access page.

Emergency Access is a "dead-man's switch" that automatically grants designated trusted contacts the ability to take over your account if you do not sign in for an extended period. It is intended for incapacitation or worst-case scenarios where a partner, family member, or executor needs access to your financial records on your behalf. Navigate to Settings > Emergency Access to enable the feature, add contacts, set the inactivity thresholds, and write an optional encrypted message that contacts will see when they claim access. For complete documentation -- including how grants work, the claim flow for contacts, the encrypted message and step-up authentication, and how to clear an accidental grant -- see the dedicated Emergency Access page.

Settings > Backup & Restore covers your own manual export and restore. Scheduled automatic backups are an administrator setting on Admin > Backups . For complete documentation, see the dedicated Backup and Restore page.
The Danger Zone section at the bottom of Settings provides options to delete your financial data or your entire user account. These actions are irreversible.

Delete Data removes your financial data while keeping your user account intact. This is particularly useful when migrating from Quicken or Microsoft Money -- if an import did not go as expected, you can wipe the data and start over without recreating your user account or reconfiguring your settings. Navigate to Settings , scroll to Danger Zone , and click Delete Data... . The section expands to show what will be deleted and asks you to confirm. The following data is always removed when you delete data: All transactions and transaction splits All scheduled/recurring transactions All securities, security prices, holdings, and investment transactions All budgets, budget periods, budget categories, and budget alerts Monthly account balance summaries (net worth snapshots) Custom reports Tags Import column mapping presets Action history (undo/redo) AI insights and usage logs You can optionally choose to also delete: Option What It Does Accounts Deletes all financial accounts. If unchecked, accounts are kept but their balances are reset to the opening balance. Categories Deletes all categories. References to categories on payees and accounts are cleared first. Payees Deletes all payees and payee aliases. Currency preferences Deletes saved exchange rate preferences. Migration Tip: If you are re-doing an import from Quicken or Microsoft Money, check all four optional boxes to get a completely clean slate. If you only want to re-import transactions but keep your account structure, leave "Accounts" unchecked -- account balances will be reset to their opening balance automatically. Password users: You must enter your password to confirm the deletion, then click Confirm Delete Data SSO (OIDC) users: You must re-authenticate with your identity provider ( Re-authenticate and Delete ) The operation runs inside a database transaction -- if an error occurs, no data is deleted.

Delete Account permanently deletes your entire user account and all associated data. After deletion, you are logged out and redirected to the login page. Navigate to Settings , scroll to Danger Zone , and click Delete Account . To confirm: Type DELETE in the confirmation field Enter your password (or re-authenticate via SSO) Click Confirm Delete Note: You cannot delete your account if you are the last admin user. Assign the admin role to another user first. If you are a delegate of another account: deleting removes your own data, but your login and the shared access others granted you are kept so the delegation keeps working -- you become a delegate-only user. To end that access, ask the owner to remove you from their Shared Access list first.

Users with the admin role have an Admin menu in the header with three pages: User Management , Notification Settings and Backups . The first account registered on an instance becomes its administrator.

Navigate to Admin > User Management to manage application users. Each user is listed with their Role , sign-in Provider (Local or SSO), Status , Last Login , and how much storage their Backups and Attachments take. Sort by any of the first five columns. Admin capabilities: Add a user (see below) Change a role : pick Admin or User in the user's Role list and confirm ( Promote to Admin / Demote to User ). You cannot change your own role. Disable or enable an account: click its Active / Disabled status. A disabled user cannot sign in, and every session, access token and connected app of theirs stops working. Reset Password : sets a temporary password, shown to you once, which the user must change at their next login. Offered for accounts that sign in with a password. Reset 2FA : switches off the user's two-factor authentication, deletes their backup codes and trusted devices, and signs them out everywhere, for someone who has lost their authenticator and backup codes. They can then sign in with their password and set up 2FA again. Unlink SSO : turns an SSO account into a local one with a temporary password, shown to you once. A later SSO sign-in with the same email address can link it again. Delete an account and all its data. If the user is also a delegate of someone else, their own data is removed but their login and delegate access remain. Your own row shows (you) and offers none of these actions.

Admins can create new user accounts directly from the User Management page. Click + New User to open the Add User form. Field Description Email The new user's email address (must be unique) Field Description First name The user's first name Last name The user's last name Role User (default) or Admin Under Credentials , choose one of three methods for setting the new user's initial credentials, then click Create User : Method Description Send an email invite to set a password Sends the user an invite link to set their own password. The link expires after 24 hours and can only be used once. Requires SMTP to be configured. Set a password now You provide a password at creation time. The password must be at least 12 characters and include an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter, a number, and a special character. Generate a temporary password A temporary password is generated and displayed to you once after creation. Share it with the user out-of-band (e.g., in person or via a secure message). The user will be required to change it on first login. Note: The email invite option is only available when SMTP is configured on the server. If SMTP is not configured, it will be greyed out and the default will be "Set a password now". If a user already exists as a delegate (someone who was granted shared access but never created a full account), creating an account with the same email address will upgrade them to a full user while preserving all existing delegations.

Navigate to Admin > Notification Settings to configure the delivery channels this Monize instance offers and the push identity behind them. Devices, test notifications and per-notification preferences belong to each account and are managed in Settings -- an administrator configures the instance and never sends to, or sees, another person's notifications. Each channel shows whether it is On , Off or Unavailable . Channel Notes In-app notifications The bell in the header. Always on and cannot be switched off: it is where a notification lives even when every other channel fails. Browser push Notifications delivered to a phone or desktop even when Monize is closed. Needs no Firebase, Google Play or Apple Developer account. Turn it on or off for the whole instance with Enable browser push for this instance . Email Bill reminders, budget digests and system alerts. Unavailable until the SMTP environment variables are set. ntfy and UnifiedPush The same encrypted push, delivered to a self-hosted UnifiedPush distributor instead of a browser vendor's service. It shares the instance's push key pair and switch, so it is unavailable while browser push is off. The page shows the instance's push Key fingerprint , when it was Generated , and how many Registered devices there are (active and retired). Rotate key pair replaces the instance's key pair. Every registered device stops being reachable and has to turn push on again, so rotate only if the key may have been exposed -- or to recover from a key pair the server can no longer decrypt. Message What to do "This instance has no push key pair. Set ENCRYPTION_KEY and restart." Monize generates the pair itself on the next start once the key is present "This instance cannot decrypt its stored push key pair." Usually ENCRYPTION_KEY changed under a live database, or a backup was restored onto a different instance. Rotate the key pair to recover; every device registers again. "This instance has no ENCRYPTION_KEY , so it cannot open the push key pair it stored." Rotating will not help. Set ENCRYPTION_KEY in the deployment and restart, and push works again with the existing devices.

Navigate to Admin > Backups to configure scheduled backups for the whole deployment: one schedule, storage location and three-tier retention policy that applies to every account, each into a folder of its own. The page also offers Validate for the folder, Back Up Every Account Now , and the status of the last run. What the scheduler writes is a compressed per-user backup of each account's own records, not a full PostgreSQL dump. Full documentation of every field is on the Backup and Restore page. Note: The admin section only appears in the navigation if your user account has the admin role.

Shared Access lets you grant another person scoped access to your Monize accounts -- ideal for spouses, family members, accountants, or bookkeepers who need to view (and optionally update) parts of your financial data without sharing your password. There are two ways an account can be shared, and they are chosen per account, per person: Way to share How it feels to the other person Best for Delegation (the original behaviour) They switch context and look at your ledger, then switch back Accountants, bookkeepers, someone helping you occasionally Joint account (added in v1.14.0) Your account simply appears in their own account list, register and net worth -- no context switching A couple sharing a chequing account Both are configured from the same Edit access dialog, and both are governed by the same per-account read / create / edit / delete grants. Joint is an extra toggle on top of a read grant, not a separate feature. Each delegate has their own login. Shared Access is not available in demo mode.

Term Meaning Owner The user who owns the accounts and grants access Delegate A separate user who has been granted access to one or more of the owner's accounts Grantee A delegate viewed from the perspective of a specific joint account -- the person the account is shared with Delegate-only user A user account that was created by an owner via Shared Access and has never registered or claimed their own data Full account A delegate who is a Monize user in their own right: they own accounts, share their own data with someone, or are an administrator. Only full accounts can be given joint access. Acting as The session state when a delegate is currently viewing an owner's data Joint account An account the owner has flagged as joint for a particular delegate, making it appear natively in that delegate's own data Delegates always have their own credentials. The owner's password is never shared, and the delegate sees only the data the owner has explicitly granted -- nothing else.

Open Settings (the gear icon with your name in the top-right corner) and choose Shared Access in the settings menu, or click the Shared Access card on the Settings page. The page lists everyone you have shared with. Each row shows the person's email and a summary of what they can reach: their Status , how many Sections and Accounts are granted, how many Shared data permissions they hold, and how many of the accounts are joint . Each row has three buttons: Edit access , Reset password and Remove .

Open Settings > Shared Access Click Add delegate Enter the delegate's Email Monize checks the address against existing Monize logins a moment after you stop typing ("Checking this email against existing Monize accounts..."). From there, one of three paths applies: Scenario What you do Result Email already has a Monize login Click Add delegate The existing user gains access using their current login.
